- **hoist-loads-out-of-k-loop** — Hoist the HBM->SBUF loads of all K tiles for a given output row/column block out of the innermost accumulation loop so they are issued once and reused.
  - why: Loading both tiles right before every nc_matmul serializes DMA and compute and re-loads the same tile N//TILE_N times, leaving TensorE idle between matmuls.
  - when: Profile shows gaps between matmul instructions on TensorE with DMA queues near 100% busy; dma_copy appears inside the k loop next to nc_matmul.
  - fix: lhsT_tiles=[dma_copy for k in range(K//128)] at the m loop; rhs_tiles at the n loop; inner loop only does nc_matmul(stationary=lhsT_tiles[k], moving=rhs_tiles[k]).
  - numbers: before_TensorE_active = 87.28%; before_DMA_active = 99.93%; after_TensorE_active = 99.85%; after_DMA_active = 99.73%
  - check (profile): AST: dma_copy inside the innermost loop that also contains nc_matmul and whose source slice does not depend on the innermost index -> hoist.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Analyzing the kernel  [stated, trn2]
- **coalesce-result-tiles-before-store** — Pack several result tiles into one contiguous (TILE_M, BLOCK_N) SBUF buffer (or allocate the N-block contiguously up front) before the SBUF->HBM dma_copy.
  - why: One large DMA per M-tile is more efficient than many 128x512 stores; allocating result tiles as (TILE_M, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N, TILE_N) avoids even the VectorE coalescing copy.
  - when: Many small dma_copy stores from separate result tiles in the eviction loop.
  - fix: result_packed = nl.ndarray((TILE_M, BLOCK_N), ...); tensor_copy each bn slice; single dma_copy(dst=result[rows, BLOCK_N*n:BLOCK_N*(n+1)], src=result_packed). Better: allocate (TILE_M, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N, TILE_N) and reshape to (TILE_M, BLOCK_N).
  - check (static): Count dma_copy stores whose free size < 2KiB per partition inside eviction loop.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension; nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3  [stated, all]
- **free-dim-flexible-indexing-cheap** — Put strided or gathered access on the free dimension of SBUF/PSUM tensors; keep partition access regular and keep HBM access sequential.
  - why: On-chip SRAM supports flexible free-dim striding at full speed but not along partitions; HBM is fastest when read sequentially.
  - when: Even/odd split, pooling windows, 4D access patterns.
  - fix: in_tile[:, 0:sz_f:2] for even columns; map parallel axis to P and contraction axes to F for pooling.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/indexing-overview.rst :: Basic Tensor Indexing; nki/guides/tutorials/average_pool2d.rst  [stated, all]
- **avoid-load-transpose2d** — Define the HBM tensor layout to match the compute layout instead of using nl.load_transpose2d, which is significantly less bandwidth-efficient than a plain load.
  - why: Transposed DMA loads use the DMA engines poorly compared to contiguous loads.
  - when: Kernel wants seq_len on partition but HBM tensor is [channels, seq_len].
  - fix: Store the input as [seq_len, channels] in HBM, or keep channels on P.
  - check (static): flag nl.load_transpose2d / dma_transpose usage inside hot loops.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Step 1 Option 2  [stated, all]
- **dma-4kib-per-partition-saturates** — Shape DMA transfers to cover as many partitions as possible with >= 4 KiB per partition (2 KiB minimum recommended) to approach peak bandwidth.
  - why: 16 DMA engines each serve 8 partitions; throughput per transfer rises with bytes per partition and saturates near 4096 free bytes.
  - when: Small per-partition transfers (e.g. [128,128] bf16 = 256 B/partition).
  - fix: Batch multiple tiles into one dma_copy: fp32 >= 512 elems, bf16 >= 1024, fp8 >= 2048 per partition for 2 KiB.
  - numbers: saturation = 4096 B/partition; min_recommended = 2048 B/partition; fp32_min_free = 512; bf16_min_free = 1024; fp8_min_free = 2048
  - check (static): dma_copy free bytes per partition < 2048 -> warn.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Performance Considerations  [stated, all]
- **dma-engine-count-scales-with-partitions** — Spread DMA destinations across all 128 partitions; a transfer touching only 4 partitions uses a single DMA engine while 128 partitions engage all 16.
  - why: Each DMA engine owns 8 partition lanes.
  - when: Loading a [4,4096] tensor into 4 partitions.
  - fix: Reshape so rows map to 128 partitions (e.g. [128,128]) when possible.
  - numbers: A_4x4096_engines = 1; A_128x128_engines = 16; per_engine_chunk = 2 KiB
  - check (static): dma_copy with dst partition count <= 8 -> warn single-engine.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Examples  [stated, trn2]
- **dma-fixed-overhead-batch-transfers** — Batch data movement into fewer, larger DMA transfers; small frequent transfers are latency-bound by trigger and semaphore overhead.
  - why: Each transfer costs a trigger from a sequencer and a completion semaphore update from all 16 engines (even idle ones write 4 B).
  - when: Many tiny dma_copy calls in a loop.
  - fix: Coalesce tiles before store; load blocks instead of tiles.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Performance Considerations; Example 1  [stated, all]
- **dma-peak-bandwidth-per-generation** — Budget HBM traffic against aggregate DMA bandwidth of 272 GB/s (trn1), 368 GB/s (trn2) or 528 GB/s (trn3) per NeuronCore.
  - why: 16 engines at 17/23/33 B/ns respectively.
  - when: Estimating memory-bound kernel time.
  - fix: time >= bytes / aggregate_bw.
  - numbers: trn1 = 272 GB/s; trn2 = 368 GB/s; trn3 = 528 GB/s; engines = 16
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Performance Considerations  [stated, all]
- **dma-queue-ordering** — Expect DMAs in the same queue on the same engine to execute in order while different queues interleave (round robin on v2/v3, QoS on v4); choose the trigger engine via dma_copy(engine=...) only with hardware DGE.
  - why: Queue id is tied to the trigger engine and descriptor generation method.
  - when: A latency-critical load is stuck behind bulk transfers in the same queue.
  - fix: Issue critical loads from a different engine/queue; check queue id by hovering the DMA in Neuron Explorer.
  - numbers: queues_per_engine = 16
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: DMA Queues; DMA Triggers  [stated, all]
- **mlp-down-proj-optimized-weight-layout** — For decode down-projection without column tiling, reinterpret W_down [I,H] as [I, lnc, 128, H/(128*lnc)] transposed to [I, lnc, H/(128*lnc), 128] so weight loads are unit-stride and the matmul initiation interval drops.
  - why: Unit-stride weight DMA feeds TensorE faster than strided gathers.
  - when: use_tkg_down_proj_column_tiling=False.
  - fix: mlp(..., use_tkg_down_proj_column_tiling=False, use_tkg_down_proj_optimized_layout=True)
  - source: nki/library/api/mlp.rst :: use_tkg_down_proj_optimized_layout  [stated, all]
- **attention-tkg-strided-mm1** — Keep strided_mm1=True so the first matmul reads K with a strided pattern and the second matmul can stream V sequentially for better DMA throughput.
  - why: Trades MM1 access regularity for sequential V reads in MM2.
  - when: Decode attention over large KV cache.
  - fix: AttnTKGConfig(strided_mm1=True)
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-tkg.rst :: Strided Memory Access  [stated, all]
- **in-kernel-mask-generation** — Generate the attention mask in-kernel from position ids (use_pos_id=True) to avoid loading a [s_prior, B, H, s_active] mask from HBM.
  - why: Reduces memory bandwidth at the cost of requiring position IDs.
  - when: Decode attention where mask DMA is noticeable.
  - fix: AttnTKGConfig(use_pos_id=True), pass rope_pos_ids/start_pos_ids.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-tkg.rst :: Mask Generation  [stated, all]
- **kv-cache-update-dma-pattern** — Update the KV cache with one batched vector-offset DMA for S_tkg=1 and per-batch scalar-offset DMAs for S_tkg>1; block caches use indirect addressing via block slot indices.
  - why: Vector offsets let a single DMA scatter all batches' tokens; scalar offsets are needed when each batch writes a range.
  - when: Writing new K/V tokens into the cache.
  - fix: For S_tkg==1: dma with vector_offset=kv_cache_update_idx; else loop over batch with scalar_offset.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-block-tkg.rst :: Cache Update Optimization  [stated, all]
- **block-weight-loading-for-prefetch** — Load projection weights in blocks (several tiles per DMA) to encourage prefetching ahead of the matmuls.
  - why: Decode projections are weight-bandwidth bound; block loads keep DMA queues full.
  - when: Weight streaming in TKG kernels.
  - fix: Follow output_projection_tkg's block-based weight loading.
  - source: nki/library/api/output-projection-tkg.rst :: Implementation Details 9  [stated, all]
- **segmented-cte-block-table-padding-skips-dma** — Pad block tables with -1 to make the kernel skip DMA for missing blocks, and prepend -1 padding when the last prior segment is shorter than prior_seg_size.
  - why: block_tables entries of -1 trigger DMA skipping in attention_segmented_cte.
  - when: Paged KV prefill with partial segments.
  - fix: block_tables[b, :pad] = -1; prior_tokens multiple of block_size.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-segmented-cte.rst :: block_tables  [stated, all]
- **packed-fp8-k-cache-view-as-bf16** — Store an FP8 K cache packed as (..., block_size//2, d_head, 2) so two consecutive tokens form one bf16-width element and the cache can be DMA'd as bf16; keep V unpacked token-major.
  - why: DMA and views work in 16-bit widths; packing avoids a dtype cast on the K path while V is loaded as fp8 and dequantized.
  - when: FP8 KV cache in a fused SWA block.
  - fix: k_cache shape (num_blocks, kv_heads, block_size//2, d_head, 2) fp8 viewed as bf16.
  - source: nki/library/api/swa-fused-cte.rst  [stated, all]
- **trivial-dim-dma-splitting** — Expect the compiler to split a [1,H] load into many tiny (e.g. 4-byte) DMAs because of trivial-dimension optimizations; reshape small vectors onto more partitions when this shows in the profile.
  - why: Trivial dims defeat descriptor coalescing.
  - when: Gamma/bias load appears as many 4 B DMAs.
  - fix: Load gamma as [128, H/128] or broadcast via TensorE once.
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Phase 1: Load Inputs  [stated, all]
- **pack-scales-into-output-row** — Pack per-row dequant scales into the tail of the quantized output row ([..., H+4] fp8 reinterpreted as fp32) so one tensor carries data and scales.
  - why: Neuron cannot pack two dtypes in one tensor natively; appending 4 fp8 bytes per row lets collectives/gathers move both at once.
  - when: Sequence-parallel RMSNorm-quant followed by all-gather.
  - fix: out[..., :H] = fp8 data; out[..., H:H+4] = fp32 scale bits.
  - numbers: scale_tail = 4 fp8 elements = 1 fp32
  - source: nki/library/api/rmsnorm-quant.rst :: return; nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Neuron Support  [stated, all]
- **dynamic-expert-weight-load-scalar-offset** — Load per-expert weight slices with a scalar_offset taken from a (1,1) SBUF expert-index tile instead of unrolling over experts.
  - why: Dynamic indexing on the DMA lets one code path serve any expert; partial tiles are zero-padded.
  - when: block_to_expert-driven weight loads.
  - fix: load_gate_up_proj_weights(gate_up_proj_weight[E,H,2,I_TP], block_expert_sb[1,1], ...)
  - source: nki/library/api/bwmm-shard-on-block-v2.rst :: load_down_proj_weight notes  [stated, all]
- **gather-via-indirect-dma** — Implement row gathers (input[index]) with an indirect DMA load whose offsets come from the index tensor; under LNC sharding make the index count divisible by the shard count.
  - why: DMA engines support scatter/gather natively, avoiding per-row loops.
  - when: Embedding lookup, token permutation.
  - fix: gather(input[N,D], dim=0, index[K])  # K % num_shards == 0
  - source: nki/library/api/gather.rst  [stated, all]
- **oob-skip-sentinel-for-indirect-dma** — Use the out-of-bounds sentinel (index == T) with oob_mode.skip so unused slots in a fixed-size indirect DMA index become no-ops.
  - why: Fixed-shape index tensors need a way to express variable counts without branching.
  - when: all-to-all-v dispatch/combine with per-destination counts.
  - fix: send_indices[t, d] = T for slots beyond send_counts[d].
  - source: nki/library/api/permute-a2av.rst :: send_indices  [stated, all]

## SBUF and PSUM budgeting (59)

- **psum-bank7-reserved-for-pe-transpose** — Budget for 7 usable PSUM banks (not 8) when the compiler lowers dma_transpose to a PE transpose on trn2+.
  - why: nl.tile_size.psum_num_banks returns 7 when NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE lowering is active because bank 7 is reserved for nc_transpose.
  - when: Manual PSUM address planning that assumes 8 banks fails or collides.
  - fix: Read nl.tile_size.psum_num_banks inside the kernel instead of hard-coding 8.
  - numbers: psum_num_banks = 8 (7 when PE-transpose lowering)
  - check (static): manual PSUM address >= 7*2048 while dma_transpose lowering is enabled
  - source: nki/language/_tile_size.py psum_num_banks property  [stated, trn2]
- **tt-inputs-not-both-psum** — Never give tensor_tensor, tensor_tensor_scan or scalar_tensor_tensor two PSUM inputs; at most one of the two tensor operands may live in PSUM.
  - why: Vector Engine has a single PSUM read port per instruction.
  - when: Adding two matmul accumulators directly from PSUM.
  - fix: Evacuate one operand to SBUF with tensor_copy first, or accumulate both matmuls into one PSUM tile.
  - check (static): tensor_tensor/scan/stt: not (buffer(a)==psum and buffer(b)==psum)
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_tensor, tensor_tensor_scan, scalar_tensor_tensor docstrings  [stated, all]
- **gpsimd-cannot-access-psum** — Keep every GpSimd Engine instruction (iota, affine_select, nc_n_gather, local_gather, tensor_partition_reduce, nonzero_with_count, topk, sequence_bounds, rng/rand_get_state with engine=gpsimd, tensor_copy/memset/tensor_tensor on gpsimd) on SBUF operands only.
  - why: GpSimd has no PSUM port; the compiler falls back to Vector where it can (int32 tensor_tensor) or errors.
  - when: iota or affine_select writing a PSUM tile; tensor_copy(engine=gpsimd) from PSUM.
  - fix: Target SBUF tiles; evacuate PSUM with Vector/Scalar tensor_copy first.
  - check (static): op.engine==gpsimd implies all operand buffers == sbuf
  - source: nki.isa.nc_n_gather, tensor_copy, rng, rand_get_state docstrings  [stated, all]
- **sbuf-per-partition-capacity** — Keep the sum of live SBUF tiles per partition under nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes (trn1 180224 B, trn2 212984 B, trn3 245752 B) and never exceed it with a single tile's free dim.
  - why: SBUF is 192/224/256 KiB per partition across 128 partitions (24/28/32 MiB total) minus 16 KiB reserved (plus 8 B on gen3/gen4); every instruction's elements-per-partition must fit the physical partition.
  - when: Large fp32 tiles (e.g. (128, 65536) fp32 = 256 KiB/partition) or too many double buffers failing allocation.
  - fix: Tile the free dim; use bf16 staging; read nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes inside the kernel for portable sizing.
  - numbers: sbuf_fmax_bytes_trn1 = 180224 B; sbuf_fmax_bytes_trn2 = 212984 B; sbuf_fmax_bytes_trn3 = 245752 B; sbuf_size_bytes_trn1 = 25165824 B; sbuf_size_bytes_trn2 = 29360128 B; sbuf_size_bytes_trn3 = 33554432 B; sbuf_fmax_fp32_trn2 = 53246 elements
  - check (static): nl.ndarray(sbuf): prod(shape[1:])*itemsize <= nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax_bytes(target)
  - source: nki/language/_tile_size.py (_SBUF_FMAX_BYTES, _SBUF_SIZE_BYTES); nki.language.tile_size rst  [stated, all]
- **psum-geometry-16kb-8-banks** — Plan PSUM usage as 8 banks x 2 KiB per partition (16 KiB total, 512 fp32 per bank); a manually addressed PSUM tensor must start at a bank boundary.
  - why: PSUM is the matmul accumulator memory; bank boundaries matter for accumulation groups and manual allocation errors otherwise.
  - when: address=(0, 1024) for a PSUM tile; more than 8 concurrent (128,512) fp32 accumulators.
  - fix: address=(0, bank_id*2048); limit live PSUM accumulators to psum_num_banks; evacuate promptly.
  - numbers: psum_partition_bytes = 16384 B; psum_bank_bytes = 2048 B; psum_banks = 8; psum_bank_fmax = 512 fp32
  - check (static): nl.ndarray(psum, address=(p,f)): f % 2048 == 0; live psum bytes per partition <= 16384
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Improved allocation API'; nki/language/_tile_size.py  [stated, all]
- **min-alignment-4-bytes** — Align manually chosen SBUF/PSUM free-dim byte offsets to at least 4 bytes (nl.tile_size.sbuf_min_align / psum_min_align).
  - why: Hardware address granularity for free-dim addressing is 4 bytes.
  - when: address=(0, 1) on a bf16 tile (2-byte offset).
  - fix: Round free offsets up to a multiple of 4 bytes (prefer larger, e.g. 64 B, for DMA efficiency).
  - numbers: sbuf_min_align = 4 B; psum_min_align = 4 B
  - check (static): nl.ndarray(address=(p,f)): f*itemsize % 4 == 0
  - source: nki/language/_tile_size.py  [stated, all]
- **manual-address-allocation** — When hand-allocating, pass address=(partition_offset, free_offset) to nl.ndarray where free_offset is in elements of the tensor dtype and translated to bytes by the compiler.
  - why: The 0.2.0+ allocation API replaced the old sb_mod/block allocators; the compiler no longer rotates addresses you fix.
  - when: Modular/mod allocators from NKI 0.1.0; overlapping manual regions.
  - fix: Compute per-buffer offsets explicitly (e.g. base + (i % nbuf) * tile_bytes) in a Python list of tensors.
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Improved allocation API'; nki.language.ndarray docstring  [stated, all]
- **nl-copy-returns-sbuf** — Expect nl.copy and tensor_copy without a pre-declared PSUM dst to produce SBUF tiles; declare a PSUM dst explicitly when needed.
  - why: Default allocation target for copies is SBUF.
  - when: Assuming nl.copy(psum_tile) stays in PSUM.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=psum_decl, src=...).
  - source: nki.language.copy and nki.isa.tensor_copy docstrings  [stated, all]
- **mem-capacity-table** — Plan SBUF residency against 28 MiB on Trainium2 (128 partitions x 224 KiB), 24 MiB on trn1 (192 KiB/partition), 32 MiB on trn3; PSUM is 2 MiB (16 KiB/partition, 8 banks of 2 KiB) on all generations.
  - why: SBUF/PSUM are software-managed 2-D SRAMs; exceeding capacity triggers compiler spills to HBM.
  - when: Choosing block sizes / number of resident weight tiles.
  - fix: Keep live tiles well below 224 KiB per partition on trn2 (e.g. a [128, 4096] bf16 tile is 8 KiB/partition).
  - numbers: trn2_sbuf = 28 MiB; trn2_sbuf_per_partition = 224 KiB; trn1_sbuf = 24 MiB; trn1_sbuf_per_partition = 192 KiB; trn3_sbuf = 32 MiB; psum = 2 MiB; psum_per_partition = 16 KiB; psum_banks = 8; sbuf_vs_hbm_bw = ~20x
  - check (static): sum bytes per partition of simultaneously live SBUF tiles; flag > 90% of 224 KiB.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: NeuronCore-v3 Compute Engine Updates; nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: NeuronCore-v2 Compute Engines; nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: NeuronCore-v4 Compute Engine Updates; nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst  [stated, all]
- **mem-start-partition-alignment** — Allocate tiles so their start partition obeys the hardware rule: >64 partitions start at 0; 33-64 start at 0 or 64; <=32 start at 0/32/64/96.
  - why: The engine read/write interfaces are organized in 32-partition quadrants and 64-partition halves; the compiler allocator enforces this, so odd sizes waste partitions.
  - when: Tiles of 48, 96 or 100 partitions, or partition-vectorization placing a second tile at partition 40.
  - fix: Use partition counts of 32/64/128 and place sub-tiles at 0/32/64/96.
  - check (static): for explicit partition slices: assert start in allowed set for size.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Accessing SBUF/PSUM tensors using compute engines  [stated, all]
- **mem-no-partition-stride** — Never stride along the partition dimension in one instruction access; the leading access-pattern step must equal the tensor's full free-dim element count.
  - why: Hardware reads a contiguous block of partitions with the same free-dim offset per time step.
  - when: t.ap(pattern=[[2*F, P/2], ...]) or t[::2, :] on SBUF/PSUM tensors.
  - fix: Use nc_stream_shuffle / transposes to rearrange partitions, or restructure the layout.
  - check (static): for SBUF/PSUM .ap(): assert pattern[0][0] == prod(free_shape).
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Restriction on SBUF/PSUM Tensors  [stated, all]
- **mem-inner-stride-16b-halves-bandwidth** — Keep the most-minor free-dim stride at or below 16 bytes (4 fp32, 8 bf16, 16 fp8 elements) on SBUF/PSUM accesses; larger strides halve the engine's read/write bandwidth (~50% slower instruction).
  - why: Each tensor read/write interface delivers 128 elements/cycle only when the inner stride is < 16 B.
  - when: Strided inner access such as x[:, ::8] in bf16 (16 B stride) or even/odd column splits in fp32 with stride > 4.
  - fix: Reorder dims so the strided axis is not the innermost, or copy once into a contiguous layout.
  - numbers: max_free_inner_stride = 16 B; peak_access_rate = 128 elements/cycle
  - check (static): for compute ops: inner_step*dtype_bytes > 16 -> warn 2x slowdown.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Performance Consideration (Access pattern)  [stated, all]
- **mem-tensor-access-overhead** — Amortize the ~60-cycle fixed cost of each tensor access request with large P and F sizes.
  - why: Initiating a read/write stream between an engine and SBUF/PSUM costs about 60 cycles on NeuronCore-v2; ILP hides some but small tiles expose it.
  - when: Many instructions on tiles with few elements per partition.
  - fix: Batch work into fewer instructions with >= 128 elements per partition.
  - numbers: access_request_overhead = ~60 cycles
  - check (simulator): per instruction cost += 60 cycles.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor access overhead  [stated, trn1]
- **mem-free-dim-access-limits** — Keep instruction free sizes within 64K elements for SBUF operands and 4K elements for PSUM operands (bn_stats: <= 512), and remember each free axis is a uint16 size with int16 stride.
  - why: ISA encodes up to four free dims per partition with 16-bit size/stride fields; most instructions only support 1-3 dims.
  - when: Very long single-instruction tiles.
  - fix: Split into multiple instructions or add an outer loop.
  - numbers: sbuf_free_max = 64K elements; psum_free_max = 4K elements; bn_stats_free_max = 512
  - check (static): assert each free size <= 65535, PSUM free <= 4096, bn_stats free <= 512.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Layout & Tile Size; Accessing SBUF/PSUM tensors  [stated, all]
- **mem-evict-psum-promptly** — Reserve PSUM for TensorE outputs and evict results to SBUF with VectorE/ScalarE as soon as each accumulation group completes.
  - why: PSUM is only 2 MiB; holding results there blocks TensorE from reusing banks and VectorE/ScalarE can only treat it as plain SRAM.
  - when: Vector/scalar intermediates allocated in PSUM, or late eviction.
  - fix: tensor_copy/activation from PSUM -> SBUF immediately after the K loop; do not allocate non-matmul tensors in nl.psum.
  - check (static): flag nl.ndarray(buffer=nl.psum) not written by nc_matmul.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst :: NeuronCore internal memory  [stated, all]
- **mem-cross-partition-limits** — Expect no cross-partition data movement for instructions spanning > 64 partitions; 33-64 partitions allow cross-half moves and <= 32 allow cross-quadrant moves (one-to-one mapping only).
  - why: src and dst must occupy the same partition count, and start-partition rules force both to start at 0 when > 64; smaller tiles may map half-to-half or quadrant-to-quadrant.
  - when: Trying to shift data across partitions with a tensor_copy on a 128-partition tile.
  - fix: Use 32- or 64-partition sub-tiles for quadrant/half moves, VectorE 32x32 transpose/shuffle, TensorE matmul-based reshapes, or DMA SBUF->SBUF.
  - check (static): flag copy ops whose src and dst partition offsets differ while P > 64.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Cross-Partition Connectivity  [stated, all]
- **mem-declare-buffers-inside-inner-loop** — Declare per-iteration SBUF buffers inside the innermost loop rather than as one large outer array indexed by loop variables.
  - why: A big outer allocation (e.g. (2,4,par_dim(128),512)) stays live across the whole nest and can cause unexpected spilling; per-iteration declarations let the compiler recycle space.
  - when: Spill traffic appears although the working set seemed small.
  - fix: for i0: for i1: buf = nl.ndarray((nl.par_dim(128), 512), buffer=nl.sbuf); buf[...] = nl.load(...)

- **down-proj-pack-multiple-h1-per-psum-bank** — In LHS/RHS-swap down_proj, pack perBankT = 512//T consecutive H1 output tiles ([128, T] each) into one PSUM bank along the free axis; if ceil(H1_shard/perBankT) > 8 banks, fall back to CTE mode.
