  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Step 6  [stated, all]
- **fuse-adjacent-loops-to-shrink-intermediates** — Fuse sibling loops over the same index so intermediate accumulators can be declared per iteration and shrink by the trip count.
  - why: Pulling scanC_accum inside the fused channel loop cuts its size by n_channel_tile.
  - when: Two consecutive loops over the same range with an intermediate tensor between them.
  - fix: for i_channel_tile: acc=nl.zeros((128, seq_len)); ...; nl.store(..., acc)
  - numbers: gain = ~1% latency
  - check (static): Two adjacent loops with identical ranges where loop 2 only consumes loop 1 output -> fuse.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Minimizing data reloading by loop reordering  [stated, all]
- **estimate-per-partition-sbuf-footprint** — Estimate per-partition SBUF footprint as sum(free_elems * dtype_bytes) over live tiles and keep it well under the partition capacity.
  - why: Three FP32 tiles of 8192 free elements consume 96 KiB per partition, half the available SBUF, which caused spilling.
  - when: Large free-dim tiles in FP32.
  - fix: Tile the free dim or use bf16 intermediates.
  - numbers: example = 8192*4B*3 = 96 KiB/partition = half of SBUF
  - check (static): sum over live tiles of shape[1:]*itemsize per partition.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Mitigate spilling by tiling seq_len  [stated, trn1]
- **psum-reserve-for-matmul-evict-fast** — Reserve PSUM for TensorE matmul outputs and evict results to SBUF with Vector/Scalar engines as soon as possible.
  - why: PSUM is small; it is the accumulation target for TensorE and can be read by VectorE/ScalarE.
  - when: Allocating non-matmul intermediates in PSUM.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=sbuf_tile, src=psum_tile) right after the accumulation loop.
  - check (static): nl.ndarray(buffer=nl.psum) not written by nc_matmul -> warn.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst :: NeuronCore internal memory  [stated, all]
- **compiler-inserts-spills-on-overflow** — Keep total live on-chip data under SBUF/PSUM capacity through tiling and loop fusion; otherwise the compiler silently inserts spills/refills to HBM.
  - why: Memories are software-managed; overflow is handled by inserting DMA traffic that shows up as SpillReload queues.
  - when: Profile shows qSyncSpillReload / qVectorSpillReload.
  - fix: Reduce tile sizes, fuse loops, reuse buffers.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst :: note  [stated, all]
- **write-k-cache-transposed-for-decode** — Write the K cache in transposed (head_dim, seq/block) layout at prefill time so decode attention can load K with d_head on partitions without an nc_transpose.
  - why: QK^T contracts over d_head, so d on partition is the native matmul layout; attention_tkg exposes tp_k_prior and attention_segmented_cte k_pre_transposed for this.
  - when: Designing the KV-cache layout for a decode path.
  - fix: qkv(..., transpose_k_cache=True); attention_tkg(cfg.tp_k_prior=True) with k_prior [B,1,d,s_prior].
  - source: nki/library/api/qkv.rst :: transpose_k_cache; nki/library/api/attention-tkg.rst :: K_prior Transpose Handling; nki/library/api/attention-segmented-cte.rst  [stated, all]
- **attention-block-tkg-keeps-everything-in-sbuf** — Fuse pre-norm, QKV, RoPE, QK-norm, attention, KV-cache update and output projection in one kernel so only X, weights, caches and the final output touch HBM.
  - why: Decode is HBM-bandwidth bound; eliminating intermediate round-trips is the main lever.
  - when: Building a decode layer.
  - fix: Use attention_block_tkg or compose attention_tkg(out_in_sb) -> output_projection_tkg(OUT_IN_SB) with a shared SbufManager.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-block-tkg.rst :: Memory Efficiency  [stated, all]
- **stack-allocator-for-determinism** — Use the stack allocator (SbufManager) for kernels so SBUF/PSUM placement is deterministic within the kernel; the default allocator considers scope outside the kernel and can vary performance.
  - why: Deterministic addresses avoid run-to-run layout changes and fragmentation.
  - when: Any hand-tuned library-style kernel.
  - fix: sbm = SbufManager(0, nl.tile_size.total_available_sbuf_size); sbm.open_scope(); t = sbm.alloc_stack(shape, dtype); sbm.close_scope()
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: SBUF/PSUM Allocation; nki/library/kernel-utils/allocator.rst  [stated, all]
- **multi-buffer-psum-banks** — Replicate the PSUM allocation of a pipelined loop across all hardware PSUM banks with directives=ncc.multi_buffer(num_hw_psum_banks) so consecutive iterations write different banks.
  - why: Separate banks let TensorE write iteration i+1 while VectorE reads iteration i.
  - when: Loop issuing a matmul per iteration whose result is consumed by another engine.
  - fix: for i in nl.affine_range(n, directives=ncc.multi_buffer(constants.num_hw_psum_banks)): ...
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Kernel Code Details  [stated, all]
- **keep-psum-resident-until-consumer-ready** — Leave matmul results in PSUM and consume them directly (e.g. scalar_tensor_tensor reading PSUM) when the consumer is pipelined with TensorE; early eviction to SBUF buys little.
  - why: VectorE/ScalarE can read PSUM; an extra copy only adds work when the pipeline is already balanced.
  - when: Gamma-broadcast result waiting on inverse-RMS scale.
  - fix: Split work into part 1 (fill banks) and part 2 (pipelined consume) instead of evicting.
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Phase 2: RMSNorm  [stated, all]
- **sbufmanager-stack-heap-discipline** — Allocate long-lived buffers (weights) with alloc_heap at the top of SBUF and release them with pop_heap in LIFO order; allocate temporaries with alloc_stack inside open_scope/close_scope so they free automatically.
  - why: The stack grows up from the lower bound and the heap down from the upper bound; close_scope resets the stack pointer so sibling scopes reuse memory.
  - when: Multi-phase kernels with different temporaries per phase.
  - fix: w=sbm.alloc_heap((128,256), nl.bfloat16); sbm.open_scope('phase'); t=sbm.alloc_stack(...); sbm.close_scope(); sbm.pop_heap()
  - check (static): Every open_scope has matching close_scope; alloc_heap count == pop_heap count.
  - source: nki/library/kernel-utils/allocator.rst :: Examples  [stated, all]
- **residual-in-sbuf-megakernel** — In a multi-layer decode megakernel keep the residual stream in SBUF and use SBUF-to-SBUF all-reduce (sbuf_residual_and_cc=True) instead of round-tripping through HBM each layer.
  - why: transformer_tkg runs attention -> all-reduce -> MLP -> all-reduce per layer; SBUF residual removes HBM traffic and launch overhead.
  - when: Token-generation transformer with TP all-reduces.
  - fix: transformer_tkg(..., sbuf_residual_and_cc=True, replica_groups=...)
  - source: nki/library/api/transformer-tkg.rst  [stated, all]
- **mx-pack-scales-fold** — Keep pack_scales=True so four H512 tiles of MX scales fold into one 128-wide block (scale region ~H/16 columns) instead of H/4 with 7/8 padding.
  - why: quantize_mx emits one uint8 scale per (32-partition quadrant x 4 lanes), occupying 4 of every 32 columns after transpose.
  - when: Packed MX output rows.
  - fix: rmsnorm_mx_prefill(..., pack_scales=True)
  - numbers: folded_scale_cols = ceil(num_H512/4)*128 (~H/16); unfolded = num_H512*128 (H/4)
  - source: nki/library/api/rmsnorm-mx-prefill.rst :: pack_scales  [stated, trn3]
- **selective-scan-accumulate-in-sbuf** — Accumulate across the state dimension in SBUF per free tile rather than read-modify-write to HBM (which needs trn2 shared memory); store carries in the final_state HBM tensor.
  - why: HBM RMW is slow and generation-dependent; SBUF accumulation is local.
  - when: Mamba selective scan over state_size.
  - fix: selective_scan with F tile 512; channels on partitions (128).
  - numbers: F_tile = 512
  - source: nki/library/api/selective-scan.rst :: Notes  [stated, all]

## Tiling and layout (43)

- **mm-explicit-tiling-required** — Explicitly tile any matmul larger than [K<=128] x [M<=128] x [N<=512] into nested loops of nc_matmul calls.
  - why: nc_matmul maps 1:1 to a hardware instruction and does not auto-tile; shapes beyond the limits are compile errors.
  - when: Calling nc_matmul directly with full-problem tensors.
  - fix: Loop m in range(0,M,128), n in range(0,N,512), k in range(0,K,128) with PSUM accumulation over k.
  - check (static): nc_matmul operand dims within tile_size limits
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size (final paragraph)  [stated, all]
- **transpose-tensor-engine-limits** — Use Tensor Engine nc_transpose only for tiles <= [128,128], reading SBUF and writing PSUM with the same dtype.
  - why: PE transpose is an identity matmul so it inherits the 128x128 stationary limit and the SBUF-in/PSUM-out rule.
  - when: nc_transpose(engine=tensor) with free dim > 128 or dst in SBUF.
  - fix: Split into 128x128 blocks; allocate a PSUM dst and evacuate with tensor_copy; multiple free dims are implicitly flattened.
  - numbers: pe_transpose_max = 128 x 128
  - check (static): nc_transpose(engine in {tensor,unknown}, shape>32x32): data.shape[0]<=128 and prod(free)<=128 and dst in psum and dst.dtype==data.dtype
  - source: nki.isa.nc_transpose docstring, sections Memory types and Tile size  [stated, all]
- **transpose-vector-engine-32x32** — Use Vector Engine nc_transpose (engine=nisa.engine.vector) only for tiles <= [32,32]; it may read/write SBUF or PSUM.
  - why: The Vector Engine transposes within a 32-partition quadrant only.
  - when: engine=vector transpose on a 128x128 tile.
  - fix: Let engine=unknown pick per shape, or use Tensor Engine for larger tiles.
  - numbers: vector_transpose_max = 32 x 32
  - check (static): nc_transpose(engine=vector): data.shape[0]<=32 and prod(free)<=32
  - source: nki.isa.nc_transpose docstring, section Tile size  [stated, all]
- **bn-stats-fmax-512** — Feed bn_stats at most 512 elements per partition (nl.tile_size.bn_stats_fmax) and aggregate the 6-element outputs of several calls with one bn_aggr whose input length per partition is a multiple of 3.
  - why: Hardware limit of the Vector Engine statistics unit; bn_stats emits (count, mean, var*count) pairs for even/odd elements.
  - when: LayerNorm over D=1024 in one bn_stats call.
  - fix: Loop over 512-element slices writing bn_stats outputs to offsets in one SBUF tensor, then bn_aggr once.
  - numbers: bn_stats_fmax = 512 elements; bn_stats_out = 6 elements/partition; bn_aggr_out = 2 elements/partition
  - check (static): bn_stats: prod(data.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.bn_stats_fmax (512); bn_aggr: prod(data.shape[1:]) % 3 == 0
  - source: nki.isa.bn_stats and bn_aggr docstrings  [stated, all]
- **layout-partition-dim-first-no-block-dims** — Declare on-chip (SBUF/PSUM) tensors with the partition dimension as dim 0 (<=128) and never use block dimensions or nl.par_dim.
  - why: Block dimensions and par_dim were removed; dim 0 of every on-chip tensor maps to hardware partitions and view ops cannot move it.
  - when: nl.ndarray((8, nl.par_dim(128), 512)) or shapes whose first dim exceeds 128.
  - fix: Fold extra leading dims into the free dims ((128, 8, 512)) or use a Python list of (128, 512) tensors.
  - numbers: pmax = 128
  - check (static): nl.ndarray(buffer in {sbuf,psum}): shape[0] <= 128; no nl.par_dim symbol (absent in 0.6.0)
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor docstring 'Partition dimension'; migration/index.rst 'Removing block dimensions'  [stated, all]
- **fold-simultaneous-blocks-into-free-dim** — When several tiles must be alive simultaneously, allocate one tensor with the block count folded into a free dim ((128, 8, 512)) or a Python list of tensors.
  - why: Block dimensions were removed; a list or a folded free dim gives the compiler the same liveness information.
  - when: Reductions over 8 loaded tiles after the load loop.
  - fix: add_buf = nl.ndarray((128, 8, 512)); add_buf[:, i, :] used per iteration.
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Use a Python-like list' / 'move the block dimension into the free dimension'  [stated, all]
- **tile-pmax-128** — Loop over the leading tensor dimension in chunks of nl.tile_size.pmax (128); any tile with partition size > 128 fails to compile.
  - why: SBUF and PSUM have 128 partitions and every tile maps shape[0] to the partition dimension.
  - when: Error 'Size of partition dimension 256 exceeds architecture limitation of 128'.
  - fix: for p in range(ceil(P/128)): slice p*128:min((p+1)*128, P) and handle the ragged tail with min().
  - numbers: pmax = 128
  - check (static): assert tile.shape[0] <= 128.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations  [stated, all]
- **tile-min-128-elements-per-partition** — Give every ScalarE/VectorE instruction at least ~128 elements per partition; one-element instructions run at ~100x overhead.
  - why: Static instruction overhead is ~100 engine cycles; dependent one-element tensor_scalar chains measured 222 ns (266 ScalarE cycles on NC-v3) initiation interval versus 1 cycle of useful work.
  - when: Profiler access pattern like fp32@0x4000[1,1,1][1,1,1] repeated back-to-back with src==previous dst.
  - fix: Reformulate (e.g. Mamba prefix scan with nisa.tensor_tensor_scan instead of seq_len tensor_scalars) so each instruction covers a long free dim.
  - numbers: static_overhead = ~100 engine cycles; observed_small_instr_II_nc_v3 = 222 ns (266 ScalarE cycles)
  - check (static): flag compute ops with free size < 128 in loops with trip count > 16.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a; nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Cost Model  [stated, all]
- **tile-partition-vectorization** — Merge several < 128-partition instructions of the same op into one 128-partition instruction by placing their inputs in disjoint partition ranges.
  - why: Instruction cost is independent of lane count, so two 64-partition reductions serialized cost 2x a single 128-partition one.
  - when: channels=64 (or smaller) operands repeated back-to-back.
  - fix: mm_tile = nl.zeros((128, ...), buffer=nl.psum); mm_tile[0:64] = nc_matmul(...); mm_tile[64:128] = nc_matmul(...); reduce = nisa.tensor_reduce(mm_tile, ...)
  - numbers: speedup_example = 2x
  - check (static): group consecutive same-op instructions with P<=64 whose partition ranges can be stacked.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5b  [stated, all]
- **tile-size-tradeoff** — Pick instruction tile sizes large enough to amortize ~100-cycle overhead but small enough to pipeline across engines and fit SBUF; iterate with the profiler.
  - why: Too small exposes instruction overhead; too large delays downstream engines (long first-tile latency) and raises SBUF pressure (spills).
  - when: Engine idle gaps at pipeline start, or spills, after enlarging tiles.
  - fix: Start at 128x512 per instruction; grow the free dim only while engine utilization improves.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a / Opt #3  [stated, all]
- **tile-block-k-accumulate-in-sbuf** — When K is blocked beyond what PSUM can hold, accumulate partial results in an SBUF fp32 tile with nisa.tensor_tensor(op=add) and store coalesced [128, BLOCK_N] rows.
  - why: The tutorial's final kernel (TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, N=2, K=8) turned a DMA-bound matmul (DMA 99.9% / TensorE 87%) into a compute-bound one (DMA 21.5% / TensorE 99.5% / VectorE 10.6%).
  - when: Matmul kernel with DMA active near 100% and TensorE < 90%.
  - fix: Load [TILE_K, BLOCK_N] and [TILE_K, BLOCK_M] blocks per K-block; memset fp32 result tiles; add PSUM into them; pack and store per N-block.
  - numbers: before = DMA 99.93% / TensorE 87.28%; after = DMA 21.54% / TensorE 99.50% / VectorE 10.55%
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension  [stated, trn2]
- **tile-hoist-loads-out-of-inner-loop** — Load each input tile once per outer iteration (hoist loads to the outer loop) instead of reloading inside the innermost loop.
  - why: In the naive loop the m=0,k=0 tile is reloaded N/TILE_N times; the Tensor Info widget's Load to SBUF Repeat Factor quantifies this (e.g. 16).
  - when: Repeat factor >> 1 for a tensor in the Tensor Info widget.
  - fix: Build lists of SBUF tiles for a row/column block in the outer loop, then reuse across the inner loop; trade against SBUF capacity.
  - check (static): count distinct dma loads of the same HBM region per kernel.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #1; nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Analyzing the kernel  [stated, all]
- **mlp-tkg-tile-T-in-128** — Tile the token axis of the TKG MLP in BS_TILE_SIZE=128 chunks and T-shard across LNC cores only when T >= 128*lnc and T % lnc == 0; otherwise shard on H.
  - why: A 128-token tile fills the partition dim for the output transpose and one PSUM column band; small T is better split along H so both cores stream half the weights.
  - when: LNC=2 decode MLP.
  - fix: use_t_sharding = T >= 128*lnc and lnc>=2 and T%lnc==0; else H-shard with sendrecv of partial sums
  - numbers: BS_TILE_SIZE = 128
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/mlp/mlp_tkg/mlp_tkg.py mlp_tkg  [stated, all]
- **exp-chunk-1k-free** — Issue softmax exp in chunks of ~1024 free elements (8 x 128 kv tiles) rather than one instruction over the whole row.
  - why: Balances per-instruction overhead against letting the downstream 128-wide PE transposes start earlier (pipelining).
  - when: Long-context decode softmax.
  - fix: exp_grp_size = 8; for g in range(div_ceil(n_sprior_tiles, 8)): nisa.activation(dst[:, g*1024:(g+1)*1024], op=nl.exp, ..., reduce_cmd=reset_reduce if g==0 else reduce)
  - numbers: exp_grp_size = 8 tiles = 1024 elems
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/attention/attention_tkg.py ~3218-3224  [stated, all]
- **fa-tile-8k-and-batch-budget** — Tile s_prior in 8192-position flash-attention tiles (only when s_prior > 8192) and tile the batch so 8*bs*q_head*s_active*fa_tile <= 16 MiB (10 bytes/elem for fp32 I/O).
  - why: The qk fp32 tile, its bf16 exp copy and the mask must stay comfortably inside SBUF.
  - when: Long-context decode.
  - fix: use_fa = s_prior > 8192; per_batch = (10 if fp32 else 8)*q_head*s_active*fa_tile; max_bs = 16MiB // per_batch
  - numbers: _FA_TILE_SIZE = 8192; _BATCH_TILE_SBUF_BUDGET = 16 MiB
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/attention/attention_tkg_utils.py uses_flash_attention, uses_batch_tiling  [stated, all]
- **gqa-share-kv-across-query-group** — Put the query heads that share a KV head side-by-side on the free axis of the Q moving tile so each K/V tile is loaded once per group.
  - why: Decode is bound by KV reads; grouping amortises each K/V DMA over `group` query heads.
  - when: GQA/MQA decode.
  - fix: q_group = q[:, kv*group:(kv+1)*group]  # [d, group]; qk = nc_matmul(stationary=q_group, moving=k_tile) or vice versa
  - check (static): K/V loaded per query head
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/decode_attention.py decode_attention_gqa_fwd; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/attention/attention_tkg_utils.py is_qk_swapped GQA note  [stated, all]
- **z-block-stationary-in-sbuf** — Order matmul loops N-block > M-block > K-block so the output block stays resident in SBUF and is stored to HBM exactly once.
  - why: Output is never spilled/reloaded regardless of K; only inputs stream.
  - when: Blocked GEMM.
  - fix: for n2: for m2: Z_SBUF = zeros((TILES_M, 128, TILES_N*512)); for k2: ... ; store Z_SBUF once
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/matmul.py  [stated, all]
- **free-dim-chunk-512-for-elementwise** — Chunk long free-dim elementwise/scan chains into ~512-element tiles so successive instructions pipeline.
  - why: Empirically profiled 'magic number' in the Mamba tutorial; keeps instruction size large enough to amortise overhead while allowing overlap.
  - when: Long seq_len elementwise pipelines.
  - fix: seq_len_fsize = 512; for t in nl.static_range(seq_len // 512): ...
  - numbers: seq_len_fsize = 512
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:src/nki_samples/tutorials/fused_mamba/mamba_nki_kernels.py mamba_v3  [stated, all]
- **interp-overlapping-chunks-along-free-dim** — Chunk stencil/upsample inputs along the free (H or D) axis with a one-row overlap (step = chunk-1) and compute the shared boundary output rows from the chunk that owns both inputs.
  - why: Interpolation needs neighbours on both sides; overlapping windows keep every output computable from a single SBUF tile.
  - when: Any 1-neighbour stencil over a dim too large for SBUF.
  - fix: for h in nl.static_range(ceil((h_src-wdw)/(wdw-1))+1): start=max(0,h*(wdw-1)); end=min(wdw+h*(wdw-1), h_src); dst_start = 2*start+1 if start else 0
  - numbers: chunk_size = 10 (2D) / 4 (3D)
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/interpolate_bilinear_fwd.py  [stated, all]
- **partition-dim-max-128** — Keep the first (partition) dimension of every SBUF and PSUM tensor at or below 128.
  - why: SBUF has 128 physical partitions; dim 0 of an on-chip tensor maps one-to-one onto them, so a larger dim 0 cannot be allocated.
  - when: Any nl.ndarray(..., buffer=nl.sbuf|nl.psum) whose shape[0] > 128, or compiler error 'Partition dimension exceeds 128'.
  - fix: Tile the outer dimension with an outer loop (TiledRange(outer, 128) or div_ceil) so each tile has shape[0] <= 128.
  - numbers: pmax = 128 partitions
  - check (static): for every on-chip ndarray: assert shape[0] <= 128 (nl.tile_size.pmax)
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: Step 2: Design Tiling Strategy / Hardware Constraints Quick Reference  [stated, all]
- **nc-transpose-tile-128x128** — Tile nc_transpose inputs to at most 128x128 and route the output through PSUM before further use.
  - why: nc_transpose is executed on the tensor engine as an identity TRANSPOSE matmul using the PSUM array as intermediate buffer, so both dims are bounded by the PE array and the dst by the PSUM free-dim limit.
  - when: nc_transpose on a tile larger than 128x128 or with a PSUM dst whose free dim exceeds the PSUM limit ('PSUM dimension exceeds limit').
  - fix: Loop over 128x128 chunks: nisa.nc_transpose(dst=out[f:f+128, p:p+128], data=in[p:p+128, f:f+128]); then nisa.tensor_copy PSUM->SBUF.
  - numbers: max_tile = 128 x 128
  - check (static): nc_transpose: assert data.shape[0] <= 128 and data.shape[1] <= 128 and dst free dim <= psum limit
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/indexing-patterns.md :: nc_transpose Indexing; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/transpose-and-layout.md :: Core Technique 1: nc_transpose  [stated, all]
- **instruction-count-limit** — Keep the generated instruction count under the NEFF limit by avoiding deep full unrolling of large loops; split the kernel or use runtime loops when it is exceeded.
  - why: affine_range/static_range/range loops are fully unrolled at compile time, so every iteration becomes separate instructions; the compiler raises NCC_EVRF007/NCC_EBVF030/NCC_EXTP004 when the per-NEFF limit is exceeded.
  - when: Compiler error 'The number of instructions generated exceeds the limit' (NCC_EVRF007, NCC_EBVF030, NCC_EXTP004).
  - fix: Increase tile sizes to reduce iteration count, move hot loops to nl.fori_loop (structured on-chip loop, not unrolled), or split into multiple kernels.
  - check (static): estimate unrolled instruction count = sum(product of trip counts of nested unrolled loops * ops per body); warn above a configurable threshold
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-debugging/references/ncc-memory-resource-errors.md :: NCC_EBVF030 / NCC_EXTP004; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: Loop Types  [inferred, all]
- **matmul-min-tile-128x512** — Issue matmuls with full tiles K=128, M=128, N=512 (stationary [128,128], moving [128,512]) whenever the problem allows.
  - why: TE throughput per initiation interval scales with the tile: undersized M or K reduce throughput linearly; a (128,512) tile keeps PSUM pipelining efficient.
  - when: nc_matmul with M < 128 or K < 128 on hot source lines; profile shows K/128, M/128 < 1.
  - fix: Re-tile so stationary and moving operands use the full 128-partition contraction and M=128; pad or batch small dims.
  - numbers: min_matmul_tile = (128, 512); achieved_utilization_mixed_example = 39% vs 98% with peak tiles
  - check (profile): from Instruction.operands extract K,M,N per MATMUL line; flag lines with K<128 or M<128 weighted by adjusted_flops
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: Kernel Efficiency Guidelines / 5. Minimum Tile Sizes; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/te_inefficiency.md :: Step 2  [stated, all]
- **vector-scalar-min-free-dim-64** — Give vector/scalar engine instructions a free dimension of at least 64 elements (prefer 128) with the full 128 partitions.
  - why: Each instruction has fixed issue overhead; tiny free dims make static instruction overhead dominate execution.
  - when: activation/tensor_tensor/tensor_scalar on tiles with free dim < 64.
  - fix: Use column_tiling_dim = 32 if T<=32, 64 if T<=64, else 128 (production mlp_tkg rule); batch rows to fill 128 partitions.
  - numbers: min_vector_tile = (128, 64); column_tiling_dim = 32 (T<=32) / 64 (T<=64) / 128 (T>64)
  - check (static): for vector/scalar ISA ops: warn if dst free size < 64
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: 5. Minimum Tile Sizes (Vector/Scalar tile sizing)  [stated, all]
- **use-full-128-partitions** — Lay out every on-chip tile so the partition dimension is the full 128 (H0 = nl.tile_size.pmax) and fold remaining size into the free dims.
  - why: Each partition is an independent lane of every compute engine; using fewer partitions leaves lanes idle.
  - when: Tiles allocated with shape[0] < 128 on hot paths (e.g. a [T, ...] tile with small token count T in decode).
  - fix: Reshape the problem so a 128-multiple dimension (hidden/H) is on partitions: e.g. [H] -> [128, H/128]; put the small dim (T) on the free axis.
  - numbers: pmax = 128
  - check (static): warn if an SBUF tile shape[0] < 128 while another dim is a multiple of 128
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: 4. Maximize Hardware Parallelism (P=128)  [stated, all]
- **block-m-n-to-cut-input-reloads** — Block the output over M and N so each input tile is loaded once per block and reused across many matmuls, rather than reloading operands in the innermost loop.
  - why: With naive (m, n, k) loops each rhs tile is reloaded once per m-tile; blocking cut rhs reloads from 32x to 3x, reduced DMA time 6x and total time 3.5x in the worked example.
  - when: Profile excess_ratio >> 1 with reload_excess dominating; TensorInfo input repeat factor > 1.5x.
  - fix: Pre-load lhsT tiles for an M-block (e.g. 8-12 tiles) into SBUF, load each rhs K-tile once per (m_block, n), then run all bm x k matmuls.
  - numbers: V0_rhs_repeat = 32x; V1_rhs_repeat = 3x; speedup = 3.5x total, 6.0x DMA
  - check (profile): repeat = sum(DmaPacketAggregated.transfer_bytes for IN tensor)/TensorInfo.size; flag > 1.5
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/example-bounds-analysis.md :: V1: Blocking free dimension  [stated, all]
- **ask-for-friendly-layout** — When the given tensor layout forces strided DMA or complex reshaping, ask the user to change it: reduction dim last (contiguous), dims aligned to 128 (partition) and 512 (PSUM free), pre-transposed to avoid strided loads.
  - why: Layout determines whether DMA can issue long contiguous descriptors and whether matmul tiles are full; a layout fix removes overhead no kernel-side trick can.
  - when: Input layout requires TensorView.slice(step) gathers or nc_transpose in the hot loop.
  - fix: Propose: 'Would you allow changing the layout to [proposed]? This simplifies the kernel and improves performance.'
  - numbers: align_partition = 128; align_psum_free = 512
  - check (static): flag kernels where >50% of DMA bytes are strided or where every matmul is preceded by nc_transpose
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: 1. Tensor Layout Flexibility (Conditional)  [stated, all]
- **reshape-nd-to-2d-for-tiling** — Collapse leading batch dims into a single outer dim ([B,S,H] -> [B*S, H]) with a zero-copy reshape on the HBM tensor before tiling.
  - why: A 2-D view lets one TiledRange over the outer dim fill 128 partitions and keeps the last (contiguous) dim as the DMA free dim.
  - when: Kernels iterating nested batch/sequence loops with partially filled partition tiles.
  - fix: x_2d = x.reshape((outer, last)); y_2d = y.reshape(...); tile over outer with TiledRange(outer, 128).
  - check (static): flag nested loops over leading dims whose inner tile shape[0] < 128 when product of leading dims >= 128
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/memory-patterns.md :: Reshape for 2D Processing; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/common-patterns.md :: rmsnorm_quant  [stated, all]
- **tiledrange-and-div-ceil-for-remainders** — Use TiledRange(total, tile) (or div_ceil + min()) for every tiled dimension so the last partial tile is handled, and never write (n + d - 1) // d inline.
  - why: Remainder tiles are the most common source of out-of-bounds slices; TiledRange exposes start_offset/size/end_offset and supports nested subtiles.
  - when: Loops computing tile bounds by hand or assuming divisibility.
  - fix: for p in TiledRange(outer, 128): dma_copy(dst=t[0:p.size, :], src=x[p.start_offset:p.end_offset, :]).
  - check (static): flag range(total // tile) loops where total % tile != 0 is possible
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: Utility Selection Guide (Always Use); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/memory-patterns.md :: TiledRange Pattern  [stated, all]
- **block-free-dims-after-hoisting** — After hoisting, block the M and N free dimensions (several tiles per DMA) so each DMA transfer moves more bytes and fewer descriptors are issued.
  - why: Larger transfers amortize DMA trigger overhead and improve HBM efficiency, although each block takes longer to arrive so prefetch depth matters.
  - when: Kernel still DMA-bound after hoisting (DMA ~99% active, TensorE ~99%).
  - fix: TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=2, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N=2 -> BLOCK_M=256, BLOCK_N=1024; load lhsT_tiles[bm][k], rhs_tiles[bn][k] per block, then loop bm,bn,k over nc_matmul.
  - numbers: TensorE_active = 99.52%; DMA_active = 95.70%; BLOCK_M = 256; BLOCK_N = 1024
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Overlapping data and compute through blocking  [stated, trn2]
- **block-k-with-sbuf-accumulation** — Block the contraction dimension K too and accumulate partial PSUM results into SBUF tiles with nisa.tensor_tensor(op=nl.add) to turn a memory-bound matmul into a compute-bound one.
  - why: Blocking K lets both operand blocks and the result stay resident, raising arithmetic intensity; the price is VectorE work for the SBUF accumulation.
  - when: DMA engines still active most of the kernel after blocking only M and N.
  - fix: TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, TILES_IN_BLOCK_N=2, TILES_IN_BLOCK_K=8; result_tmps memset(0) in SBUF; per block: nc_matmul over bk into a PSUM tile, then tensor_tensor(dst=result_tmps[m][bm][bn], data1=same, data2=psum_tile, op=nl.add).
  - numbers: DMA_active = 21.54%; TensorE_active = 99.50%; VectorE_active = 10.55%; TILES_IN_BLOCK_M = 16; TILES_IN_BLOCK_N = 2; TILES_IN_BLOCK_K = 8
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking the contraction dimension  [stated, trn2]
- **matmul-blocking-config-and-sbuf-budget** — Size matmul blocks so arithmetic intensity exceeds the threshold while all live blocks (operands plus result accumulators) fit the SBUF budget.
  - why: With 16 M-tiles, 2 N-tiles and 8 K-tiles the AI is 683 Flops/Byte; lhsT needs 4 MB, rhs 2 MB and results 4*NUM_BLOCK_M MB, which fits 24 MB only while M <= 8192.
  - when: Choosing TILES_IN_BLOCK_* meta-parameters.
  - fix: Start from TILES_IN_BLOCK_M=16, N=2, K=8 for bf16 and shrink the M block when M > 8192 or SBUF spills appear.
  - numbers: AI = 683 Flops/Byte; lhsT_block = 4 MB; rhs_block = 2 MB; result = 4*NUM_BLOCK_M MB; sbuf_budget = 24 MB; max_M_without_spill = 8192
  - check (static): bytes(lhsT_block)+bytes(rhs_block)+bytes(result_tiles) <= 24 MB.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3: Blocking M, N and K Dimension  [stated, trn1]
- **ai-formula-k-blocking** — Expect lower arithmetic intensity whenever one of M, N, K is much smaller than the others, and block all three dimensions rather than only the free ones.
  - why: AI = 2MNK / (2(MK+KN+MN)) for 2-byte dtypes; requiring full K resident caps the M/N block size by SBUF capacity.
  - when: Skinny matmuls or very large K.
  - fix: Block K and accumulate partials in SBUF (see block-k-with-sbuf-accumulation), accepting extra VectorE adds.
  - numbers: AI_formula = 2*M*N*K/(2*(M*K+K*N+M*N))
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 3  [stated, all]
- **keep-layout-consistent-across-steps** — Choose one partition mapping (e.g. channels on P) and keep it through all steps of a fused kernel, even if a single step would prefer otherwise, to avoid transposes.
  - why: A transpose between steps costs a TensorE instruction or an inefficient transposed load that outweighs a locally cheaper instruction.
  - when: Multi-step element-wise pipelines with conflicting broadcast directions.
  - fix: Accept p-dim broadcast + tensor_tensor for B/C in Mamba step 3/5 because delta/u already have channels on P.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Step 3  [stated, all]
- **loop-order-prioritize-largest-reuse** — Order loops so that the dimension over which the largest tensors are reused is innermost (and hoist their loads above it), prioritizing reuse of the bigger operand when reuse dimensions conflict.
  - why: delta/u (channels x seq) are reused across states while B/C (states x seq) are reused across channels; channels (4096) dwarf state_size (16) so delta/u reuse wins.
  - when: Two input groups reused along different loop dimensions.
  - fix: for i_channel_tile: load delta_i,u_i; for i_state: steps 1-6  (instead of state outer, channel inner).
  - numbers: latency_before = 2.34 ms; latency_after = 1.61 ms; reduction = 31% (reorder ~30%, fusion ~1%); VectorE_active_after = 99.63%
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Minimizing data reloading by loop reordering  [stated, all]
- **tile-free-dim-to-avoid-spills** — Tile large free-dimension extents (e.g. seq_len) with an extra loop level so live tiles stay small enough to avoid SBUF fragmentation and spill/reload traffic.
  - why: Growing seq_len 16x without tiling increased latency 33x and dropped VectorE to 58.93% with new qSyncSpillReload/qVectorSpillReload rows; tiling seq_len at 512 recovered 94.85%.
  - when: Profile shows qSyncSpillReload0 / qVectorSpillReload0 activity and blocking waits on them.
  - fix: Add a seq_len tile loop (seq_len_fsize=512 to start) and carry scan state via initial=.
  - numbers: untiled_latency_8K = 53.33 ms; tiled_latency_8K = 27.8 ms; reduction = 48%; VectorE_untiled = 58.93%; VectorE_tiled = 94.85%; scaling_eff_v2_8K = 49.04%; scaling_eff_v3_8K = 92.09%
  - check (profile): Live bytes per partition of all tiles in a loop body > ~half SBUF partition -> suggest tiling.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Increasing input seq_len size  [stated, all]
- **vector-ops-parallel-axis-on-partition** — For non-matmul (vector/scalar/gpsimd) instructions map the parallel axis to the partition dimension and the contraction axis to the free dimension.
  - why: Layout Constraint #2: engines reduce along the free dim per partition.
  - when: Row-wise reductions like RMSNorm or pooling.
  - fix: tensor_reduce over axis=free with rows on P.
  - check (static): Reduction over dim 0 of an SBUF tile -> suggest transposing layout.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Layout considerations  [stated, all]
- **handle-partition-remainder-with-min** — Bound the last partition tile with min(p_end, sz_p) (or nl.ds) so inputs whose first dim is not a multiple of 128 stay in bounds.
  - why: Tiles must not exceed pmax, and the final tile may be partial.
  - when: sz_p % 128 != 0.
  - fix: for p in range(math.ceil(sz_p/128)): i_p = slice(p*128, min((p+1)*128, sz_p))
  - source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations  [stated, all]
- **output-proj-tkg-layout-n-next-to-s** — In decode, place the heads dimension next to the (tiny) sequence dimension ([D,B,N,S]) so GQA loads several heads in one DMA; CTE uses [B,N,D,S] instead.
  - why: With S small, N adjacent to S makes a contiguous free extent for multi-head loads.
  - when: Choosing attention output layout for TKG vs CTE.
  - fix: TKG: attention[d,b,n,s]; CTE: attention[b,n,d,s].
  - source: nki/library/api/output-projection-tkg.rst :: Background  [stated, all]
- **attention-cte-flash-sectioning** — For K/V longer than 10K tokens process the KV sequence in 8K-token sections (flash attention) so each section fits SBUF.
  - why: Full scores for very long sequences exceed on-chip memory.
  - when: Prefill attention with long context.
  - fix: attention_cte handles this internally; replicate in custom kernels.
  - numbers: section_tokens = 8K; threshold = 10K
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-cte.rst :: Flash Attention  [stated, all]
- **rmsnorm-collapse-outer-dims** — Collapse all leading dims into one outer dim ([B,S,H] -> [B*S, H]) and tile it by 128 so every partition processes one token's H vector.
  - why: Row-wise ops only touch the processing (minor) dim; full-partition tiles use every engine lane.
  - when: RMSNorm / quantization / row-wise kernels.
  - fix: outer = B*S; for t in range(ceil(outer/128)): tile=[128, H]
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Input Tensor Outer Dimension Collapse; Tiling  [stated, all]
- **rmsnorm-tile-h-by-512-for-gamma-matmul** — Tile the hidden dim in 512-element chunks when gamma is broadcast via a TensorE matmul, matching gemm_moving_fmax so each chunk fills a PSUM bank and pipelines ScalarE (scale), TensorE (gamma broadcast) and VectorE (apply).
  - why: 512 is the TensorE moving free-dim limit; splitting the work across three engines gives pipeline parallelism.
  - when: RMSNorm with learned gamma.
  - fix: for h in range(H//512): gamma_bc = matmul(ones[1,128].T, gamma[1, h*512:(h+1)*512]) in PSUM; scalar_tensor_tensor(x_chunk, inv_rms, gamma_bc)
  - numbers: H_tile = 512; S_tile = 128
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Tiling; Gamma Broadcast  [stated, trn2]
- **cross-entropy-chunk-sizing** — Choose the vocabulary chunk for online-LSE cross entropy as V for V <= 32K, 32768/40960 for 32K-128K, 65535 (bf16) or 32768 (fp32) for 128K-256K, and keep positions_per_batch x chunk_size x dtype_bytes <= 24 MiB.
  - why: Chunks must fit SBUF (24 MiB budget) and the free-dim hardware limit (65535) while minimizing loop iterations.
  - when: Large-vocab loss kernel.
  - fix: cross_entropy_forward(logits, targets, positions_per_batch=32, chunk_size=32768)
  - numbers: sbuf_budget = 24 MiB; F_MAX = 65535
  - check (static): ppb*chunk*bytes <= 24 MiB and chunk <= min(V, 65535).
  - source: nki/library/api/cross-entropy.rst :: Chunk Size Selection Guide  [stated, trn2]

## Tensor Engine matmul (52)

- **mm-operands-sbuf-dst-psum** — Place nc_matmul stationary and moving operands in SBUF and the dst tile in PSUM.
  - why: The Tensor Engine can only read its inputs from SBUF and only writes its accumulator output to PSUM; any other buffer placement is rejected.
  - when: nc_matmul whose dst is an SBUF/HBM tensor or whose inputs are PSUM/HBM tensors.
  - fix: Allocate dst with nl.ndarray(..., buffer=nl.psum); stage inputs into SBUF (dma_copy) first; evacuate PSUM with tensor_copy/activation afterwards.
  - check (static): for every nisa.nc_matmul: buffer(stationary)==sbuf and buffer(moving)==sbuf and buffer(dst)==psum
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Memory types  [stated, all]
- **mm-contraction-on-partition-dim** — Lay out both nc_matmul operands so the contraction (K) dimension is their partition dimension, with identical partition sizes <= 128.
  - why: nc_matmul computes dst = stationary.T @ moving; the systolic array contracts along the 128 partition rows, so K must be the partition axis of both tiles.
  - when: Shapes where K is a free dimension, or stationary.shape[0] != moving.shape[0], or partition dim > 128.
  - fix: Transpose the operand (nc_transpose / dma_transpose / load with transposed access pattern) so K is dim 0; tile K into chunks of <= nl.tile_size.pmax (128) and accumulate.
  - numbers: pmax = 128 partitions
  - check (static): nc_matmul: stationary.shape[0] == moving.shape[0] <= nl.tile_size.pmax (or <= tile_size[0] when tiling mode is on)
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, sections Layout and Tile size  [stated, all]
- **mm-stationary-free-le-128** — Keep the free dimension of the nc_matmul stationary operand at most 128 (nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax).
  - why: The stationary tile is latched into the 128x128 PE array; its free size maps onto the 128 PE columns and becomes the partition dim of dst.
  - when: stationary.shape[1:] product > 128 (e.g. passing a [128, 512] weight tile as stationary).
  - fix: Tile M (stationary free) into 128-wide chunks, or swap operand roles so the large dimension is the moving free dim (up to 512).
  - numbers: gemm_stationary_fmax = 128 elements
  - check (static): nc_matmul: prod(stationary.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax (128), or <= tile_size[1] when tiling mode on
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size; nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax  [stated, all]
- **mm-moving-free-le-512-pre-trn3** — On trn1/trn2 keep the nc_matmul moving free dimension at most 512 (nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax).
  - why: The moving free size equals the dst free size, and one PSUM bank holds 512 fp32 elements per partition (2 KiB); NeuronCore-v2/v3 cannot span banks in one matmul.
  - when: moving free dim > 512 on trn1/trn2 or when the kernel should be portable.
  - fix: Loop over N in 512-element chunks, each writing its own PSUM region/bank.
  - numbers: gemm_moving_fmax = 512 elements; psum_bank_fmax = 512 fp32 elements; psum_bank_fmax_bytes = 2048 bytes
  - check (static): nc_matmul on nc_version<=3: prod(moving.shape[1:]) <= nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax (512)
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size; nl.tile_size  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-moving-free-trn3-4096-8192** — On trn3 the nc_matmul moving free dimension may go up to 4096 for fp32 dst or 8192 for bf16 dst (entire 8-bank PSUM).
  - why: NeuronCore-v4 lets a single matmul write across all 8 PSUM banks; bf16 outputs are half the size so twice as many fit.
  - when: Kernels hard-coding 512 moving chunks on trn3 leave throughput on the table; exceeding 4096/8192 fails.
  - fix: Pick moving chunk size from target: 512 for v2/v3, 4096 (fp32) or 8192 (bf16) for v4; gate with nisa.get_nc_version().
  - numbers: moving_fmax_fp32_v4 = 4096 elements; moving_fmax_bf16_v4 = 8192 elements; psum_num_banks = 8
  - check (static): nc_matmul on nc_version==4: prod(moving.shape[1:]) <= (8192 if dst.dtype==bf16 else 4096)
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tile size  [stated, trn3]
- **mm-dst-dtype-fp32-pre-trn3** — Declare the nc_matmul dst PSUM tile as float32 on trn1/trn2; bf16 dst is only allowed starting trn3.
  - why: Tensor Engine accumulates in fp32 internally; only NeuronCore-v4 can down-convert to bf16 on PSUM write.
  - when: nl.ndarray(..., dtype=nl.bfloat16, buffer=nl.psum) used as a matmul dst on trn2.
  - fix: Use dtype=nl.float32 for the PSUM accumulator and cast on the PSUM->SBUF evacuation (tensor_copy/activation casts for free).
  - check (static): nc_matmul: dst.dtype == float32 if nc_version<=3 else dst.dtype in {float32, bfloat16}
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Data types  [stated, all]
- **mm-fp32-operands-must-pair** — Do not mix an fp32/tfloat32 nc_matmul operand with a lower-precision (bf16/fp16/fp8) operand.
  - why: The PE array runs in a single precision mode per instruction: if either input is fp32/tf32 both must be; other dtypes may be mixed freely.
  - when: stationary bf16 with moving float32 (common when activations stay fp32 and weights are bf16).
  - fix: Cast one side (tensor_copy / activation with dtype cast) so both are fp32-class or both are <=16-bit; prefer bf16 for 4x PE throughput.
  - check (static): nc_matmul: (stationary.dtype in {fp32,tf32}) == (moving.dtype in {fp32,tf32})
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Data types  [stated, all]
- **mm-accumulate-first-write-must-overwrite** — Start every PSUM accumulation group with accumulate=False (or accumulate=None) and only then use accumulate=True.
  - why: accumulate=True adds onto existing PSUM content; on an uninitialized location the result is undefined on all targets. The default None lets the compiler infer first-write-overwrite.
  - when: A K-loop that passes accumulate=True unconditionally, or accumulates into a PSUM tile that was never written by a matmul.
  - fix: Use accumulate=(k > 0) in the loop, or omit the parameter so the compiler tracks first write.
  - check (static): for each PSUM region: the first nc_matmul writing it must not have accumulate=True literal
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Accumulation mode  [stated, all]
- **mm-pe-tiling-mode-rules** — When using Tensor Engine tiling mode set both tile_position and tile_size, with start_row a multiple of row_size, column_size == 128 and start_column == 0.
  - why: Row tiling splits the 128 PE rows into 2x64 (v2+) or 4x32 (v3+) tiles so several small-K matmuls run concurrently; the exposed API currently only allows row tiling.
  - when: Small-K (<=64) matmuls at low PE utilization; or tile_position set without tile_size.
  - fix: Use tile_size=(64,128)/(32,128) and tile_position=(0|32|64|96, 0) across independent matmuls; keep stationary within the chosen tile.
  - numbers: row_tiles_v2 = 2 x 64 rows; row_tiles_v3 = 4 x 32 rows
  - check (static): nc_matmul: (tile_position set) == (tile_size set); tile_size[1]==128; tile_position[1]==0; tile_position[0] % tile_size[0] == 0; tile_size[0] in {32 (v3+),64,128}
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tiling mode and param docs  [stated, all]
- **mm-double-row-fp8-perf-mode** — Use perf_mode=nisa.matmul_perf_mode.double_row only on trn2/trn3 with fp8 operands shaped [K/2, 2, free], never together with column tiling.
  - why: double_row packs two FP8 pairs per PE for 2x throughput by splitting K between the partition dim and a first free dim of exactly 2.
  - when: double_row on trn1, with bf16 operands, or with first free dim != 2.
  - fix: Reshape operands to [128, 2, M] / [128, 2, N] fp8 tiles (contraction = 256) and set perf_mode=double_row.
  - numbers: contraction_double_row = 256 per instruction
  - check (static): nc_matmul(perf_mode=double_row): nc_version>=3 and dtypes in fp8 set and stationary.shape[1]==2 and moving.shape[1]==2
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, sections Performance mode, Data types, Layout  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-onezero-hint-for-fp32** — Set is_stationary_onezero/is_moving_onezero=True when an fp32 operand contains only 0/1 values (masks, one-hot, identity).
  - why: The hint lets the compiler use a faster fp32 PE path, up to 2x; it has no effect for non-fp32 operands.
  - when: fp32 identity/one-hot/selection matrices used as a matmul operand without the hint.
  - fix: Add is_stationary_onezero=True (or is_moving_onezero=True) on the one-zero operand.
  - numbers: speedup = up to 2x for fp32
  - check (static): nc_matmul with fp32 operand built from nl.shared_identity_matrix/ones/iota-compare without onezero hint
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, param is_stationary_onezero  [stated, all]
- **mx-matmul-trn3-only** — Only call nisa.nc_matmul_mx and nisa.quantize_mx when targeting trn3 (NeuronCore-v4).
  - why: MX (microscaling) datapaths exist only in the v4 Tensor and Vector Engines.
  - when: nc_matmul_mx/quantize_mx in a kernel compiled for trn1/trn2.
  - fix: Guard with nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen4 and fall back to bf16 nc_matmul elsewhere.
  - check (static): call to nc_matmul_mx/quantize_mx requires target nc_version>=4
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul_mx and nki.isa.quantize_mx docstrings, notes  [stated, trn3]
- **mx-matmul-tile-size** — Shape nc_matmul_mx operands with partition size a multiple of 32 (<=128), an even stationary free size <= 128, and moving free <= 4096 (fp32 dst) or 8192 (bf16 dst).
  - why: Scale groups span 8-partition blocks inside 32-partition quadrants; column tiling is unavailable so stationary free must fit 128 PE columns.
  - when: Odd stationary free sizes or K tiles of 64 that are not multiples of 32.
  - fix: Pad K to a multiple of 32 and M to an even number; use row tiling (tile_size=(64|32,128)) for small K.
  - check (static): nc_matmul_mx: shape[0] % 32 == 0 and <= 128; stationary free even and <= 128; moving free <= 4096/8192 by dst dtype
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul_mx docstring, section Tile size  [stated, trn3]
- **mx-matmul-row-tiling-only** — Use only row tiling for nc_matmul_mx: tile_size=(row,128) and tile_position=(start_row,0).
  - why: The MX datapath supports slicing PE rows (2x64 or 4x32) but not PE columns.
  - when: tile_size with column_size != 128 on nc_matmul_mx.
  - fix: Set column_size=128, start_column=0.
  - check (static): nc_matmul_mx: tile_size[1]==128 and tile_position[1]==0
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul_mx docstring, section Tiling Mode  [stated, trn3]
- **mm-contraction-on-partition** — Put the contraction dim K on the partition axis of both matmul inputs: nc_matmul(stationary[K,M], moving[K,N]) computes stationary.T @ moving -> [M,N].
  - why: Each SBUF partition feeds one row of PEs, so K is streamed across partitions; the free axis of stationary becomes the output partition axis and the free axis of moving becomes the output free axis.
  - when: Any matmul formulation.
  - fix: Deliver LHS pre-transposed ([K,M]) from the framework when possible to avoid an on-chip transpose.
  - check (static): assert stationary.shape[0]==moving.shape[0]<=128.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Layout; nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Layout considerations  [stated, all]
- **mm-tile-size-limits** — Respect nc_matmul limits: stationary free <= 128, partition (K) <= 128, moving free <= 512 (one PSUM bank = 512 fp32 per partition).
  - why: 128 PE columns bound stationary_fsize; 128 PE rows/SBUF partitions bound K; each instruction writes a single PSUM bank holding 512 fp32 values per partition.
  - when: Shapes exceeding these in a single call.
  - fix: Tile M and N into independent calls; tile K into accumulating calls into the same PSUM tile.
  - numbers: stationary_fmax = 128; pmax = 128; moving_fmax = 512; psum_bank_fmax = 512 fp32
  - check (static): check against nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax=128, pmax=128, gemm_moving_fmax=512, psum_bank_fmax=512.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tile Size; nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations  [stated, all]
- **mm-ideal-back-to-back-sequence** — Aim for long runs of LoadStationary(128x128) / MultiplyMoving(128x512) pairs with no intervening engine switches.
  - why: TensorE is deeply pipelined with background LoadStationary; the largest tiles keep the array in the regime where MM, not LS, bounds throughput.
  - when: Matmul-heavy kernels with TensorE < 90% busy or small MM free sizes.
  - fix: Reorder loops so the moving tile reaches N=512 and the stationary tile is reused across several moving tiles.
  - numbers: ideal_stationary = 128x128; ideal_moving = 128x512
  - check (static): compute avg moving free size and stationary reuse count per nc_matmul.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Performance Consideration  [stated, all]
- **mm-initiation-interval-model** — Estimate MultiplyMoving cost as max(N, 64) TensorE cycles for BF16/FP16/TF32/FP8 inputs (N = moving free size); FP32 inputs cost ~4x.
  - why: TensorE is pipelined so initiation interval, not latency, matters; MM_INIT_LATENCY is 64 cycles on NeuronCore-v2 and small-N instructions are turnaround-bound.
  - when: Cost modeling or many small-N matmuls.
  - fix: Downcast FP32 operands to BF16/FP16/TF32/FP8 before matmul; keep N >= 64 (ideally 512).
  - numbers: MM_INIT_LATENCY_v2 = 64 cycles; fp32_penalty = ~4x
  - check (simulator): mm_cycles = max(N, 64) * (4 if fp32 else 1).
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Cost Model  [stated, trn1]
- **mm-fast-load-stationary-vector-moving** — For matrix-vector products (decode GEMV, M or N << 128), make the large matrix the stationary tensor and the short vector the moving tensor.
  - why: LoadStationary is pure data movement and runs up to 4x faster than a MultiplyMoving of the same free size; with the short tensor as moving, MM issues every ~64 cycles instead of every ~128+.
  - when: Profiler shows LDWEIGHTS with 1 element/partition and MATMUL with 128 elements/partition, or nl.matmul with a [1,K] x [K,N] shape.
  - fix: Swap operands: nc_matmul(stationary=W[K,128], moving=x[K,1..]) and transpose the (tiny) output, or restructure to batch tokens into N.
  - numbers: fast_LS_speedup = up to 4x; short_moving_MM_II = ~64 cycles; short_stationary_MM_II = ~128 cycles
  - check (static): flag nc_matmul where stationary free size < moving free size / 4 and stationary free < 32.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Fast LoadStationary; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #7  [stated, all]
- **mm-tensore-throughput-trn2** — Use TensorE peak numbers per NeuronCore-v3 for roofline math: 158 FP8, 79 BF16/FP16/TF32, 20 FP32 dense TFLOPS (316 sparse); 8 cores give 1299 FP8 / 667 BF16 / 181 FP32 TFLOPS per chip.
  - why: TensorE is a 128x128 systolic array at 2.4 GHz with 2x128 inputs/cycle (4x128 FP8).
  - when: Computing ridge point: 79e12 FLOPS / (2.9e12/8 B/s per core) ~ 218 FLOP/B per core for BF16.
  - fix: If arithmetic intensity (FLOP per HBM byte) < ~218 on trn2 BF16 the kernel is memory-bound; optimize DMA, not TensorE.
  - numbers: trn2_core_fp8_tflops = 158; trn2_core_bf16_tflops = 79; trn2_core_fp32_tflops = 20; trn2_core_sparse_tflops = 316; trn2_chip_bf16_tflops = 667; trn2_chip_fp8_tflops = 1299; trn2_chip_fp32_tflops = 181; bf16_ridge_point_per_core = ~218 FLOP/B (inferred)
  - check (simulator): ai = flops / hbm_bytes; compare to 79e12 / 362e9.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine; about-neuron/arch/neuron-hardware/trainium2.rst :: Trainium2 chip components  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-double-fp8-trn2** — To double matmul throughput on Trainium2, use FP8_E4/FP8_E5 inputs with perf_mode=nisa.matmul_perf_mode.double_row and shapes stationary [128,2,128], moving [128,2,512] (K=256 per instruction).
  - why: Each PE multiplies two FP8 pairs per cycle; the contraction dim 256 is split into 128 partitions x a major free dim of 2. The sequence takes the same time as a BF16 K=128 pair. FP8_E3 gets no speedup. Accumulation remains FP32.
  - when: FP8-quantized weights on trn2 with K >= 256.
  - fix: Pad K to a multiple of 2 with zeros; do not combine with column tiling, sparse matmul, or transpose mode; mixing E4 in one operand and E5 in the other is allowed.
  - numbers: effective_K = 256; stationary_max = [128,2,128]; moving_max = [128,2,512]; throughput = 2x BF16
  - check (static): if dtype in (fp8_e4, fp8_e5) and perf_mode==double_row: assert shape[1]==2 for both operands.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Double FP8 Matmul Performance  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-transpose-mode-trn2** — On Trainium2 use nisa.nc_transpose(engine=tensor) / nc_matmul(is_transpose=True) rather than an explicit identity matmul.
  - why: Transpose mode is bit-accurate for NaN/Inf, 2x faster for FP32, and emits FP16/BF16 PSUM output for 16-bit inputs (halving eviction bytes) instead of FP32. FP8 input yields 16-bit output with upper 8 bits zero.
  - when: Any PF transpose on trn2.
  - fix: nisa.nc_transpose(dst, src, engine=nisa.engine.tensor)
  - numbers: fp32_transpose_speedup = 2x
  - check (static): flag nc_matmul whose moving/stationary is a constant identity.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Built-in Transpose Support  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-psum-accumulation-group** — Accumulate over K > 128 by issuing successive nc_matmul calls into the same PSUM tile; the first write overwrites and later ones accumulate in FP32 (auto-detected, or set accumulate=True/False).
  - why: PSUM supports read-accumulate-write per element driven by TensorE; a run of matmuls into one bank is a matmul accumulation group.
  - when: K-tiled matmuls.
  - fix: psum = nl.ndarray((M,N), fp32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in range(K//128): nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=a[k], moving=b[k])
  - check (static): verify all K-slices target the same PSUM allocation and no intervening non-TensorE write.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Near-memory accumulation in PSUM  [stated, all]
- **mm-eight-outstanding-groups** — Rotate output tiles across the 8 PSUM banks (8 x 2 KiB per partition) so TensorE can start the next accumulation group while VectorE/ScalarE evict the previous one.
  - why: PSUM has 128 partitions x 16 KiB = 8 banks of 512 fp32; TensorE can have up to eight outstanding accumulation groups.
  - when: TensorE idle waiting for PSUM eviction (semaphore on Vector/Scalar).
  - fix: Allocate PSUM result tiles per (m,n) tile inside the loop so the allocator double/triple-buffers banks.
  - numbers: psum_banks = 8; bank_size_per_partition = 2 KiB (512 fp32); psum_total = 2 MiB
  - check (static): count live PSUM tiles; flag if 1 bank reused serially with eviction on the critical path.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Near-memory accumulation in PSUM  [stated, all]
- **mm-full-pe-columns** — Make the stationary free size 128 so MATMUL uses all 128 PE columns; a '128*96' operand in the profiler means 25% of the array is idle.
  - why: The stationary free axis maps to PE columns / output partitions; fewer than 128 leaves columns unused at the same instruction cost.
  - when: MATMUL instruction operand field showing < 128 output partitions.
  - fix: Partition-vectorize: write two 64-row outputs into partitions 0-63 and 64-127 of one PSUM tile and process them with one downstream instruction.
  - check (static): flag nc_matmul with stationary free size < 128 in hot loops.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5b  [stated, all]
- **mm-swap-operands-to-avoid-transpose** — Choose which operand is stationary based on the layout the consumer needs: output is [stationary_free, moving_free], so swapping operands yields the transposed output for free.
  - why: nc_matmul(moving, stationary) = (stationary.T @ moving).T; e.g. linear -> layernorm needs features on the free dim for bn_stats, so put the input feature map as stationary.
  - when: A PF transpose between a matmul and its consumer (bn_stats, tensor_reduce, next matmul).
  - fix: Swap stationary/moving in nisa.nc_matmul; for RMSNorm keep weight stationary and do the cross-partition sum on TensorE.
  - check (static): detect nc_transpose on a matmul output; propose operand swap.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #8 Intermediate Transpose  [stated, all]
- **mm-trn3-mx-matmul** — On Trainium3 use nisa.nc_matmul_mx with x4-packed MXFP8/MXFP4 tiles (stationary [128,128], moving [128,512] in _x4 types = K of 512) plus uint8 scale tiles for 4x BF16 throughput.
  - why: Each PE does four MX multiply-accumulates per cycle; K=512 is split as 128 partitions x 4 packed elements that were 128 apart in the original contraction axis; scales (group of 32 = 8 partitions x 4 elements) live in the same SBUF quadrant as their data, 4 partitions per quadrant.
  - when: Quantized MLP/attention projections on trn3.
  - fix: Interleave data with a strided tensor_copy or DMA, quantize with nisa.quantize_mx on VectorE (src must be SBUF; no FP4 output), call nc_matmul_mx(dst, stationary, moving, stationary_scale, moving_scale) with BF16 or FP32 PSUM dst.

- **mm-trn3-bf16-psum** — On Trainium3 write matmul results directly as BF16 into PSUM (and accumulate into BF16 PSUM) to halve eviction bytes, choosing RNE or stochastic rounding.
  - why: NeuronCore-v4 downcasts FP32 array output immediately before the PSUM write; accumulation into a BF16 PSUM tensor upcasts, adds in FP32, and rounds back.
  - when: Memory/eviction-bound matmul chains on trn3 that tolerate bf16 partial sums.
  - fix: Allocate the PSUM dst with dtype=nl.bfloat16.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: BF16 Matmul Results in PSUM  [stated, trn3]
- **mm-trn3-pe-row-tiling-small-k** — On Trainium3, matmuls with small contraction (packed K <= 64, i.e. unquantized K <= 256 for MX) can be PE row-tiled to run in parallel on TensorE.
  - why: Matmul-MX supports row-tiling only; with the 4x effective K this covers more shapes.
  - when: Many small-K MX matmuls.
  - fix: Group small-K matmuls so the hardware/compiler can row-tile them.

- **mm-structured-sparsity-trn2** — Consider M:N structured-sparse weights on Trainium2/3 for up to 4x TensorE throughput (316 TFLOPS on trn2); the NKI sparse_matmul API was not yet published in these docs.
  - why: TensorE rows can read from 4/2/1 SBUF partitions per compression ratio; supported patterns 4:16, 4:12, 4:8, 2:8, 2:4, 1:4, 1:2 with a packed uint16 tag tensor.
