  - why: Matmul-MX scaling groups are 8 partitions x 4 free; scales must sit in the quadrant their data came from; quantize_mx packs 4 elements per output element.
  - when: FP8/FP4 MX weights in decode.
  - fix: scale_sbuf: for q in range(P//32): nisa.dma_copy(src=scale.ap([[F,4],[1,F]], offset=4*q*F), dst=scale_sbuf.ap([[F,4],[1,F]], offset=32*q*F)); nisa.nc_matmul_mx(dst, stationary, moving, stationary_scale, moving_scale)
  - numbers: group = 8P x 4F; quadrant = 32
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:src/nki_samples/tutorials/mxfp-matmul/mx_kernels.py, mx_kernel_utils.py  [stated, trn3]
- **matmul-operand-shapes** — Shape nc_matmul operands as stationary [K<=128, M<=128] and moving [K<=128, N<=nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax] with the result [M, N] in PSUM.
  - why: The tensor engine contracts over the partition dimension of both operands; the stationary free dim is bounded by the PE array width (128) and the moving free dim by gemm_moving_fmax (512 on gen2/3).
  - when: nc_matmul with stationary.shape[1] > 128, moving.shape[1] > gemm_moving_fmax, or operand partition dims > 128.
  - fix: Tile M to 128, N to gemm_moving_fmax (512), K to 128 per instruction and accumulate over K tiles in PSUM.
  - numbers: stationary_free_max = 128; moving_free_max = nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax (~512); K_per_instruction = <=128 partitions; K_contraction_total = <=2048 per tile group (stated)
  - check (static): nc_matmul: assert stationary.shape==(K<=128,M<=128); moving.shape==(K,N<=gemm_moving_fmax); dst.shape==(M,N); dst.buffer==psum
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/common-patterns.md :: Matrix Multiply - CRITICAL: PSUM Accumulation Pattern (Operand dimensions); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/indexing-patterns.md :: nc_matmul Indexing  [stated, all]
- **matmul-k-contraction-limit-2048** — Keep the total contraction (K) dimension handled by one accumulation group at or below 2048 and tile K beyond that.
  - why: The documented per-tile contraction limit for nc_matmul is 2048; larger K must be split into multiple accumulation groups.
  - when: A matmul whose K dimension exceeds 2048 elements.
  - fix: Split K into chunks of <= 2048 (each itself in 128-row operand tiles) and accumulate in PSUM.
  - numbers: K_max = 2048
  - check (static): matmul lowering: assert K_total_per_group <= 2048
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/SKILL.md :: Step 2: Design Tiling Strategy; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-docs/SKILL.md :: Hardware Constraints  [stated, all]
- **psum-accumulate-flag-no-memset** — Control PSUM initialization with accumulate=(k_idx > 0) on nisa.nc_matmul and never nisa.memset the PSUM tile before the K loop.
  - why: accumulate=False makes the first matmul overwrite (initialize) the PSUM location in hardware; a memset is a wasted instruction and accumulate=True on an uninitialized location is invalid.
  - when: nisa.memset(dst=psum, ...) preceding a matmul accumulation loop, or accumulate=True on the first K tile.
  - fix: psum = nl.ndarray((M,N), nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in nl.affine_range(nk): nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, stationary=a, moving=b, accumulate=(k > 0)).
  - check (static): flag memset whose dst.buffer == psum; flag nc_matmul with accumulate=True that is the first writer of its dst
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/nki-language-constraint.md :: MatMul PSUM Accumulation — Required Pattern (NKI 0.4.0); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/common-patterns.md :: Matrix Multiply  [stated, all]
- **no-dma-between-accumulation-steps** — Never write the PSUM accumulator to HBM (or copy it out) between K-accumulation steps.
  - why: Each copy-out breaks the hardware accumulation chain and adds HBM traffic; PSUM accumulation in FP32 is nearly free.
  - when: dma_copy/tensor_copy with src=psum inside the K loop.
  - fix: Move the PSUM->SBUF tensor_copy after the K loop completes.
  - check (static): flag reads of a PSUM accumulator inside the loop that accumulates into it
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/common-patterns.md :: Anti-patterns (NEVER DO THIS)  [stated, all]
- **n-underutilization-is-cheap** — When something must be undersized, shrink N (moving free dim) rather than M or K.
  - why: The moving operand streams through the PE array, so a shorter N shortens the initiation interval proportionally; M and K underutilization leave PE rows/columns idle and cut throughput linearly.
  - when: Choosing which matmul dimension to tile smaller for an odd-shaped problem.
  - fix: Keep K=128 and M=128; let N be whatever remains (e.g. 64) if needed.
  - numbers: N_example = N=64 of 512 produced 12.5% of peak FLOPs per tile but with proportionally shorter initiation interval
  - check (profile): per MATMUL line compute K*M fraction of 128*128; rank by adjusted_flops
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/te_inefficiency.md :: Step 2: Localize  [stated, all]
- **matmul-single-tile-limits** — Keep each nc_matmul call within a 128x128 stationary tile, a 128x512 moving tile and a 128x512 PSUM output.
  - why: The TensorE instruction operates over a fixed-size array; larger operands must be tiled by the programmer.
  - when: Any nc_matmul whose stationary free dim >128, moving free dim >512 or partition dim >128.
  - fix: assert K <= nl.tile_size.pmax; assert M <= nl.tile_size.gemm_stationary_fmax; assert N <= nl.tile_size.gemm_moving_fmax before nisa.nc_matmul(dst, stationary=lhsT_tile, moving=rhs_tile).
  - numbers: pmax = 128; gemm_stationary_fmax = 128; gemm_moving_fmax = 512
  - check (static): For each nc_matmul: stationary.shape[0]<=128, stationary.shape[1]<=128, moving.shape[1]<=512.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Starting simple  [stated, all]
- **matmul-stationary-is-transposed-lhs** — Deliver the left operand already transposed as lhsT with shape [K, M] so the contraction dim K sits on the partition axis of both operands.
  - why: TensorE contracts over the partition dimension; nc_matmul computes stationary.T @ moving, so a non-transposed result needs the stationary operand stored transposed.
  - when: Writing a matmul of [M,K] @ [K,N].
  - fix: Pass lhsT=[K,M] and rhs=[K,N] tiles; result [M,N]. Transpose on the host (torch.from_numpy(lhs.T)) or with nc_transpose on device.
  - check (static): For nc_matmul(stationary, moving): stationary.shape[0]==moving.shape[0] (shared K on partition).
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Starting simple; nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Layout considerations  [stated, all]
- **arithmetic-intensity-threshold** — Raise the kernel's arithmetic intensity (FLOPs per HBM byte) above the TensorE saturation threshold before tuning anything else.
  - why: The roofline for NeuronCore-v2 bf16 saturates TensorE at 222 Flops/Byte; a naive tiled inner loop reads 160 KB per 16 MFlops (102 Flops/Byte) and is memory bound.
  - when: TensorE utilization well below 100% while DMA queues are saturated.
  - fix: Reuse loaded tiles across more matmuls (hoisting, blocking) so bytes loaded from HBM per FLOP drop.
  - numbers: saturation_AI_bf16_ncv2 = 222 Flops/Byte; naive_tiled_AI = 102 Flops/Byte; naive_bytes_per_matmul = 160 KB; flops_per_matmul = 16 MFlops
  - check (profile): Estimate AI = 2*M*N*K / (bytes of HBM traffic); flag if < 222 for bf16.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Optimization 1: Removing Redundant Loads  [stated, trn1]
- **psum-accumulate-over-k** — Accumulate the K tiles of a matmul into one PSUM tile with repeated nc_matmul calls inside an affine_range loop instead of adding partial products on VectorE.
  - why: TensorE can read-add-write every PSUM address; the first nc_matmul overwrites and subsequent ones accumulate, and associative reductions are not loop-carried dependencies.
  - when: Contraction dimension K > 128.
  - fix: psum_buf = nl.ndarray((128,512), nl.float32, buffer=nl.psum); for k in nl.affine_range(K//128): nisa.nc_matmul(psum_buf, lhsT[k], rhs[k])
  - check (static): nc_matmul into a fresh PSUM tile inside a K loop followed by tensor_tensor add -> suggest accumulation in PSUM.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/matrix_multiplication.rst :: Tiling matrix multiplications  [stated, all]
- **fold-heads-into-contraction** — Fold the heads dimension N into D for the output-projection contraction (N*D on partitions, up to 128 at a time) when beneficial.
  - why: A larger contraction tile uses the full TensorE array instead of many d-wide matmuls.
  - when: d_head < 128 (e.g. 64) with several heads.
  - fix: Treat weight as [N*D, H] and stack heads on partitions.
  - source: nki/library/api/output-projection-cte.rst :: Dimension Packing  [stated, all]
- **pe-column-tiling-for-small-t** — For matmuls with very few tokens (T < 128) split the PE array column-wise into 32/64/128-column tiles so several independent matmuls run in parallel instead of under-filling the array.
  - why: A decode matmul with T rows uses only T of 128 columns; column tiling recovers utilization.
  - when: Router logits or projections in decode.
  - fix: router_topk(..., use_column_tiling=True); mlp(use_tkg_*_column_tiling=True)
  - numbers: column_tiles = 32/64/128
  - source: nki/library/api/router-topk.rst :: PE Array Column Tiling; nki/library/api/mlp.rst  [stated, all]
- **mxfp8-physical-vs-logical-tiles** — Treat MXFP8 operands as 4-packed: a physical [128,128] LHS tile is a logical [512,128] (K=512 per tile), RHS physical [128,512] is logical [512,512]; keep K divisible by 512 and swizzle to [K/4, M*4].
  - why: float8_e4m3fn_x4 packs four K elements per partition entry.
  - when: matmul_mxfp8 / nc_matmul_mx.
  - fix: quantize_block_mxfp8_kernel(src[F,K]) -> scales [K//4, F], data [K//4, F*4]; LNC2 needs >= 2 blocks in N.
  - numbers: logical_K_per_tile = 512
  - check (static): K%512==0; F%8==0.
  - source: nki/library/api/matmul-mxfp8-generic-kernel.rst :: Notes; nki/library/api/quantize-mxfp8.rst  [stated, trn3]

## Which engine runs what (39)

- **act-runs-on-scalar-engine-fp32** — Route activation functions (exp, gelu, sigmoid, ...) through nisa.activation/activate2 on the Scalar Engine; math is always fp32 internally with free output casting.
  - why: Scalar Engine evaluates piecewise-polynomial activations with fused scale/bias and optional free-dim reduce; input is upcast to fp32 and dst cast is free.
  - when: Elementwise exp/tanh done via tensor_tensor/tensor_scalar on Vector Engine or via nl.* wrappers in a Vector-bound kernel.
  - fix: nisa.activation(dst, op=nl.exp, data, scale=s, bias=b, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=rowsum) fuses scale, bias, exp and row-sum in one instruction.
  - source: nki.isa.activation docstring  [stated, all]
- **tt-int32-defaults-to-gpsimd** — Expect tensor_tensor on all-int32/uint32 tiles to run on GpSimd (exact integer math) unless an operand is in PSUM or engine=vector is forced; nl.power always runs on GpSimd.
  - why: Vector Engine casts through fp32 and loses precision above 2^24; GpSimd has native integer ALUs but cannot touch PSUM.
  - when: Index arithmetic giving wrong results after forcing engine=vector; power op with PSUM operands failing.
  - fix: Keep int32 index math in SBUF; avoid PSUM operands for power/int32 ops.
  - numbers: fp32_exact_int_limit = 2^24
  - check (static): tensor_tensor(op==power or all int32): no operand in psum
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_tensor docstring  [stated, all]
- **ts-engine-restrictions** — In tensor_scalar use bitvec ops only on Vector Engine with integer dtypes; on trn2 the Scalar Engine only accepts (multiply,add), (multiply,None), (add,None); engine=gpsimd is only allowed for rsqrt.
  - why: Each engine implements a subset of ALU ops; both ops in one instruction must be the same class (bitvec or arithmetic).
  - when: tensor_scalar(op0=nl.maximum, engine=scalar) on trn2; bitwise_and on bf16 data.
  - fix: Leave engine=unknown, or move clamps to Vector Engine.
  - check (static): tensor_scalar: class(op0)==class(op1); bitvec -> engine in {vector,unknown} and int dtypes; engine==scalar and nc_version==3 -> (op0,op1) in {(mul,add),(mul,None),(add,None)}; engine==gpsimd -> op0==rsqrt
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_scalar docstring  [stated, all]
- **tensor-partition-reduce-on-gpsimd** — Use nisa.tensor_partition_reduce (GpSimd) for cross-partition add/average/max/bitwise_or/bitwise_and reductions when a matmul-based reduction is not suitable.
  - why: GpSimd can reduce across its 16-partition groups; Vector Engine cannot reduce axis 0.
  - when: Looping over partitions with tensor_tensor adds.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_partition_reduce(dst, nl.add, data) (SBUF only, GpSimd cannot read PSUM).
  - check (static): tensor_partition_reduce: buffers sbuf
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_partition_reduce docstring  [stated, all]
- **tensor-copy-engine-semantics** — Pick tensor_copy's engine deliberately: Scalar casts via fp32 (lossy for int32 and unsupported on trn1 - use activation(op=nl.copy) there), Vector/GpSimd are bit-accurate when dtypes match, and PSUM operands require Vector or Scalar.
  - why: Three engines implement copy with different casting behaviour and memory ports.
  - when: tensor_copy of int32 ids on Scalar Engine corrupting values > 2^24; tensor_copy(engine=scalar) on trn1.
  - fix: Use engine=vector for exact int copies; use nisa.activation(op=nl.copy) for Scalar copies on trn1.
  - check (static): tensor_copy(engine==scalar): nc_version>=3 and not (int32 dtype); any psum operand -> engine in {vector,scalar,unknown}
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_copy docstring  [stated, all]
- **em-tensore-sbuf-in-psum-out** — Feed nc_matmul only from SBUF and expect its output only in PSUM.
  - why: TensorE streams stationary/moving operands from SBUF and writes to PSUM; it cannot read PSUM or write SBUF.
  - when: nc_matmul with a PSUM operand as input or an SBUF dst.
  - fix: Evict previous PSUM results to SBUF (tensor_copy) before reusing them as matmul inputs; allocate dst with buffer=nl.psum.
  - check (static): check nc_matmul operand buffers: stationary/moving in SBUF, dst in PSUM.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine (Layout)  [stated, all]
- **em-psum-access-rights** — Use VectorE or ScalarE (tensor_copy, activation, tensor_tensor, tensor_reduce) to read PSUM; TensorE is write-only to PSUM and only TensorE can trigger PSUM accumulation.
  - why: PSUM is the TensorE landing buffer with read-accumulate-write per 4 B element controlled only by TensorE; VectorE/ScalarE see it as plain SRAM.
  - when: Trying to accumulate into PSUM from a vector op, or routing PSUM reads through GpSimd.
  - fix: Accumulate on TensorE via repeated nc_matmul into the same bank; evict with ScalarE/VectorE.
  - check (static): flag GpSimd-mapped instructions with PSUM operands; flag non-TensorE writes expecting accumulate semantics.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Near-memory accumulation in PSUM; nki/get-started/about/memory-hierarchy-overview.rst :: NeuronCore internal memory  [stated, all]
- **em-activation-functions-on-scalare** — Put non-linear functions (exp, gelu, sqrt, sigmoid, ...) on ScalarE via nisa.activation and fold the preceding multiply/add into the same instruction.
  - why: ScalarE has hardware non-linear evaluation plus a pipelined multiply-add before func; all activation instructions cost the same regardless of scale/bias use.
  - when: Separate nl.multiply / nl.add / nl.exp chain on a tile.
  - fix: exp = nisa.activation(nl.exp, data, bias=bias_tile[128,1], scale=scale_tile_or_const)  # 3x faster than 3 ops
  - numbers: speedup_vs_three_ops = 3x; speedup_vs_two_ops = 2x
  - check (static): detect tensor_scalar(mul/add) immediately feeding an activation on the same tile; suggest fusion.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Scalar Engine - Pipelined Multiply-Add / Instruction Combination; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #6  [stated, all]
- **em-scalare-single-input** — Route two-input elementwise ops (tensor_tensor) to VectorE; ScalarE can read only one input tensor per instruction.
  - why: ScalarE lanes stream one source tensor; VectorE can stream two (cost ~2N cycles vs ~N for one input).
  - when: Attempting elementwise add/mul of two tiles on ScalarE.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_tensor(dst, data1, data2, op=nl.add) (VectorE); use activation(scale=vec,bias=vec) only when the second operand is per-partition.
  - numbers: vectore_one_input_cost = ~N cycles; vectore_two_input_cost = ~2N cycles
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Scalar Engine Performance Consideration; Vector Engine Cost Model  [stated, all]
- **em-transpose-engine-choice** — Choose the PF-transpose engine by context: TensorE nc_transpose (128x128 via identity matmul, fastest) when TensorE is idle; VectorE nc_transpose for 32x32 blocks; DMA transpose when ScalarE/VectorE are the bottleneck; free-dim/free-dim transposes need only dma_copy or access patterns.
  - why: TensorE transposes occupy the highest-FLOPS engine and need PSUM eviction; VectorE reshape banks only transpose within 32 partitions; DMA transposes cost DMA bandwidth.
  - when: Any nc_transpose or layout change in the kernel.
  - fix: Pick engine= in nisa.nc_transpose, or nisa.dma_transpose, per the bottleneck engine in the profile.
  - numbers: tensore_transpose_tile = 128x128; vectore_transpose_tile = 32x32
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Alternative Use Case; Cross-partition Data Movement; nki/get-started/about/indexing-overview.rst :: Case #2; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: SBUF2SBUF DMA transpose  [stated, all]
- **em-gpsimd-role** — Reserve GpSimd for work the other engines cannot express (iota, triangular/causal masks, custom C++ ops, software DGE) and read per-instruction costs from the ISA docs; there is no cycle rule of thumb.
  - why: GpSimd is eight programmable 512-bit processors, each wired to 16 SBUF partitions (proc0 -> partitions 0-15, ...), with 64 KB TCM each on trn1; performance depends on the hand-tuned kernel per instruction.
  - when: Mask generation, index generation, or ops with no VectorE/ScalarE lowering.
  - fix: nisa.iota / nisa.affine_select style ops on GpSimd; keep GpSimd free if the kernel relies on swdge gathers.
  - numbers: processors = 8; partitions_per_processor = 16; simd_width = 512-bit; tcm_per_processor_trn1 = 64 KB
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: GpSimd Engine  [stated, all]
- **em-v2-sbuf-psum-access-exclusions** — On trn1/inf2 do not expect VectorE and GpSimd to overlap SBUF work, nor VectorE and ScalarE to overlap PSUM work; on trn2 both overlap (PSUM: only if on different banks).
  - why: NeuronCore-v2 serializes VectorE/GpSimd SBUF accesses and VectorE/ScalarE PSUM accesses (compiler-enforced). NeuronCore-v3 lifted both restrictions, with full parallel PSUM bandwidth as long as accesses do not hit the same PSUM bank.
  - when: Scheduling PSUM eviction on ScalarE while VectorE reduces PSUM, or GpSimd masks alongside VectorE on trn1.
  - fix: On trn2 place concurrent VectorE and ScalarE PSUM consumers on different banks (different 2 KiB/partition regions); on trn1 do not count on the overlap.
  - check (static): on trn2: flag concurrent VectorE+ScalarE ops reading the same PSUM bank.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Data Movement restrictions; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Data Movement Updates  [stated, all]
- **em-vectore-perf-mode-bf16** — Keep VectorE tensor_copy/tensor_scalar operands in SBUF, in BF16/FP16, with a contiguous inner-most free dim to get the 4x Trainium2 performance mode (2x if one condition fails or one side is PSUM; tensor_tensor gets 2x with both inputs SBUF BF16/FP16).
  - why: NeuronCore-v3 VectorE auto-detects these conditions and uses a wider shared memory bus (with GpSimd) for 512 BF16 elements/cycle; computation still happens in FP32.
  - when: VectorE-bound kernel using FP32 intermediates or strided inner dims.
  - fix: Store intermediates as bf16, avoid inner stride != 1 on VectorE copies, evict PSUM with ScalarE if VectorE is the bottleneck.
  - numbers: vectore_width_bf16 = 512 elements/cycle; vectore_width_other = 256 elements/cycle; vectore_freq_trn2 = 0.96 GHz
  - check (static): for VectorE ops on trn2: score 4x if all(SBUF, bf16/fp16, inner_step==1), 2x partial, 1x otherwise.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Performance Mode  [stated, trn2]
- **em-trn3-scalare-runs-tensor-scalar** — On Trainium3, load-balance tensor_scalar and tensor_copy between VectorE and ScalarE (both support the 2x BF16 mode) by setting the engine argument.
  - why: NeuronCore-v4 ScalarE natively supports those instructions at 256 BF16/FP16/FP8 elements per cycle.
  - when: One of VectorE/ScalarE is saturated on trn3.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_scalar(..., engine=nisa.engine.scalar) for part of the work.
  - numbers: scalare_width_bf16_trn3 = 256 elements/cycle
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: Scalar Engine Performance mode  [stated, trn3]
- **em-trn3-exponential-on-vectore** — On Trainium3 compute softmax exponentials with nisa.exponential on VectorE (exp(src - max) with fused row-sum) instead of activation(exp) on ScalarE.
  - why: The VectorE fast-exponential instruction runs at 4x the throughput of ScalarE activation exp and fuses the max subtraction and accumulation.
  - when: Attention softmax on trn3 bound by ScalarE exp.
  - fix: nisa.exponential(dst, src, max_value=row_max[M,1], reduce_res=row_sum[M,1])
  - numbers: speedup = 4x vs ScalarE exp
  - check (static): on trn3 flag activation(op=exp) feeding a tensor_reduce(add).
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: Fast Exponential Evaluation  [stated, trn3]
- **em-cross-partition-reduce-via-tensore** — Sum across partitions with a matmul against a ones vector on TensorE only when TensorE is otherwise idle; sum along the free dim with nisa.tensor_reduce on VectorE.
  - why: Partition-dim summation on TensorE uses a single PE column (1/128 of the array); VectorE reduces along the free dim at full lane parallelism.
  - when: Reduction direction mismatched with layout (e.g. RMSNorm sum).
  - fix: Pick the layout so the reduction axis is the free dim for VectorE, or use TensorE for the P-dim sum in norm/softmax kernels where TensorE has slack.
  - numbers: tensore_columns_used = 1 of 128
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Alternative Use Case (Cross-Partition Accumulation)  [stated, all]
- **em-partition-broadcast-via-matmul** — Know that broadcast_to across partitions lowers to a TensorE matmul with a ones stationary (is_stationary_onezero=True) and costs TensorE time plus PSUM eviction.
  - why: Broadcasting a single-partition vector to M partitions is implemented as ones[1,M].T @ v on the systolic array.
  - when: Frequent per-tile broadcasts in a matmul-bound kernel.
  - fix: Pre-broadcast once and keep the result in SBUF, or restructure so the per-partition operand is used as activation scale/bias.
  - check (static): count broadcast_to calls inside hot loops.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Alternative Use Case (Partition Broadcast)  [stated, all]
- **em-stream-shuffle-32** — For arbitrary partition permutations or broadcasts within a 32-partition group, use nisa.nc_stream_shuffle on VectorE rather than a TensorE matmul.
  - why: Each VectorE Reshape Bank serves 32 partitions and accepts a 32-entry shuffle mask SM[i] = source partition (mod 32); e.g. 32 zeros broadcasts partition 0.
  - when: Partition shuffles confined to quadrants.
  - fix: nisa.nc_stream_shuffle(dst, src, shuffle_mask=[...32 ints...])
  - numbers: group_size = 32 partitions
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Cross-partition Data Movement  [stated, all]
- **em-engine-clock-table** — Convert engine cycle costs to time with the per-generation clocks: trn2 TensorE 2.4 GHz, VectorE 0.96 GHz, ScalarE 1.2 GHz, GpSimd 1.2 GHz (trn1: 2.8/1.12/1.4/1.4; trn3: 2.4/1.2/1.2/1.2).
  - why: Each engine has its own sequencer and clock; ScalarE/VectorE process 128 elements per cycle (one per partition lane), TensorE 2x128 inputs per cycle (4x128 for fp8 on trn2, 8x128 MXFP8 on trn3).
  - when: Any cycle-based cost estimate.
  - fix: time = cycles / f_engine.

## Scheduling, multi-buffering, pipelining (37)

- **loops-range-aliases-fully-unrolled** — Treat nl.affine_range, nl.sequential_range, nl.static_range and nl.range as deprecated aliases of Python range(): every static loop is fully unrolled; write plain range().
  - why: In NKI 0.6.0 there is no distinction between affine/sequential/static loops; the compiler unrolls and schedules the straight-line program.
  - when: Kernels relying on affine_range for 'parallel' semantics or sequential_range to 'force dependencies'.
  - fix: Use range(); express ordering with nl.no_reorder() or Kernel.with_schedule edges; keep trip counts bounded (unrolled code size).
  - check (static): call to nl.affine_range/sequential_range/static_range/nl.range
  - source: nki.language.affine_range/sequential_range/static_range/range docstrings (deprecation warnings)  [stated, all]
- **loops-unroll-code-size** — Keep statically unrolled trip counts modest (product of nested static ranges in the hundreds, not tens of thousands) or move the outer loop to nl.fori_loop.
  - why: All range loops are fully unrolled into straight-line instructions, so instruction count and compile time grow linearly with total iterations.
  - when: Compile times of minutes or instruction-stream limits on large sequence/batch loops.
  - fix: Restructure to fewer, larger tiles; use fori_loop for large outer counts with register offsets.
  - check (static): product of static loop bounds > ~10k nc_matmul-equivalent instructions
  - source: inferred from affine_range docstring ('fully unrolled loop')  [inferred, all]
- **no-reorder-region** — Wrap instruction sequences that must execute in program order in 'with nl.no_reorder():' (static loops allowed inside, register loops not).
  - why: The scheduler otherwise freely reorders independent instructions for engine utilization.
  - when: Accumulator-register chains or barrier/DMA ordering being reordered.
  - fix: with nl.no_reorder(): activation(reset_reduce); activation(reduce); ...
  - check (static): no_reorder block containing fori_loop/while_loop
  - source: nki.language.no_reorder docstring  [stated, all]
- **schedule-edges-and-depends-on** — Add explicit scheduling dependencies with instruction name= tags and Kernel.with_schedule([(from_name, to_name_or_list), ...]) or instr.depends_on(other); the second tuple element must be a str or list, not a tuple.
  - why: with_schedule attaches dependency edges the scheduler must respect; names come from the name= kwarg on nisa calls.
  - when: Needing to delay a DMA until compute finishes without a data dependency.
  - fix: k = nki.jit(fn).with_schedule([('store_out', ['mm_last'])]); nisa.dma_copy(..., name='store_out').
  - check (static): with_schedule edge second element is tuple
  - source: nki.Kernel.with_schedule docstring; nki.isa.NkiInstruction docstring  [stated, all]
- **hoist-tensor-decl-inside-loop** — Declare per-iteration SBUF tiles inside the loop body (not once outside) so the compiler can multi-buffer them; reuse one outer tensor only when iterations must serialize.
  - why: A single tensor reused across iterations carries a loop dependency that serializes load/compute/store; a fresh declaration per iteration lets unrolled copies overlap.
  - when: Load->compute->store pipelines running serially in the profile.
  - fix: for i in range(n): buf = nl.ndarray((128,512), ...); dma_copy(buf,...); ...
  - check (static): sbuf tensor declared before a loop and both written and read in every iteration
  - source: migration/index.rst 'If blocks do not need to be alive at the same time' (warning)  [stated, all]
- **sched-pipeline-engines-with-tiles** — Slice multi-engine operator chains into tiles so ScalarE, VectorE, TensorE and GpSimd process different tiles concurrently (e.g. attention: matmuls on TensorE, exp on ScalarE, sum on VectorE, rescale on ScalarE, causal mask on GpSimd).
  - why: Without tiling, each engine waits for the previous engine to finish the whole tensor; with tiling the first tile unblocks the next engine early.
  - when: Idle-gap first instruction waits on a semaphore named after another engine (e.g. S[4] (Scalar) == 6).
  - fix: Restructure loops so each iteration emits a tile's worth of work for every engine.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #3  [stated, all]
- **sched-overlap-dma-with-compute** — Issue loads for tile i+1 (or block i+1) before computing tile i so DMA runs in parallel with compute.
  - why: DMA engines are asynchronous; the compiler overlaps independent loads if dependencies and SBUF space allow. Idle gaps whose wait is on a q* semaphore (qSyncIO0) mean compute is blocked on loads.
  - when: EVENT_SEMAPHORE waiting on S[32] (qSyncIO0) before compute instructions.
  - fix: Allocate double buffers for input tiles and hoist the next load above the current compute in program order.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #4  [stated, all]
- **sched-dependent-chains-overhead** — Avoid long chains where every instruction consumes the previous instruction's output tile with tiny free sizes; add ~100 engine cycles per instruction in that regime.
  - why: A RAW dependency forces the next instruction to wait until the previous output is fully committed to SRAM, exposing static overhead instead of pipelining.
  - when: src address of inst_i equals dst of inst_{i-1} across many consecutive instructions.
  - fix: Batch independent rows into one instruction, or use scan/fused instructions.
  - numbers: overhead = ~100 cycles per instruction
  - check (static): detect chains of length > 8 with free size < 128 where each op reads the previous op's dst.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Vector Engine Cost Model; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a  [stated, all]
- **sched-combine-instructions** — Combine multiply + add + nonlinearity (activation), activation + free-dim sum (activation_reduce), and scans (tensor_tensor_scan) into single ISA instructions on VectorE/ScalarE-bound kernels.
  - why: Deep engine pipelines perform the extra ops at no additional cost; ActReadAccumulator costs only ~64 ScalarE cycles to dump the reduction.
  - when: Profile where VectorE or ScalarE is busy at all times while TensorE idles (self-attention inner loop).
  - fix: nisa.activation_reduce(op=nl.exp, data, bias, scale, reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_res=row_sum)
  - numbers: act_read_accumulator = ~64 ScalarE cycles
  - check (static): pattern-match activation followed by tensor_reduce(add) over the same tile.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Pipelined Reduction; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #6  [stated, all]
- **sched-dynamic-range-for-large-or-unknown-trip** — Use nl.dynamic_range for trip counts unknown at compile time or large enough that unrolling bloats compile time/code size; keep range() for everything else.
  - why: range()/static_range/affine_range/sequential_range fully unroll at specialization; dynamic_range emits one hardware loop instruction whose step must be a compile-time positive int and whose loop variable is a device register (cannot be used in host-side if).
  - when: Compile time explodes or code size scales with sequence length.
  - fix: for i in nl.dynamic_range(start_reg, stop_reg, 128): ... using .ap(scalar_offset=i) for addressing.
  - check (static): flag unrolled loops with trip count > ~256 containing DMAs.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dynamic-loops.rst :: Comparison with Other Range Iterators; When to Use dynamic_range  [stated, all]
- **sched-cross-engine-sync-granularity** — Make each pipeline stage's tile large enough that its compute exceeds the ~1.3 us cross-engine semaphore round trip; do not synchronize engines per tiny tile.
  - why: Semaphore-to-start latency is about 1300 ns cross-engine, so fine-grained handoffs leave engines waiting more than working.
  - when: Many short instructions separated by semaphore waits in the trace.
  - fix: Coarsen tiles (e.g. 128 x 512+ elements per stage) so each stage runs >= several microseconds.
  - numbers: cross_engine_semaphore_latency = ~1300 ns
  - check (simulator): per stage: compute_time vs 1300 ns; flag stages shorter than ~2x.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dma-bandwidth-guide.rst :: Why Large Contiguous DMA Payloads Are Required  [inferred, all]
- **sched-background-load-stationary** — Order TensorE work so the next LoadStationary overlaps the current MultiplyMoving; whichever of LS or MM reads the longer tensor bounds throughput.
  - why: TensorE supports background LoadStationary; with stationary 128x128 and moving 128x512 the engine is MM-bound (case a), the desired regime.
  - when: TensorE utilization limited by LS (short moving tensors).
  - fix: Reuse one stationary across several moving tiles; prefer long moving free dims.
  - check (simulator): tensore_time = sum(max(LS_cost, MM_cost)) per pair.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Background LoadStationary  [stated, all]
- **sched-mx-quantize-rate** — On trn3 expect Quantize-MX (VectorE) to consume matmul output at half the rate TensorE produces it; rely on tiled reuse of quantized tiles rather than back-to-back matmul -> quantize -> matmul on small tensors.
  - why: TensorE runs at double the VectorE clock; back-pressure only appears for small tensors where no reuse hides the quantization.
  - when: Small-tensor MX chains stalling TensorE.
  - fix: Increase tile reuse or interleave independent matmuls.
  - numbers: tensore_vs_vectore_clock = 2x
  - source: nki/deep-dives/mxfp-matmul.rst :: Additional Tips  [stated, trn3]
- **sched-sequential-program-order** — Write kernels in natural sequential order and let the compiler reorder independent operations; the NKI compiler preserves your explicit allocation and scheduling choices.
  - why: NKI is a sequential programming model; independent ops are reordered for performance, dependent ones are synchronized across engines automatically.
  - when: Over-constraining with no_reorder or manual semaphores.
  - fix: Use nl.no_reorder only to pin a critical pipeline order.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Core Programming Model; nki/deep-dives/nki-compiler.rst :: Overview  [stated, all]
- **weight-ring-offset-avoid-anti-dependency** — When a second projection (up, then down) reuses the gate weight ring buffer, start its tile index at (num_required_tiles % num_allocated) so it writes the slot least recently read.
  - why: Writing into the slot the previous projection just read creates a WAR anti-dependency that serializes the DMA behind the matmul; offsetting lets the next weights stream in early.
  - when: Two phases share SBUF weight buffers.

- **loop-type-selection** — Pick loop constructs by dependency: nl.affine_range for independent iterations (full unroll, schedulable), nl.sequential_range only for true loop-carried dependencies, nl.static_range for small constant loops, nl.fori_loop/nl.while_loop for runtime or data-dependent bounds.

  - when: sequential_range used where iterations are independent; dynamic_range or bare while reg: used for runtime loops.

## LNC=2 sharding across the two physical cores (25)

- **lnc-launch-bracket-matches-runtime** — Launch LNC2 kernels as kernel[2](args) and keep that degree equal to NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG; default is LNC=1.
  - why: The bracket syntax sets the kernel's logical core count; a mismatch with the runtime configuration is a runtime error.
  - when: kernel(args) under NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2.
  - fix: Use kernel[lnc](...) and nki.simulate(kernel[2]) for simulation.
  - numbers: lnc_values = 1 or 2
  - check (static): Kernel.lnc != env NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG
  - source: nki.jit docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-program-id-sharding** — Shard work across the two physical cores with nl.program_id(0)/nl.num_programs(0), launching with an SPMD grid equal to the LNC degree; expect future releases to specialize across PNCs automatically and reject mismatched grids.
  - why: Under LNC2 each physical NeuronCore runs the same program with a different program_id.
  - when: SPMD grid size differing from the LNC degree.
  - fix: core = nl.program_id(0); process rows [core*half:(core+1)*half].
  - check (static): SPMD grid dims == lnc
  - source: nki.language.program_id/num_programs docstrings; migration/index.rst 'Deprecation notice: SPMD launch grid'  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-core-barrier-before-cross-core-read** — Insert nisa.core_barrier(data=shared_tensor, cores=(0,1)) after each core writes its part of a shared HBM tensor and before any core reads the other's part (trn2+, LNC2 only).
  - why: Cores run asynchronously; the barrier exchanges semaphores so reads see completed writes. Only cores=(0,1) and shared-HBM data are supported; it blocks only the chosen engine (default GpSimd).
  - when: Stale/zero halves of a shared tensor read by the peer core.
  - fix: dma_copy(shared[half], ...); core_barrier(shared, (0,1)); then read.
  - check (static): LNC2 kernel: shared_hbm tensor written by one program_id and read by another without core_barrier between
  - source: nki.isa.core_barrier docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-sendrecv-rules** — Use nisa.sendrecv only between ranks 0 and 1 with SBUF src/dst of identical dtype/shape; with dma_engine.gpsimd_dma keep per-partition payload <= 1024 B (32-bit), 512 B (16-bit), 256 B (8-bit); group operations with pipe_id.
  - why: sendrecv swaps SBUF tiles between the two cores sharing an HBM stack; the GpSimd DMA path is low latency but size limited.
  - when: sendrecv of a (128, 1024) bf16 tile over gpsimd_dma (2048 B/partition).
  - fix: Split into chunks or use dma_engine.dma.
  - numbers: gpsimd_dma_max_32bit = 1024 B/partition; gpsimd_dma_max_16bit = 512 B/partition; gpsimd_dma_max_8bit = 256 B/partition
  - check (static): sendrecv: buffers sbuf; same dtype/shape; ranks in {0,1}; gpsimd_dma -> bytes_per_partition <= 1024/512/256 by itemsize
  - source: nki.isa.sendrecv docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-shared-constant-identical** — Keep nl.shared_constant data identical for both cores under LNC2 and use only the supported element types (fp32/fp16/bf16/int*/uint*/fp8_e4m3fn/fp8_e5m2/e8m0fnu).
  - why: Constants are embedded in the NEFF and loaded once to shared HBM.
  - when: Per-core constant tables; packed/tfloat32 constants (untested on hardware).
  - fix: Index into one shared table with program_id.
  - check (static): shared_constant dtype in supported set
  - source: nki.language.shared_constant docstring  [stated, all]
- **lnc-launch-two-cores** — Launch on both physical cores of a Trainium2/3 logical core with kernel[2](...) and split work by nl.program_id(0) in {0,1}; nl.num_programs() reports the count.
  - why: An LNC can contain up to two physical NeuronCores sharing HBM; each receives its own program_id.
  - when: Any kernel whose work divides into two independent halves.
  - fix: i = nl.program_id(0); process input[i]; kernel[8] errors on current hardware.
  - numbers: max_cores_per_lnc = 2
  - check (static): check kernel is launched with [2] when num_programs branches exist.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/lnc.rst :: Launching a kernel on multiple cores; nki/nki_faq.rst  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-io-in-shared-hbm** — Allocate LNC kernel inputs/outputs in nl.shared_hbm so both cores can address them.
  - why: The two physical cores of an LNC share one HBM address space; private buffers are not visible across cores.
  - when: Output allocated with buffer=nl.hbm in an LNC=2 kernel.
  - fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm)
  - check (static): flag kernel outputs not in shared_hbm when launched with [2].

- **lnc-hbm-bandwidth-needs-both-cores** — For memory-bound (decode) kernels under LNC=2, split the HBM streaming across both physical cores so both sets of 16 DMA engines pull from the shared HBM bank.
  - why: Trainium2 has 4 HBM banks of 24 GB, each shared by two physical cores; chip HBM bandwidth 2.9-3 TB/s over 8 cores is ~360-375 GB/s per core, matching one core's 16-engine DMA peak of 368 GB/s. A single core therefore cannot use the bank's full bandwidth; two cores can approach ~2x.
  - when: LNC=2 kernel where program_id 1 does little while program_id 0 streams weights.
  - fix: Shard weight rows/heads by program_id so each core DMAs half the bytes; each core still needs >= 4 KiB/partition transfers.
  - numbers: hbm_banks_trn2 = 4 x 24 GB; cores_per_bank = 2; chip_hbm_bw = 2.9 TB/s (hardware page) / 3 TB/s (NKI guide); per_core_dma_peak = 368 GB/s; per_core_hbm_share = ~0.36 TB/s
  - check (static): in [2]-launched kernels compare DMA bytes issued under each program_id branch.
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/logical-neuroncore-config.rst :: LNC = 2; nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: device overview; nki/deep-dives/nki-dma-bandwidth-guide.rst :: bandwidth table  [inferred, trn2]
- **lnc-h-shard-partial-sum-sendrecv** — Under LNC=2 shard gate/up/down weights along H (each core computes a partial contraction), then exchange fp32 partials with nisa.sendrecv and add; apply bias on shard 0 only.
  - why: Each core only reads half the weights (the bandwidth bottleneck); the exchange of a [T, I] fp32 tile is cheap relative to the weights saved. Adding bias on both cores would double-count it.
  - when: LNC=2 decode projections.
  - fix: nisa.sendrecv(src=gate_up_fp32, dst=recv, send_to_rank=1-shard_id, recv_from_rank=1-shard_id, pipe_id=0); nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=gate_up_fp32, data1=gate_up_fp32, data2=recv, op=nl.add); is_bias = bias is not None and shard_id == 0
  - check (static): bias add present on all shards when H-sharded
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/mlp/mlp_tkg/mlp_tkg_gate_up_projection.py _post_process_gate_up, gate_up_projection  [stated, all]
- **rmsnorm-lnc-sharding-threshold** — Shard RMSNorm on H across LNC cores (exchanging the [T,1] sum-of-squares via sendrecv) only when T >= 18 and H1 % lnc == 0; for smaller T each core redundantly normalizes the full row.
  - why: Below ~18 tokens the sendrecv round-trip costs more than the halved compute; the threshold was tuned empirically.
  - when: Decode RMSNorm under LNC=2.
  - fix: shard_on_h = (H1 % lnc == 0) and (18 <= T)
  - numbers: SHARDING_THRESHOLD = 18
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/mlp/mlp_tkg/mlp_tkg_rmsnorm.py SHARDING_THRESHOLD  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-attention-batch-vs-sprior-sharding** — Under LNC=2 shard attention on batch when bs % 2 == 0 and (bs*q_head*s_active >= 128 or curr_sprior <= 256); otherwise shard s_prior (requires curr_sprior >= 256) and merge partial softmax stats via sendrecv.
  - why: Batch sharding keeps both cores running identical code with one partition tile each; s_prior sharding is needed for batch=1 long context and costs a cross-core max/sum exchange and output add.
  - when: Decode attention with batch=1 -> s_prior sharded.
  - fix: batch_sharded = bs%2==0 and (bs*q_head*s_active >= 128 or curr_sprior <= 2*128); sprior_sharded = not batch_sharded and curr_sprior >= 2*128
  - numbers: p_max = 128
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/attention/attention_tkg_utils.py is_batch_sharded / is_s_prior_sharded  [stated, trn2]
- **lnc-interleave-fa-tiles-across-cores** — When s_prior is sharded for block KV, assign flash-attention tiles to cores alternately (NC0 even tiles, NC1 odd) instead of contiguous halves.
  - why: With DMA skipping of inactive blocks a partially filled cache would leave one core idle; interleaving balances work.
  - when: Block KV + LNC2 s_prior sharding.
  - fix: nc_start_offset = prg_id * tile_size; tile stride = 2 * tile_size

- **core-barrier-after-shared-hbm-write** — Insert nisa.core_barrier(tensor, cores=[0,1]) after each core writes its shard of a shared HBM tensor that the other core will read next.
  - why: Without the barrier the consumer core can read stale HBM data.
  - when: LNC=2 dma_compute into shared_hbm followed by normalisation.

- **kv-cache-update-core-split** — Under LNC=2 split the KV-cache scatter by token range when BxS % 2 == 0 (both cores run identical K+V code), else put all V on core 0 and all K on core 1.
  - why: Symmetric op streams keep the cores in lockstep; the asymmetric fallback still halves the DMA count per core.
  - when: Decode KV cache write.
  - fix: batch_sharded = n_prgs > 1 and BxS % n_prgs == 0; do_v = batch_sharded or prg_id==0; do_k = batch_sharded or prg_id==1

- **supported-lnc-per-generation** — Choose --lnc from the supported set for the target: trn1 {1}, inf2 {1,2}, trn2 {1,2,4}, trn3 {1,2,4,8}.
  - why: neuronx-cc rejects unsupported logical NeuronCore groupings with NCC_EARG001.
  - when: NEURON_CC_FLAGS --lnc value not in the target's set.

- **lnc2-spmd-grid-must-equal-lnc-degree** — When launching an LNC2 kernel with an SPMD grid, make the grid dimension equal the LNC degree; a kernel is always specialized across all physical NeuronCores in the LNC.
  - why: The SPMD grid requirement is being deprecated; a mismatched SPMD dimension will become a compile-time error, while matching grids keep working.

- **simulator-lnc2-threads** — Simulate LNC2 kernels by launching kernel[2]; the simulator runs two Python threads with distinct program_id over shared_hbm inputs and thread-safe sendrecv/core_barrier.
  - why: Inputs are wrapped as shared_hbm so both threads see the same memory.

- **lnc-same-control-flow-per-core** — Keep dynamic control flow identical on every core of an LNC launch; divergent dynamic branches are undefined behavior and usually a runtime error.
  - why: The SDK assumes the program on each core is the same.
  - when: Using program_id to drive dynamic while/dynamic_range bounds differently per core.
  - fix: Divide data by program_id but keep loop structures identical.

- **lnc-program-id-work-split** — Branch on nl.num_programs() and use nl.program_id(0) to pick each core's slice so the same kernel works for LNC=1 and LNC=2.
  - why: num_programs returns 1 without LNC; program_id returns 0/1 under LNC2.

- **transposed-io-layout-for-per-core-contiguous-dma** — Use the transposed HBM layout [H0, n_prgs, H1_shard, BxS] for TKG inputs/outputs so each NeuronCore DMAs its H shard contiguously without a transpose_store.
  - why: Sharding H across cores with this layout removes cross-core data movement and strided stores.

- **attention-tkg-lnc2-sharding-rule** — For LNC2 decode attention shard on batch when batch is even AND (s_prior < 256 OR b*q_head*s_active > 128); otherwise shard the prior sequence (requires s_prior >= 256).
  - why: Batch sharding needs no cross-core reduction; sequence sharding splits the KV cache and merges softmax partials via GPSIMD SBUF-to-SBUF transfers.
  - when: attention_tkg under kernel[2].
  - fix: Set bs/q_head/s_active/curr_sprior in AttnTKGConfig; keep use_gpsimd_sb2sb=True.

  - check (static): if bs%2==0 and (s_prior<256 or bs*q_head*s_active>128): batch-shard else seq-shard.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-tkg.rst :: Adaptive LNC2 Sharding  [stated, all]
- **attention-cte-lnc2-sharding** — Shard prefill attention across two cores primarily on batch, falling back to sequence sharding for odd batch sizes.
  - why: Batch sharding avoids cross-core reductions; sequence sharding balances odd batches.
  - when: attention_cte under kernel[2].
  - fix: Launch with a 1-D SPMD grid for LNC2.
  - source: nki/library/api/attention-cte.rst :: LNC2 Sharding  [stated, all]
- **moe-cte-sharding-choice** — Shard MoE prefill on blocks (shard_on_block, PING_PONG/HI_LO) when there are many blocks; shard the intermediate dimension (shard_on_i) otherwise, accepting an all-reduce to combine partials; use the _mx variants on trn3.
  - why: Block sharding has no cross-core reduction but needs enough blocks to balance; I-sharding always balances but reduces.
  - when: LNC2 MoE CTE.
  - fix: MoECTESpec(implementation=MoECTEImplementation.shard_on_block)  # or shard_on_i / shard_on_i_hybrid
  - source: nki/library/api/moe-cte.rst :: MoECTESpec  [stated, all]
- **non-overlapping-shards-skip-reduce** — When token routing guarantees shards never touch the same output rows (e.g. HI_LO with sequence sharding), set non_overlapping_shards=True to skip zero-init and the cross-shard reduce.
  - why: The accumulation output [T,2,H+E] and its FMA reduce exist only to merge overlapping shard writes.
  - when: Blockwise MoE with disjoint token sets per core.
  - fix: bwmm_shard_on_block(..., block_sharding_strategy=HI_LO, non_overlapping_shards=True)
  - source: nki/library/api/bwmm-shard-on-block-v2.rst :: non_overlapping_shards  [stated, all]
- **duplicate-compute-shard-store** — For tiny decode kernels (T <= 128) let both cores compute identical results and shard only the HBM store across cores for bandwidth.
  - why: Compute is negligible; splitting the store halves per-core write traffic without any inter-core exchange.
  - when: Fused RMSNorm + router for MoE token generation.
  - fix: rmsnorm_router_topk_a2av: both NCs compute, store sharded.
  - source: nki/library/api/rmsnorm-router-topk-a2av.rst :: Notes  [stated, all]

## Collectives (19)

- **coll-uniform-memory-space** — Give each collective tensors all in HBM or all in SBUF; coalesced (multi-tensor) collectives require HBM.
  - why: The collective engines treat HBM and SBUF transfers differently and cannot mix them in one op.
  - when: all_reduce(srcs=[hbm_t, sbuf_t], ...).
  - fix: Stage to one memory space; pass a single tensor for SBUF collectives.
  - check (static): collective: all buffers equal; len(srcs)>1 -> buffers hbm
  - source: nki.collectives.all_reduce/all_gather/reduce_scatter docstrings  [stated, all]
- **coll-collective-dim-zero** — Use collective_dim=0 for HBM all_gather/reduce_scatter/all_to_all; for SBUF all_gather 0 or 1 is allowed but only on 2-D tensors with a single free dim.
  - why: Concatenation/splitting is implemented along the leading dim; SBUF collectives are 2-D only.
  - when: all_gather on a 3-D SBUF tile or collective_dim=1 on HBM.
  - fix: Reshape to put the gathered dim first.
  - check (static): collective_dim==0 unless (buffer==sbuf and ndim==2)
  - source: nki.collectives.all_gather/reduce_scatter/all_to_all docstrings  [stated, all]
- **coll-hbm-only-ops** — Keep all_to_all, all_to_all_v, all_gather_v and collective_permute tensors in HBM; collective_permute takes exactly one tensor per list.
  - why: SBUF variants are not implemented for these ops.
  - when: collective_permute(srcs=[sbuf_tile], ...).
  - fix: dma_copy to an HBM staging tensor first.
  - check (static): op in {all_to_all, all_to_all_v, all_gather_v, collective_permute}: buffers hbm; collective_permute len(srcs)==1
  - source: nki.collectives docstrings  [stated, all]
- **coll-reduce-ops-limited** — Use only nl.add, nl.minimum or nl.maximum as the reduction op for all_reduce/reduce_scatter/collective_permute_implicit_reduce.
  - why: Collective reduction hardware supports sum/min/max only.
  - when: op=nl.multiply in all_reduce.
  - fix: Reduce locally with log/exp tricks or do products on-core.
  - check (static): collective op in {add, minimum, maximum}
  - source: nki.collectives.all_reduce docstring  [stated, all]
- **coll-all-to-all-v-metadata** — For all_to_all_v/all_gather_v supply a uint32 metadata tensor shaped (rows, group_size) in HBM or (1, rows, group_size) in SBUF on one partition, rows=3 without rdispls or 4 with; row 2 (recv_counts) is written by the op unless recv_counts_known=True.
  - why: Per-rank counts/displacements are read at execution time from the metadata rows.
  - when: int32 metadata, or reading recv counts before the op completes.
  - fix: meta = nl.ndarray((3, G), nl.uint32, buffer=nl.shared_hbm) with rows send_counts/send_displs/recv_counts.
  - check (static): metadata.dtype==uint32 and shape matches rows x group_size
  - source: nki.collectives.all_to_all_v and all_gather_v docstrings  [stated, all]
- **coll-variable-length-restrictions** — Expect all_gather_v to require LNC=2 with 4-rank intra-chip subgroups and no rdispls, and all_to_all_v on NeuronSwitch instances to require LNC=2, >1 device, and rank lists that include all 4 ranks of each participating device (set send_count=0 to exclude).
  - why: Current runtime support for variable-length collectives is limited to these topologies.
  - when: all_to_all_v under LNC=1 or with partial-device rank lists.
  - fix: Restructure replica groups as sequential 4-rank lists per device.
  - check (static): all_gather_v: lnc==2 and len(rank_list)==4 and not has_rdispls
  - source: nki.collectives.all_gather_v and all_to_all_v docstrings 'Current restrictions'  [stated, trn3]
- **coll-channels-limits** — Use at most 4 channels for replica groups covering all devices in a node and 2 otherwise; channel_ids must be consecutive integers starting at 0.
  - why: Channel count is bounded by system connectivity; each channel carries one tensor per list.
  - when: channel_ids=[1,2] or 6 channels.
  - fix: channel_ids=list(range(n)) with n<=4.
  - numbers: max_channels_full_node = 4; max_channels_other = 2
  - check (static): channel_ids == list(range(len(channel_ids))) and len<=4
  - source: nki.collectives.collective_permute_implicit docstring  [stated, all]
- **coll-replica-groups-disjoint** — Define ReplicaGroup sub-groups as non-overlapping rank lists.
  - why: Overlapping groups make collective membership ambiguous.
  - when: Rank appearing in two sub-lists.
  - fix: Partition ranks exactly once.
  - check (static): ReplicaGroup lists pairwise disjoint
  - source: nki.collectives.ReplicaGroup docstring  [stated, all]
- **lnc-local-collectives** — Exchange data between the two cores of an LNC through shared HBM / local collectives instead of the NeuronLink network.
  - why: Under LNC=2 the cores share an address space and can perform local collective operations without network traffic.
  - when: Reductions across the two halves of an LNC-sharded kernel.
  - fix: Write partials to shared_hbm, nisa.core_barrier(data, cores), then reduce.
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/logical-neuroncore-config.rst :: LNC = 2; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control  [stated, trn2]
- **cc-engines-overlap-compute** — Overlap collectives with compute: dedicated CC-Cores and NeuronLink handle AllReduce/ReduceScatter/AllGather/All2all while engines keep computing.
  - why: Trainium2 has 16-20 CC-Cores (docs disagree: 20 in the NKI guide, 16 on the hardware page) and 4 NeuronLink-v3 at 1.28 TB/s per chip (1024 GB/s intra-instance, 256 GB/s inter-instance in an UltraServer).
  - when: Tensor-parallel decode where all-reduce latency is exposed.
  - fix: Issue the collective (nisa.sendrecv / core_barrier or framework CC) early and keep independent compute after it.
  - numbers: trn2_cc_cores = 16-20; neuronlink_v3_per_chip = 1.28 TB/s; intra_instance_per_chip = 1024 GB/s; inter_instance_per_chip = 256 GB/s; trn1_cc_cores = 6; trn1_neuronlink_v2 = 384 GB/s per chip
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: device overview; about-neuron/arch/neuron-hardware/trainium2.rst :: Trainium2 chip components; about-neuron/arch/neuron-hardware/trn2-arch.rst  [stated, trn2]
- **cc-trn3-all-to-all-fabric** — On Trainium3 UltraServers design MoE/all-to-all style communication around the switched all-to-all fabric: 256 GB/s intra-server, 320 GB/s inter-server, 128 GB/s inter-rack per chip.
  - why: NeuronSwitch-v1 PCIe Gen6 fabric replaces the 2D torus; routing is address-based and transparent, with semaphore writes following the data path.
  - when: Expert-parallel dispatch on trn3.
  - fix: Keep per-chip all-to-all volume within these link budgets; prefer intra-server placement for the heaviest pairs.
  - numbers: intra_server = 256 GB/s; inter_server = 320 GB/s; inter_rack = 128 GB/s; neuronlink_v4_per_chip = 2.56 TB/s
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-hardware/trn3-arch.rst :: Bandwidth summary  [stated, trn3]
- **cc-nki-primitives** — Use nisa.core_barrier(data, cores) and nisa.sendrecv(src, dst, send_to_rank, recv_from_rank, pipe_id) for intra-kernel multi-core coordination.
  - why: NKI exposes collective primitives so kernels can synchronize and exchange data across NeuronCores without leaving the kernel.
  - when: Multi-core NKI kernels needing a barrier or point-to-point exchange.
  - fix: Call core_barrier before reading another core's shared_hbm output.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control with nki.isa  [stated, trn2]
- **fuse-gate-up-into-one-sendrecv** — Allocate gate and up fp32 outputs contiguously ([T, 2*I]) so a single sendrecv exchanges both partials.
  - why: One larger DMA has lower fixed overhead than two and halves the cross-core synchronisation points.
  - when: LNC>1 and both gate and up are computed.
  - fix: gate_up_sb_fp32 = sbm.alloc_stack((T, 2*I), fp32); gate_view = [:, :I]; up_view = [:, I:]; one nisa.sendrecv on the whole buffer
  - check (static): two consecutive sendrecv on adjacent buffers
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/mlp/mlp_tkg/mlp_tkg_gate_up_projection.py run_gate_up_projection_non_lhs_rhs_swap (use_fused_gate_up_sendrecv)  [stated, all]
- **gpsimd-sb2sb-sendrecv-small-transfers** — Use dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma for LNC sendrecv when the per-partition free size is <= 256 elements (<=1024 bytes); otherwise use the regular DMA.
  - why: gpsimd_dma routes SBUF-to-SBUF without bouncing through HBM, eliminating PSEUDO_CORE_BARRIER stalls, but has a 256-element/partition hardware limit.
  - when: Exchanging rmsnorm partial sums, softmax max/sum stats, small partials.
  - fix: if free_elems <= 256: nisa.sendrecv(..., dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma) else nisa.sendrecv(...)
  - numbers: gpsimd limit = 256 elems/partition (1024 B)
  - check (static): sendrecv with small src and no dma_engine
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/utils/lnc_sendrecv.py; attention_tkg.py line ~1654; mlp_tkg_rmsnorm.py  [stated, trn2]
- **ping-pong-ring-buffers-and-cpi-first** — In a ring all-gather+matmul, keep two private-HBM ping-pong buffers, issue collective_permute_implicit for the next step before the local matmul, and skip the final CPI.
  - why: Matmul and CPI both only read buf_cur, and CPI writes buf_next, so they run on disjoint engines; issuing CPI first hints the scheduler to overlap. Collectives cannot source IO tensors, so seed with dma_copy.
  - when: Tensor-parallel decode projections with ring overlap.
  - fix: nisa.dma_copy(buf0, input_shard); for step: if step < N-1: ncc.collective_permute_implicit(srcs_by_channel=[[buf_cur]], dsts_by_channel=[[buf_next]], replica_group=rg); matmul(buf_cur)
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:src/nki_samples/tutorials/allgather_matmul_ring/allgather_matmul_ring_nki_kernels.py  [stated, trn2]
- **collective-api-forms** — In collectives use channel_ids=[0, 1, ...] (not num_channels=N) for collective_permute_implicit, and dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma (not use_gpsimd_dma=True) for sendrecv.
  - why: The Beta-2 keyword forms were removed in NKI 0.3.0 and fail to compile.
  - when: num_channels= or use_gpsimd_dma= in collective calls.
  - fix: nisa.collective_permute_implicit(..., channel_ids=[0,1]); nisa.sendrecv(..., dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.gpsimd_dma).
  - check (static): flag kwargs num_channels, use_gpsimd_dma
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/nki-language-constraint.md :: Hard Rules — Beta 2 → NKI 0.3.0  [stated, all]
- **fused-cc-overlap-with-compute** — Overlap collectives with compute by ring-based collective_permute with double buffering (fine_grained_allgather / allgather_compute_matmul), choosing the SBUF path when the tensor fits and HBM otherwise.
  - why: Fine-grained ring steps let matmul on chunk i proceed while chunk i+1 is in flight.
  - when: TP all-gather followed by matmul.
  - fix: allgather_compute_matmul(lhs[m,K], rhs[K,N], tp_degree=8, num_groups=1)  # trn2, tp_degree even, M % (RANK_N*LNC_N*CHANNEL_N)==0
  - source: nki/library/api/fgcc.rst; nki/library/api/fg-allgather.rst  [stated, trn2]
- **sb2sb-allgather-fit** — Use allgather_sb2sb only when H*W*dtype fits SBUF with H <= 128 partitions; otherwise use allgather_sb2sb_tiled (TILE_M capped at 128, tiles distributed over LNC cores).
  - why: SBUF-to-SBUF collectives avoid HBM but need the whole tensor on-chip.
  - when: Gathering small activations across TP ranks.
  - fix: allgather_sb2sb_tiled(inp[M,K], replica_groups, tp_degree) -> [M, K*tp]
  - source: nki/library/api/sb2sb-allgather.rst  [stated, all]
- **rank-id-arithmetic-via-lookup** — Precompute per-rank offsets in a lookup tensor (iota_workers) and read it with rank_id as scalar_offset, because the NKI compiler does not support arithmetic on rank_id.
  - why: rank_id is a runtime register value; a table converts it into any derived offset.
  - when: Rank-dependent slicing after an all_gather.
  - fix: iota=[(r % G)*B_per_rank for r in ranks]; offset = dma(iota, scalar_offset=rank_id)
  - source: nki/library/api/batch-shard.rst :: iota_workers; nki/library/api/collectives.rst :: dma_copy_rank_id_kernel  [stated, all]

## Numerics and dtypes (43)

- **mm-supported-input-dtypes** — Use only float8_e4m3/float8_e5m2/bfloat16/float16/tfloat32/float32 (plus float8_e4m3fn on trn3) as nc_matmul inputs, and never mix legacy float8_e4m3 with OCP float8_e4m3fn.
  - why: These are the PE-array native formats; integer tiles are not accepted and the two e4m3 variants have different max values (legacy max 240) so cannot share one instruction.
  - when: int8/int32 tiles passed to nc_matmul, or e4m3 + e4m3fn operands together, or e4m3fn used on trn2.
  - fix: Quantize/cast to a supported float dtype before the matmul; on trn2 use nl.float8_e4m3 (legacy), on trn3 prefer nl.float8_e4m3fn.
  - numbers: float8_e4m3_legacy_max = 240
  - check (static): nc_matmul: dtype(op) in allowed set for target; not (e4m3 in dtypes and e4m3fn in dtypes); e4m3fn only if nc_version>=4
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Data types; nki/compiler/target.py comment  [stated, all]
- **mm-is-transpose-bit-accuracy** — Set is_transpose=True for identity-matmul transposes; on trn2+ it is bit-accurate (NaN/Inf preserved), on trn1 it only tags the op for the profiler.
  - why: NeuronCore-v3+ has a native transpose mode; v2 performs a real fp multiply so NaN/Inf propagate incorrectly.
  - when: Transposing tensors that may hold NaN/Inf on trn1.
  - fix: On trn1, replace NaN/Inf with finite sentinels before PE transpose, or use Vector Engine nc_transpose for <=32x32 tiles.
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Transpose mode; nki.isa.nc_transpose docstring  [stated, all]
- **mx-matmul-dtypes** — Feed nc_matmul_mx packed x4 operands (float8_e5m2_x4, float8_e4m3fn_x4, float4_e2m1fn_x4) with float8_e8m0fnu scales and an fp32 or bf16 PSUM dst.
  - why: The MX datapath dequantizes groups of 32 (8 partitions x 4 packed elements) using one shared e8m0 exponent; uint8 scales are only accepted for backward compatibility.
  - when: Unpacked fp8 tiles or fp32 scale tiles passed to nc_matmul_mx.
  - fix: Produce operands with nisa.quantize_mx (bf16/fp16 -> x4 + e8m0fnu scale) or load pre-packed data via dma_copy.
  - numbers: mx_group_size = 32 elements = 8 partitions x 4
  - check (static): nc_matmul_mx: dtype(stationary/moving) in x4 set; dtype(scales) in {float8_e8m0fnu, uint8}; dst.dtype in {fp32, bf16}
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul_mx docstring, section Data types  [stated, trn3]
- **dma-copy-dtype-conversion-via-fp32** — Expect dma_copy with differing dtypes to cast src->fp32->dst, except under dge_mode=hwdge where dtypes must match exactly.
  - why: Static/SW-DGE DMAs have cast logic; HWDGE moves raw bytes without interpreting data.
  - when: dma_copy(dst=bf16, src=fp32, dge_mode=hwdge) fails validation.
  - fix: Use dge_mode=none/swdge for casting copies, or .view(dtype) to reinterpret bytes under hwdge.
  - check (static): dma_copy(dge_mode==hwdge): src.dtype==dst.dtype
  - source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring Data types; migration/index.rst 'dge_mode type matching'  [stated, all]
- **tensor-scalar-cumulative-dtypes** — Do not use int32/uint32 tiles as input or output of tensor_scalar_cumulative; op1 must be add/subtract/mult/max/min.
  - why: ISA limitation of the cumulative path; 32-bit integers are not representable in its fp32 datapath.
  - when: Cumulative sums over int32 index arrays.
  - fix: Compute in fp32/int16 and cast, or use iota-based arithmetic.
  - check (static): tensor_scalar_cumulative: dtype(src/dst) not in {int32,uint32}; op1 in {add,subtract,multiply,maximum,minimum}
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_scalar_cumulative docstring  [stated, all]
- **range-select-reduce-res-fp32-avoid-nan** — When range_select writes a bf16/fp16/fp8 dst, keep reduce_res in fp32 so a fully-masked row (-inf after downcast) does not produce NaN in the following activation subtract.

  - why: The systolic array accumulates in FP32 and PSUM near-memory accumulation is FP32; trn3 adds optional BF16 PSUM output with rounding at the write.

- **num-fp8-formats** — Choose FP8 formats deliberately: FP8_E5M2 (5-bit exp), FP8_E4M3 (4-bit exp), FP8_E3M4; cFP8 on trn2 has adjustable exponent bias, and only E4/E5 get the double-rate matmul.

- **num-rounding-modes** — Pick the rounding mode explicitly: RNE is the hardware default; enable stochastic rounding with NEURON_RT_STOCHASTIC_ROUNDING_EN=1 (default on in PyTorch-Neuron when XLA_USE_BF16=1) when accumulating small increments into bf16/fp16.

  - when: rmsnorm_mx_prefill with router_weights; any nc_matmul_mx on swizzled activations.
