  - source: nki/library/api/rmsnorm-mx-prefill.rst :: router_weights  [stated, trn3]
- **unpadded-hidden-size-for-rms-mean** — When H is zero-padded to a multiple of 512, pass unpadded_hidden_size so the RMS mean divides by the true H while the sum of squares runs over the padded H.
  - why: Zero padding contributes 0 to the sum but would wrongly enlarge the denominator.
  - when: Padded hidden dims for MX block alignment.
  - fix: rmsnorm_mx_prefill(..., unpadded_hidden_size=H_true)
  - source: nki/library/api/rmsnorm-mx-prefill.rst :: unpadded_hidden_size  [stated, trn3]
- **mxfp8-activations-stay-bf16-when-gathered** — Keep activations in BF16 (not pre-quantized MXFP8) when they are gathered per block via indirect DMA, because row gathers break the 32-element MX quantization group alignment.
  - why: MX scales are shared by 32 consecutive elements; gathering rows scrambles the groups.
  - when: Blockwise MoE forward/backward with MXFP8 weights.
  - fix: blockwise_mm_fwd_mxfp8(hidden_states bf16, gate_up_proj_weight MXFP8 + scales)
  - source: nki/library/api/blockwise-mm-forward-mxfp8.rst; nki/library/api/blockwise-mm-backward-mxfp8.rst  [stated, trn3]
- **scan-fp32-accumulate-and-carry** — Accumulate cumsum/linear scans in fp32 regardless of input dtype, tile the free dim at 2048 and carry the last column into the next tile's initial value; expect ~1e-2 abs error beyond ~5K elements.
  - why: tensor_tensor_scan precision degrades over long sequences; fp32 limits drift.
  - when: Long cumulative sums.
  - fix: cumsum(x) / linear_scan(decay, data, initial)
  - numbers: F_tile = 2048; abs_err_gt_5K = ~1e-2
  - source: nki/library/api/cumsum.rst; nki/library/api/linear-scan.rst  [stated, all]
- **bf16-score-drops-hadamard-and-quantize** — Keep projections in MX but compute attention scores with bf16 nc_matmul so the Q swizzle + quantize_mx + Hadamard chain leaves the per-tile critical path; Hadamard rotation is a mathematical no-op (q H H^T k^T = q k^T).
  - why: The rotation only exists to make MX quantization well-behaved; without score quantization it is unnecessary and precision improves.
  - when: Sparse-attention indexer or any score path with MX inputs.
  - fix: sparse_attention_indexer_mx_bf16score(...)
  - source: nki/library/api/sparse-attention-indexer-mx-bf16score.rst :: Notes  [stated, trn3]

## Correctness pitfalls (42)

- **mm-no-accumulate-onto-memset-psum** — Do not memset/tensor_copy a PSUM tile and then accumulate matmuls onto it on trn1/trn2.
  - why: On NeuronCore-v2/v3 matmul accumulation onto a PSUM location value-initialized by a non-matmul instruction is undefined behavior in hardware.
  - when: nisa.memset(psum_tile, 0) followed by nc_matmul(..., accumulate=True) as a 'bias init' trick.
  - fix: Let the first matmul overwrite (accumulate=False) and add the bias during PSUM evacuation (activation bias=, tensor_tensor).
  - check (static): flag nc_matmul(accumulate=True) whose dst was last written by memset/tensor_copy and nc_version<=3
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, note under Accumulation mode  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-output-orientation** — Remember nc_matmul computes dst = stationary.T @ moving: stationary free dim becomes dst partition dim, moving free dim becomes dst free dim.
  - why: Operands are both K-major (K on partitions); the output rows come from the stationary columns, so passing A as stationary yields A.T @ B, not A @ B.
  - when: Mismatched dst shape errors or transposed results when porting A @ B.
  - fix: For C[M,N] = A[M,K] @ B[K,N]: stationary = A.T tile [K, M<=128], moving = B tile [K, N<=512], dst = [M, N] PSUM.
  - check (static): nc_matmul: dst.shape[0] == prod(stationary.shape[1:]) and prod(dst.shape[1:]) == prod(moving.shape[1:])
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Layout  [stated, all]
- **act-valid-input-ranges** — Keep inputs of Scalar Engine log/sin/arctan/sqrt/rsqrt/reciprocal within their valid ranges (log [2^-64,2^64], sin [-pi,pi], arctan [-pi/2,pi/2], sqrt [2^-116,2^118], rsqrt [2^-87,2^97], reciprocal +-[2^-42,2^42]); use nl.sin for unbounded sine.
  - why: Activations are polynomial fits with no range reduction or clamping; e.g. nisa.activation(op=nl.sin) on 9.0 returns ~27.65. nl.sin adds range-reduction instructions.
  - when: Rotary/positional kernels feeding raw angles to nisa.activation(op=nl.sin); log of 0; reciprocal of tiny denominators.
  - fix: Reduce arguments modulo 2*pi (or call nl.sin), clamp with tensor_scalar max/min, or add epsilon before log/rsqrt.
  - numbers: log_range = [2^-64, 2^64]; sin_range = [-pi, pi]; arctan_range = [-pi/2, pi/2]; sqrt_range = [2^-116, 2^118]; rsqrt_range = [2^-87, 2^97]; reciprocal_range = +-[2^-42, 2^42]
  - check (simulator): activation(op in {sin,arctan,log,sqrt,rsqrt,reciprocal}) without preceding range reduction/clamp
  - source: nki/api/nki.api.shared.rst table tbl-act-func and note  [stated, all]
- **acc-scalar-reduce-regs-shared** — Treat the Scalar Engine's 128 reduce registers as shared mutable state across all activation/activate2/activation_reduce calls; reset with reset_reduce before each new reduction chain and do not interleave activation_reduce with activation chains.
  - why: There is one 32-bit accumulator per lane shared by all Scalar reduce-capable instructions; reduce_regs persist until reset.
  - when: Interleaved softmax row sums from two independent streams producing wrong totals.
  - fix: Start each chain with reduce_cmd=reset_reduce, continue with reduce, pass reduce_res only on the last call (extra readout instruction costs a little).
  - numbers: reduce_regs = 128 x 32-bit
  - check (static): activation chain: first call reduce_cmd==reset_reduce; no activation_reduce between reduce and final readout
  - source: nki.isa.activation and activation_reduce docstrings  [stated, all]
- **acc-vector-accumulators-shared** — Treat Vector Engine accumulators as shared across exponential, range_select, select_reduce, tensor_scalar_reduce and tensor_scalar_cumulative; always issue reset_reduce after any instruction that ran with reduce_cmd=idle.
  - why: Even idle-mode instructions may clobber the accumulator state, so continuing with reduce after them yields garbage.
  - when: Flash-attention loops mixing range_select(reduce) with unrelated select_reduce(idle).
  - fix: Use reduce_cmd=reset_reduce at the start of each accumulation group and reduce for continuation; avoid interleaving other accumulating ops.
  - check (static): vector accumulating op with reduce_cmd==reduce preceded by a vector accumulating op with reduce_cmd==idle
  - source: nki.isa.exponential, select_reduce, tensor_scalar_reduce docstrings (Accumulator behavior notes)  [stated, all]
- **match-replace8-duplicate-order** — Do not assume nc_match_replace8 and nc_find_index8 order duplicate matches the same way: match_replace8 pairs duplicates in descending position order across dst_idx columns, find_index8 in ascending order.
  - why: The two instructions process vals in opposite directions (match_replace8 iterates i=7..0).
  - when: Top-k index extraction that mixes the two instructions giving permuted indices.
  - fix: Use one instruction consistently or sort indices afterwards.
  - source: nki.isa.nc_match_replace8 docstring  [stated, all]
- **nonzero-with-count-partition-stride** — Expect nonzero_with_count (trn2+) to read and write only partitions 0,16,...,112; dst needs one extra free element (count) and int32 dtype, src fp32/int32 in SBUF.
  - why: Each GpSimd core touches only the first of its 16 connected partitions.
  - when: Reading results from partitions other than multiples of 16.
  - fix: Place one row per 16-partition group or replicate inputs; read dst[k*16, :].
  - numbers: active_partitions = 0,16,...,112
  - check (static): nonzero_with_count: dst.shape[1]==src.shape[1]+1; dst.dtype==int32; src.dtype in {fp32,int32}; nc_version>=3
  - source: nki.isa.nonzero_with_count docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **nl-var-keepdims-ignored** — Expect nl.var to always return a keepdims=True shape regardless of the keepdims argument.
  - why: Documented current behavior of the experimental wrapper.
  - when: Shape mismatch after nl.var(x, axis=1, keepdims=False).
  - fix: Squeeze explicitly or accept (P,1).
  - source: nki.language.var docstring  [stated, all]
- **tile-shape-mismatch-garbage** — Assert kernel input shapes match the tiling the kernel implements; mismatched larger inputs silently produce garbage for untouched regions.
  - why: There is no bounds checking: a [128,512] kernel applied to a [256,512] tensor leaves the bottom half uninitialized.
  - when: Output rows beyond the processed tile contain random values.
  - fix: assert in_tensor.shape == (X, Y) or loop over ceil(P/128).
  - check (static): compare kernel loop coverage with declared input shapes.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations (garbage data)  [stated, all]
- **lnc-identical-control-flow** — Keep dynamic control flow identical on both cores of an LNC; divergent device-side branches are undefined behavior (likely runtime error).
  - why: The SDK assumes each core runs 'the same' program; static (compile-time) branches on program_id are fine, dynamic register-based divergence is not.
  - when: while reg: loops whose condition differs per core.
  - fix: Make trip counts/conditions core-independent or pad work so both cores execute the same dynamic path.
  - check (static): flag dynamic_range/while conditions derived from program_id-dependent data.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/lnc.rst :: Final Notes  [stated, trn2]
- **num-transpose-nan-inf** — Do not transpose tensors that may contain NaN/Inf with an identity matmul on trn1; the NaN/Inf propagates across the output. Use trn2+ transpose mode (is_transpose=True) for bit-accurate transposes.
  - why: Matmul-based transpose multiplies by 0.0/1.0 and accumulates, so NaN*0 = NaN spreads along the accumulation chain.
  - when: Transposing logits/attention scores with masked -inf values on trn1.
  - fix: Mask after transposing, or use DMA transpose / VectorE 32x32 transpose which are bit-accurate.
  - check (static): flag TensorE transposes of tiles produced after a -inf mask on trn1.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Built-in Transpose Support  [stated, all]
- **cp-uninitialized-allocations** — Explicitly initialize any SBUF/PSUM/HBM tensor that is read before being fully written (accumulators, loop conditions): nl.ndarray does not zero memory.
  - why: Allocation only reserves space; the tutorial memsets fp32 result tiles before tensor_tensor accumulation and zeroes the loop-condition tensor via DMA.
  - when: Accumulating with op=add into a freshly allocated tile, or nl.zeros expected from ndarray.
  - fix: nisa.memset(dst=tile, value=0.0) or nl.zeros(...).
  - check (static): dataflow: flag reads of an allocation with no prior full write.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Optimizing DMA through blocking; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control  [stated, all]
- **cp-psum-accumulate-semantics** — When reusing a PSUM tile across accumulation groups, be explicit with accumulate=False on the first matmul of each group (or allocate a fresh PSUM tile per group).
  - why: Default auto-detection treats the first write to a PSUM location as overwrite and subsequent writes as accumulate; reuse without a clear 'first write' risks accumulating onto stale data.
  - when: Loop that reuses one psum buffer for multiple output tiles without nl.zeros.
  - fix: nisa.nc_matmul(dst=psum, ..., accumulate=False) for k==0, accumulate=True otherwise.
  - check (static): track PSUM allocation reuse across independent output tiles.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Near-memory accumulation in PSUM (note)  [stated, all]
- **cp-dynamic-loop-var-not-python** — Never use a dynamic_range loop variable in host-side Python logic (if i == 0, shape math); it is a device register.
  - why: The loop body is emitted once and iterated by hardware, so the variable has no compile-time value.
  - when: if i == 0: inside dynamic_range.
  - fix: Use device-side conditionals (register compares) or peel the first iteration statically.
  - check (static): AST: dynamic loop var used in Python control flow or arithmetic feeding shapes.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dynamic-loops.rst :: Hardware Lowering  [stated, all]
- **cp-double-fp8-padding** — Pad the contraction dim to a multiple of 2 (zeros) before using double-row FP8 matmul; both operands' second dim must be exactly 2.
  - why: The hardware pairs two K-halves per PE; an odd K would read uninitialized data.
  - when: K % 2 != 0 with perf_mode=double_row.
  - fix: memset the padding slice to 0 in both stationary and moving tiles.
  - check (static): check shape[1]==2 and padded regions zeroed.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium2_arch.rst :: Double FP8 Matmul Performance  [stated, trn2]
- **cp-mx-interleave-layout** — For MX matmul, pack the four elements that were 128 apart along K into adjacent free-dim slots (interleave) before quantize_mx; feeding row-contiguous data gives wrong results, not an error.
  - why: nc_matmul_mx assumes each _x4 element holds K positions k, k+128, k+256, k+384 and the scale for its 8P x 4F group.
  - when: MX kernels verified only against nc_matmul_mx_golden with pre-packed inputs.
  - fix: Use copy_data_strided-style tensor_copy to build [128, F, 4] from [4,128,F]; validate against the golden model.
  - check (simulator): compare against the reference packing in the tutorial.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/mxfp-matmul.rst :: Data Tensor; nki/guides/architecture/trainium3_arch.rst :: Quad-MXFP8/MXFP4  [stated, trn3]
- **cp-print-is-compile-time** — Use nki device_print (or nki.simulate) to inspect runtime values; ordinary print() in a kernel executes during compilation only.
  - why: Most NKI code runs at specialization; only nki.isa calls become device instructions.
  - when: Debug prints that never show per-iteration values.
  - fix: Build kernels incrementally and verify small operators in simulation mode.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Core Programming Model; nki/nki_faq.rst :: How can I debug numerical issues  [stated, all]
- **cp-tensore-transposes-via-nl-matmul** — Know that nl.matmul(x, y) with transpose_x=False (or nisa.nc_matmul high-level form on [M,K]) silently inserts a TensorE transpose of x; pass pre-transposed operands to avoid hidden cost.
  - why: nc_matmul(x, y) for [M,K] inputs is a two-step nc_transpose + matmul.
  - when: Unexpected transpose instructions in the profile after a plain matmul call.
  - fix: Provide x as [K,M] (lhsT) and call nisa.nc_matmul(stationary=xT, moving=y).
  - check (static): flag nl.matmul without transposed LHS in hot loops.
  - source: nki/guides/architecture/trainium_inferentia2_arch.rst :: Tensor Engine Layout; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #8  [stated, all]
- **cp-single-core-note-outdated** — Do not take the performance guide's 'NKI only supports running a kernel on a single NeuronCore' note at face value; the LNC guide and FAQ document kernel[2] launches on two physical cores.
  - why: The docs were updated at different times; the LNC page (12/2025) and FAQ are newer.

- **align-4-bytes-small-vectors** — Align small per-partition vectors (ones, eps, fp32 stats) to 4 bytes (align=4) when manually allocating.
  - why: Unaligned 4-byte vectors adjacent to 2-byte buffers caused a race (NKILIB-876).

  - fix: bufs.one_vec = sbm.alloc_stack((128, 1), dtype=io_type, align=4)
  - numbers: align = 4 B
  - check (static): fp32 alloc_stack without align

- **zero-bias-tensor-for-activation** — Keep a memset-zero [P,1] fp32 bias tensor and pass it to nisa.activation calls that need a scale but no bias.

  - fix: zero_bias = nl.ndarray((128,1), fp32); zero_bias[...] = 0.0; nisa.activation(np.copy, x, scale=s, bias=zero_bias)
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/rmsnorm/rmsnorm_quant_constants.py bias_vector_sbuf comment; aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/pipelined_attention.py zero_bias_tensor  [stated, all]
- **mask-partial-partition-tiles** — When N*C (or H) is not a multiple of 128, use mask=(i_p < n) on load/compute/store with the full 128-partition mgrid instead of shrinking the tile.
  - why: Masking keeps instruction shapes uniform (no per-tail code) while skipping out-of-range partitions.

  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/interpolate_*_fwd.py; maxpooling.py (old API)  [stated, all]
- **uint32-indices-for-dma-transpose-int32-for-skip** — Keep two copies of a block index table: int32 with -1 sentinels for dma_copy(oob_mode.skip) and a uint32 cast (done once upfront on VectorE) for dma_transpose which requires uint32.

- **unused-per-core-input-compile-error** — Ensure every kernel input is referenced on every core; an input consumed only on one LNC branch causes a compiler error (compute a dummy use on the other core).
  - why: The compiler rejects inputs that are dead on one program.

- **validate-against-cpu-reference-multi-metric** — Compute the reference result on CPU (tensor.cpu()) and compare with several metrics (allclose atol/rtol, max abs diff, norm of diff, cosine similarity) using dtype-appropriate tolerances.

- **validate-stage-by-stage** — For multi-stage kernels, translate and validate one logical stage at a time (store the intermediate to HBM, compare to the PyTorch intermediate) before fusing stages in SBUF; test the failing stage on a single 128x128 tile.

- **print-is-compile-time** — Use nl.device_print for runtime values; Python print() inside a kernel executes at trace/compile time and shows only static shapes.

- **tensor-reduce-axis-for-nd** — Pass the axis that matches the actual tensor rank to nisa.tensor_reduce on 3D/4D tiles (reduce innermost first, e.g. axis=2 then axis=1); do not copy Beta-2 axis=1 examples blindly.

- **partition-broadcast-via-zero-stride-only-free-dims** — Use stride-0 (.broadcast / .ap stride 0) only on free dims or a size-1 partition dim; cross-partition replication of a non-size-1 partition needs stream_shuffle_broadcast or a matmul.

  - check (static): Load/view whose resulting dim0 > 128 after integer indexing -> error.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Initial NKI Kernel  [stated, all]
- **simulator-nan-sentinel-for-uninitialized** — Assert the simulated output contains no NaN (float) or stray 4s (int) to catch reads of memory that was never written; hardware may hide this by returning stale but plausible data.
  - why: The simulator fills every fresh allocation with NaN/4 sentinels that propagate through arithmetic.
  - when: Unexpected NaN in simulation output.
  - fix: result = nki.simulate(k)(inputs); assert not np.any(np.isnan(result)); check nl.ndarray tiles are fully written, loop bounds, conditional writes.
  - numbers: float_sentinel = NaN; int_sentinel = 4
  - check (simulator): After simulate: np.isnan(out).any() -> report uninitialized read.
  - source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: Uninitialized Memory Detection  [stated, all]
- **simulator-ignores-sbuf-psum-capacity** — Do not rely on the simulator to catch SBUF/PSUM capacity overflow or overlapping-address conflicts; it allocates every tensor independently.
  - why: The simulator's memory model has no capacity limits or aliasing, so kernels with memory conflicts pass simulation yet fail or corrupt on hardware.
  - when: Kernel passes simulation but misbehaves on device.
  - fix: Check footprint statically (per-partition bytes) and test on hardware; use SbufManager for deterministic layout.
  - source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: Memory Model  [stated, all]
- **simulator-accepts-unsupported-python** — Restrict kernel bodies to the NKI meta-programming subset even though the simulator runs arbitrary Python; otherwise the kernel will fail at hardware compile time.
  - why: The simulator interprets Python directly with no compilation step, while the NKI compiler only supports a restricted subset (NKIObject classes, string-key dicts, etc.).
  - when: Kernel uses closures, arbitrary classes or dynamic control flow.
  - fix: Follow the NKI Language Guide value/container rules; test a hardware compile early.
  - source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: NKI Meta-Programming Support  [stated, all]
- **simulator-constraint-checks-incomplete** — Treat a clean simulator run as necessary but not sufficient; some hardware constraint checks (shape limits, dtype, buffer, engine, arch version) are still missing.
  - why: Hardware constraint validation is actively being developed.
  - when: Kernel passes sim, fails on HW compile/run.
  - fix: Report to Neuron; add explicit asserts in the kernel for tile sizes.
  - source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: Hardware Constraint Validation  [stated, all]
- **kernel-cache-requires-purity** — Make kernel behavior depend only on its arguments (shapes, dtypes, compile-time values); global state or mutable closures can return a stale cached compilation.
  - why: NKI caches compiled kernels keyed on input arguments.
  - when: Kernel reads module-level variables or mutated objects.
  - fix: Pass configuration as explicit kwargs / NKIObject dataclasses.
  - check (static): Kernel body references free variables that are not constants -> warn.
  - source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Kernel Caching  [stated, all]
- **inplace-output-aliasing** — Treat in-place kernel outputs (cross_entropy_backward inplace=True, scatter_add input) as consumed: the input tensor is overwritten and cannot be reused afterwards.
  - why: In-place writes save HBM (num_positions x vocab x bytes) but alias the input.
  - when: Reusing logits after the backward kernel.
  - fix: Set inplace=False or clone before the call.
  - source: nki/library/api/cross-entropy.rst :: cross_entropy_backward; nki/library/api/scatter-add.rst  [stated, all]
- **ndarray-is-uninitialized** — Initialize every nl.ndarray (memset, dma_copy, or compute) before reading it; allocation does not zero memory.
  - why: Contents are undefined until written; HBM shared tensors used as loop conditions must be explicitly initialized too.
  - when: Accumulators or flags allocated with nl.ndarray.
  - fix: acc = nl.ndarray(...); nisa.memset(dst=acc, value=0.0)  or use nl.zeros.
  - check (simulator): Simulator NaN sentinel; static: tensor read before any write.
  - source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Creating Tensors; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control  [stated, all]
- **shape-mismatch-yields-silent-garbage** — Assert that framework tensor shapes match the shapes the kernel tiles over; a kernel written for [128,512] fed a [256,512] tensor silently leaves the remainder as garbage.
  - why: Untouched rows of the output HBM tensor retain whatever was there.
  - when: Kernel hard-codes tile extents.
  - fix: assert in_tensor.shape == (X, Y) or loop over ceil(sz_p/128) tiles.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/tiling-overview.rst :: Tile size considerations (garbage data note)  [stated, all]
- **scatter-add-unique-indices-per-tile** — Ensure indices within each 128-row tile are unique when using the gather-accumulate-scatter pattern; duplicate indices in a tile lose updates.
  - why: The pattern reads old rows, adds, and writes back once per tile with no atomicity.
  - when: scatter_add with repeated targets.
  - fix: Pre-sort/deduplicate indices or use the accumulating MoE unpermute path.
  - check (static): Duplicate indices within any 128-chunk -> warn.
  - source: nki/library/api/scatter-add.rst :: Notes  [stated, all]
- **do-not-pass-shape-ints-as-runtime-args** — Derive dimensions like H from tensor shapes inside the kernel; do not pass them as runtime scalars, because the framework materializes them as HBM tensors and shape math built on them is garbage.
  - why: Only trace-time Python ints participate in specialization.
  - when: Kernel signature with an int that the framework wraps as a tensor.
  - fix: H = wuv_qtz_hbm.shape[0]*4 // L  instead of a runtime H argument.
  - check (static): int-typed kernel arg used in shape arithmetic that is actually a tensor at trace time -> error.
  - source: nki/library/api/mla-vup-oproj-cte.rst :: Notes  [stated, all]

## API constraints (NKI 0.6.0) (146)

- **mm-tensor-indirection-rules** — When using .indirect() views on nc_matmul operands (trn3), keep tile_position at (0,0), use a Tensor-Engine float dtype, and do not use indirection on moving when is_transpose=True.
  - why: Tensor indirection (gather/scatter) is incompatible with hardware tiling and only defined for fp16/bf16/fp8 operands.
  - when: nc_matmul with .indirect() plus tile_position/tile_size, or fp32 indirect operands.
  - fix: Drop tiling mode and cast to bf16/fp16/fp8 when gathering operands; index starts on a 32-partition quadrant boundary.
  - numbers: indirect_index_alignment = 32 partitions
  - check (static): nc_matmul: any(is_indirect(op)) implies tile_position in {None,(0,0)} and dtype in {fp16,bf16,fp8*} and not (is_transpose and is_indirect(moving))
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Tensor indirection  [stated, trn3]
- **mx-indirection-pairs-agree** — Apply .indirect() to an MX data tile and its scale tile together with the same index (or to neither).
  - why: In MX format data bytes and scale exponents form one logical tensor; gathering one without the other mis-pairs scales.
  - when: stationary.indirect(idx) with a plain stationary_scale.
  - fix: Use the identical index view on both members of the pair; keep tile_position (0,0).
  - check (static): nc_matmul_mx: is_indirect(stationary)==is_indirect(stationary_scale) with same index; same for moving pair
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul_mx docstring, section Tensor indirection  [stated, trn3]
- **quantize-mx-shape-rules** — Give quantize_mx a bf16/fp16 SBUF src with partition size a multiple of 32 (<=128) and free size a multiple of 4; dst free size is src free / 4.
  - why: Quantization groups are 8 partitions x 4 elements and the x4 output packs four 8-bit values into one 32-bit element.
  - when: Free sizes not divisible by 4 or fp32 inputs.
  - fix: Cast to bf16 first; pad free dim to a multiple of 4; allocate dst (P, F//4) x4 dtype and dst_scale e8m0fnu in SBUF.
  - numbers: block_scale_rule = 2^(floor(log2(amax)) - (Emax-1)), Emax=8 e4m3fn / 15 e5m2; zero group -> 2^-127
  - check (static): quantize_mx: src.dtype in {bf16,fp16}; src.shape[0]%32==0; prod(src.shape[1:])%4==0; dst free == src free/4; all buffers sbuf
  - source: nki.isa.quantize_mx docstring, sections Tile size and Scale calculation  [stated, trn3]
- **dma-engine-param-only-with-hwdge** — Pass engine=nisa.engine.sync or nisa.engine.scalar to dma_copy only together with dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge.
  - why: The engine field selects which sequencer drives the hardware DGE; it is meaningless for swdge/none.
  - when: dma_copy(engine=scalar) without hwdge.
  - fix: Add dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge or drop engine.
  - check (static): dma_copy: engine != unknown implies dge_mode == hwdge and engine in {sync, scalar}
  - source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, param engine  [stated, trn2]
- **dma-priority-trn3-only** — Use the DMA priority (0-3, lower is higher priority) argument only on trn3.
  - why: DMA QoS levels are a NeuronCore-v4 feature; earlier targets reject or ignore it.
  - when: priority= passed to dma_copy/collectives on trn2.
  - fix: Gate priority usage on nisa.get_nc_version()==gen4.
  - numbers: priority_range = 0-3
  - check (static): priority is not None implies nc_version>=4
  - source: nki.isa.dma_copy docstring, param priority; nki.collectives docstrings  [stated, trn3]
- **dma-rmw-removed-use-dma-compute** — Do not pass dst_rmw_op/unique_indices to dma_copy; use nisa.dma_compute(dst, [src, dst], reduce_op=nl.add) for read-modify-write.
  - why: DMA RMW moved to dma_compute in NKI 0.3.0; dma_copy no longer accepts those parameters.
  - when: Old scatter-add loops using dma_copy(dst_rmw_op=nl.add).
  - fix: First iteration dma_copy; later iterations dma_compute(dst=acc, srcs=[src.ap(...), acc], reduce_op=nl.add, unique_indices=True).
  - check (static): dma_copy kwargs contain dst_rmw_op or unique_indices
  - source: migration/index.rst 'dst_rmw_op and unique_indices removed'  [stated, all]
- **ap-pattern-format** — .ap(pattern=[[stride,count],...]) overrides shape/strides entirely; list the partition dim first for on-chip tensors and keep counts consistent with the instruction's expected element count.
  - why: It is the as_strided-style escape hatch; the compiler trusts the pattern and the offset composes with the view's base offset.
  - when: Patterns with mismatched element totals or partition dim not first.
  - fix: Start from t.get_pattern() and edit strides; pass offset explicitly when shifting.
  - check (static): ap(): len(pattern)>=1 and pattern[0][1] <= 128 for sbuf/psum
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.ap and get_pattern docstrings  [stated, all]
- **nl-load-store-are-experimental-wrappers** — Treat nl.load/nl.store as experimental conveniences; for control and portability write nisa.dma_copy(dst=..., src=...) with explicit SBUF tiles.
  - why: nl.load/store were removed in 0.2.0 and reintroduced in 0.3.0 as wrappers that allocate the SBUF tile for you; nisa.dma_copy exposes dge_mode/oob/priority.
  - when: Kernels mixing nl.load with manual allocation/scheduling needs.
  - fix: sb = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(dst=sb, src=hbm[...]).
  - source: nki.language.load/store docstrings (<<experimental>>); migration/index.rst note on nl.load/nl.store  [stated, all]
- **act-scale-bias-dtype-and-shape** — Give activation a float32 scale (scalar or [N,1] vector) and a bias that is an [N,1] vector on trn1 (scalar allowed from trn2) of any dtype except tfloat32.
  - why: Scale/bias are broadcast along the free dim per partition; NeuronCore-v2 lacks scalar-bias immediates.
  - when: bias=0.5 scalar on trn1; scale tile in bf16; bias shape (1,N).
  - fix: Allocate bias as nl.ndarray((N,1), ...) in SBUF; keep scale fp32.
  - check (static): activation: scale is const or (shape==(N,1) and dtype==fp32); bias scalar -> nc_version>=3; bias.dtype != tfloat32; N==data.shape[0]
  - source: nki.isa.activation docstring, sections Data types and Layout  [stated, all]
- **act-partition-and-free-size-match** — Make activation/activate2 data and dst share the same partition size (<=128) and the same number of elements per partition.
  - why: The instruction is a per-lane streaming op; shapes may differ but element counts per partition must match.
  - when: dst (128,512) with data (128,2,256) is fine; dst (128,256) with data (128,512) is rejected.
  - fix: Reshape views rather than changing element counts.
  - check (static): activation: data.shape[0]==dst.shape[0]<=128 and prod(data.shape[1:])==prod(dst.shape[1:])
  - source: nki.isa.activation docstring, section Tile size  [stated, all]
- **act-supported-function-table** — Use only the Scalar Engine activation set as activation op: copy, square, sigmoid, relu, prelu, gelu, gelu_dx, gelu_apprx_tanh, gelu_apprx_sigmoid, gelu_apprx_sigmoid_dx, silu, silu_dx, tanh, softplus, mish, erf, erf_dx, exp, log, sin, arctan, sqrt, rsqrt, reciprocal, sign, abs.
  - why: Only these have hardware polynomial tables; other nl ops (e.g. nl.cos, nl.tan, nl.power) are not activation ops.
  - when: nisa.activation(op=nl.cos) or op=nl.power.
  - fix: Compose from supported ops (cos via sin(x+pi/2) with range reduction; power via exp(y*log(x)) on valid ranges) or use tensor_tensor(op=nl.power) on GpSimd.
  - check (static): activation.op in ACT_FUNCS
  - source: nki/api/nki.api.shared.rst table tbl-act-func  [stated, all]
- **act-scattered-dst-not-psum** — When a Scalar Engine instruction writes through a .indirect() scatter view, the dst must be in SBUF, not PSUM.
  - why: Scalar Engine scatter writes are only wired to SBUF on NeuronCore-v4.
  - when: activation/tensor_scalar(engine=scalar)/tensor_copy(engine=scalar) with dst.indirect(idx) in PSUM.
  - fix: Scatter into an SBUF tile, or run the op on Vector Engine.
  - check (static): scalar-engine op: is_indirect(dst) implies buffer(dst)==sbuf
  - source: nki.isa.activation docstring, section Tensor indirection  [stated, trn3]
- **activate2-trn3-only-and-op-combos** — Use nisa.activate2 only on trn3 and only with (op0,op1) in {(multiply,add),(multiply,subtract),(multiply,bypass),(add,bypass),(subtract,bypass),(bypass,bypass)}.
  - why: activate2 is the NeuronCore-v4 three-stage Scalar pipeline (tensor-scalar, activation, reduce); other combos have no encoding.
  - when: activate2 with op0=nl.add, op1=nl.multiply, or activate2 on trn2.
  - fix: Reorder as (multiply, add) with reverse flags, or fall back to tensor_scalar + activation.
  - check (static): activate2: nc_version>=4 and (op0,op1) in ALLOWED6; op1 set -> op0 set; reverse0 -> op0 set; reverse1 -> op1 set
  - source: nki.isa.activate2 docstring  [stated, trn3]
- **activation-reduce-deprecated** — Prefer nisa.activation(reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_cmd=nisa.reduce_cmd.reset_reduce, reduce_res=...) over nisa.activation_reduce.
  - why: activation_reduce is kept only for backward compatibility and is equivalent to activation with reset_reduce.
  - when: New code calling nisa.activation_reduce.
  - fix: Replace with nisa.activation(..., reduce_op=nl.add, reduce_cmd=nisa.reduce_cmd.reset_reduce, reduce_res=out).
  - check (static): call to nisa.activation_reduce
  - source: nki.isa.activation_reduce docstring  [stated, all]
- **act-reduce-op-add-only-on-activation** — Use reduce_op=nl.add for nisa.activation's fused reduction; the richer set (add, maximum, minimum, abs_max, abs_min) is only available through activate2 on trn3.
  - why: The legacy activation instruction only has a summing reduce path; v4's activate2 adds max/min variants.
  - when: activation(reduce_op=nl.maximum) to compute a row max on trn2.
  - fix: Compute row max with tensor_reduce(op=nl.maximum) or range_select/select_reduce on Vector Engine.
  - check (static): activation: reduce_op in {None, add}; activate2: reduce_op in {add,maximum,minimum,abs_max,abs_min}
  - source: nki.isa.activation docstring ('reduce_op must be nl.add'); nki.isa.activate2 docstring  [stated, all]
- **act-reciprocal-no-bias-trn1** — Do not pass a bias to nisa.activation(op=nl.reciprocal) on trn1.
  - why: NeuronCore-v2 Scalar Engine reciprocal lacks bias support.
  - when: activation(op=nl.reciprocal, bias=eps) on trn1.
  - fix: Add epsilon with tensor_scalar first, or use nisa.reciprocal on Vector Engine.
  - check (static): activation(op==reciprocal) and bias is not None and nc_version==2
  - source: nki/api/nki.api.shared.rst Engine Selection note  [stated, trn1]
- **tensor-scalar-reduce-rules** — In tensor_scalar_reduce use one arithmetic op0, reduce_op in {add, multiply, max, min}, pass reduce_init only with load_reduce, and do not rely on reverse0 (unsupported).
  - why: Only one ALU stage exists before the reduce path; identity init is 0/1/-inf/+inf per reduce_op.
  - when: tensor_scalar_reduce(op0=..., op1=...) or reverse0=True.
  - fix: Chain a tensor_scalar first if two ops are needed; use reduce_cmd=load_reduce with reduce_init for warm starts.
  - check (static): tensor_scalar_reduce: reduce_op in {add,multiply,maximum,minimum}; reduce_init set iff reduce_cmd==load_reduce; reverse0==False
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_scalar_reduce docstring  [stated, all]
- **ts-operands-fp32-and-shape** — Make tensor_scalar operand0/operand1 either compile-time constants or (data.shape[0],1) fp32 tiles; for unary op0 (abs, rsqrt) pass operand0=None or 0.
  - why: The broadcast operand is read as a per-partition fp32 immediate.
  - when: operand0 as a bf16 (P,1) tile or an (1,N) row vector.
  - fix: Cast the per-partition vector to fp32 (tensor_copy) and shape it (P,1).
  - check (static): tensor_scalar: operand tiles have shape (P,1) and dtype fp32
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_scalar docstring  [stated, all]
- **tensor-reduce-axis-last-contiguous** — Reduce only over the trailing contiguous free axes with tensor_reduce/nl.sum/nl.max etc. (e.g. (3,), (2,3), (1,2,3) for a 4-D tile); axis 0 is never reducible.
  - why: Vector Engine reduces along the innermost free dims per partition; since 0.3.0 axis numbers refer to real tensor dims (axis=1 no longer means 'last').
  - when: nl.sum(x, axis=1) on a 3-D tile, or axis=0.
  - fix: Rearrange the tile so the reduced dims are last, or transpose for partition reductions.
  - check (static): reduce axis tuple == range(k, ndim) for some k>=1
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_reduce docstring; nl.sum/mean/max docstrings; migration/index.rst tensor_reduce axis fix  [stated, all]
- **tensor-reduce-dst-shape-consistency** — Size the tensor_reduce dst so elements per partition equal the product of the non-reduced free dims (1 when all free dims are reduced); use keepdims=True to keep broadcastable shape.
  - why: The instruction writes exactly one result per surviving free index per partition.
  - when: dst (128,512) for a full-free reduction of (128,512) data.
  - fix: dst = nl.ndarray((P,1), ...) or keepdims=True.
  - check (static): tensor_reduce: prod(dst.shape[1:]) == prod(data.shape[1:k])
  - source: nki.isa.tensor_reduce docstring, section Tile size  [stated, all]
- **memset-engine-and-dtype** — Call memset with a value literal of the destination dtype (int literal for int tiles) and value=0 only for x4 packed dtypes; engine may be vector or gpsimd.
  - why: Since 0.3.0 the value type is strictly validated; the ISA memset writes one u32 pattern so packed sub-elements cannot be set to non-zero.
  - when: memset(int32_tile, 2.0); memset(fp8_x4_tile, 1).
  - fix: memset(buf, 2); for non-zero x4 data load precomputed values with dma_copy.
  - check (static): memset: type(value) matches dst.dtype class; dst.dtype endswith _x4 -> value==0
  - source: nki.isa.memset docstring; migration/index.rst memset sections  [stated, all]
- **iota-affine-select-sbuf-only-int32** — Write iota and affine_select outputs to SBUF (partition <= 128) with a pattern whose total element count equals elements per partition; iota values are int32-computed, affine_select on_false_value must be float32.
  - why: Both run on GpSimd, generate an affine value per element from [[step,num],...] (<=4-D) and cast to dst dtype.
  - when: Causal mask via affine_select into PSUM; pattern [[1,512]] for a (128,1024) dst.
  - fix: dst in SBUF; pattern product == prod(dst.shape[1:]); cast on write via dst dtype.
  - check (static): iota/affine_select: buffer(dst)==sbuf and prod(num in pattern)==prod(dst.shape[1:]) and len(pattern)<=4
  - source: nki.isa.iota and nki.isa.affine_select docstrings  [stated, all]
- **range-select-constraints** — Use range_select (trn2+) with on_false_value=FP32_MIN (-3.4028235e+38), fp32 (P,1) bounds, comp ops in {equal, less, less_equal, greater, greater_equal}, reduce_op=nl.maximum, and range_start + free index < 2^24.
  - why: The hardware fill value is fixed and comparisons run in fp32 so indices must be exactly representable.
  - when: range_select(on_false_value=-1e9) or on tiles wider than 2^24 columns offset.
  - fix: Keep the default on_false_value; cast bounds to fp32 (P,1).
  - numbers: fp32_min = -3.4028235e+38; index_limit = 2^24
  - check (static): range_select: on_false_value==-3.4028235e+38; bound dtypes fp32 and shape (P,1); nc_version>=3
  - source: nki.isa.range_select docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **select-reduce-and-predicated-copy-rules** — For select_reduce/tensor_copy_predicated keep predicate in an integer dtype (uint8/int8/uint16/int16; uint32 allowed for predicated copy), identical shapes, at most one of on_true/predicate in PSUM, scalar on_false as fp32, and reduce_op=max only.
  - why: Vector Engine predicate path reads integer masks and has a single PSUM port.
  - when: Float 0/1 masks passed as predicate; both predicate and on_true from PSUM.
  - fix: Produce masks with comparison ops using dtype=nl.uint8; evacuate one PSUM operand.
  - check (static): select_reduce: predicate.dtype in int set; not(both psum); on_true.dtype not in {tfloat32,int32,uint32}; reduce_op==maximum
  - source: nki.isa.select_reduce and tensor_copy_predicated docstrings  [stated, all]
- **dropout-dtype-rules** — For nisa.dropout keep dst.dtype == data.dtype and use an fp32 prob when data is integer.
  - why: The Vector Engine dropout path preserves dtype and reads probabilities as floats.
  - when: dropout casting bf16->fp32 in one call.
  - fix: Cast separately; prob scalar or (P,1) tile.
  - check (static): dropout: dst.dtype==data.dtype; data int -> prob.dtype==fp32
  - source: nki.isa.dropout docstring  [stated, all]
- **stream-shuffle-quadrant-rules** — Use nc_stream_shuffle only within 32-partition quadrants: same dtype and elements per partition, 32-entry mask (255 = keep), and start partitions 0 (96/128 active), 0/64 (64 active) or 0/32/64/96 (32 active).
  - why: Vector Engine cross-partition movement is limited to a quadrant with fixed base alignment.
  - when: Shuffling partition 10 to 40, or src starting at partition 16.
  - fix: Align tiles to quadrant boundaries; for arbitrary partition moves use a PE transpose/matmul with a permutation matrix.
  - numbers: quadrant = 32 partitions
  - check (static): nc_stream_shuffle: len(mask)==32; start partitions in allowed set for ceil(max(P)/32)*32
  - source: nki.isa.nc_stream_shuffle docstring  [stated, all]
- **max8-find-index8-limits** — Give max8/nc_find_index8/nc_match_replace8 between 8 and 16384 elements per partition; outputs are exactly 8 per partition (find_index8 uint32 default, sentinel 0xFFFFFFFF when absent).
  - why: Fixed-width top-8 hardware path on Vector Engine.
  - when: Top-k over 32768 columns in one call.
  - fix: Split into <=16384-column chunks and merge the 8-wide results; or use nisa.topk on GpSimd.
  - numbers: max_elems = 16384
  - check (static): max8/find_index8: 8 <= prod(src.shape[1:]) <= 16384; dst.shape[1]==8
  - source: nki.isa.max8 and nc_find_index8 docstrings  [stated, all]
- **topk-gpsimd-constraints** — Use nisa.topk with BF16 SBUF src in 16-partition snake layout, partition dim multiple of 16, 8 <= n < 65536, 1 <= K < 32768, K <= n, src free >= ceil(n/16); cost ~4n+K GpSimd cycles per partition.
  - why: GpSimd top-k reads a snake of n BF16 values across 16 partitions.
  - when: fp32 inputs or n > 65535.
  - fix: Cast to bf16 and reshape into the snake layout; derive K from val_dst free dim.
  - numbers: cost = 4*n + K GpSimd cycles/partition
  - check (static): topk: src.dtype==bf16; val_dst bf16; idx_dst uint32; shape[0]%16==0; 8<=n<65536; 1<=K<32768; K<=n; src.shape[1]>=ceil(n/16)
  - source: nki.isa.topk docstring  [stated, all]
- **local-gather-rules** — For local_gather use uint16 indices, src_buffer.shape[0]==index.shape[0] with a multiple of 16, num_elem_per_idx in {1,2,4,8,16,32}, and <= 4096 indices per GpSimd core; indices are partition offsets within each 16-partition group.
  - why: Each of 8 GpSimd cores gathers independently from its 16 connected partitions; OOB is undefined.
  - when: Gathering across the whole 128 partitions with a single index set.
  - fix: Replicate the index tile 8x across 16-partition groups; use nc_n_gather for within-partition gathers.
  - numbers: group = 16 partitions per core; max_indices_per_core = 4096
  - check (static): local_gather: index.dtype==uint16; shape[0]%16==0; num_elem_per_idx in {1,2,4,8,16,32}; indices per core <= 4096
  - source: nki.isa.local_gather docstring  [stated, all]
- **nc-n-gather-rules** — For nc_n_gather use uint32 indices in SBUF with the same partition count as data, dst dtype == data dtype, indices in [0, elems_per_partition); cost scales as ceil(elems/512) ISA groups.
  - why: GpSimd gathers within each partition over the flattened free dims; it avoids DMA entirely.
  - when: Using indirect dma_copy for in-SBUF gathers.
  - fix: nisa.nc_n_gather(dst, data, indices_u32).
  - numbers: isa_groups = ceil(elems_per_partition/512)
  - check (static): nc_n_gather: indices.dtype==uint32; all sbuf; dst.dtype==data.dtype; prod(dst.shape[1:])==prod(indices.shape[1:])
  - source: nki.isa.nc_n_gather docstring  [stated, all]
- **sequence-bounds-partition-1** — Call sequence_bounds with a partition dim of exactly 1 and fp32/int32 dtypes; output shape is (1, 2, N).
  - why: GpSimd segment scan is single-lane.
  - when: Passing (128,N) segment ids.
  - fix: Reshape so segment ids are (1,N).
  - check (static): sequence_bounds: segment_ids.shape[0]==1 and dtype in {fp32,int32}
  - source: nki.isa.sequence_bounds docstring  [stated, all]
- **rng-and-rand-rules** — Use nisa.rng for integer-dtype random bits (Vector on trn1; Vector or GpSimd on trn2+), nisa.rand2 (trn3, Vector) for uniform floats, and seed with rand_set_state using 6 (GpSimd) or 24 (Vector) uint32 elements per partition.
  - why: Different PRNG implementations per engine with different state sizes; GpSimd outputs must be SBUF.
  - when: rand2 on trn2; rng into a float tile; rand_set_state with 1 element.
  - fix: Generate uint16 bits with rng then scale, or use nl.rand wrapper.
  - numbers: xorwow_state_gpsimd = 6 uint32; xorwow_state_vector = 24 uint32
  - check (static): rng: dst.dtype int; rand2: nc_version>=4; rand_set_state: shape[1] in {6 (gpsimd), 24 (vector)}
  - source: nki.isa.rng, rand2, rand_set_state, rand_get_state docstrings  [stated, all]
- **abs-max-abs-min-trn3-only** — Use nl.abs_max/nl.abs_min (and activate2 reduce_op abs_max/abs_min) only on trn3.
  - why: These ALU ops were added in NeuronCore-v4.
  - when: abs_max in an amax-quantization kernel for trn2.
  - fix: Compute abs then maximum on trn2.
  - check (static): op in {abs_max, abs_min} implies nc_version>=4
  - source: nki.language.abs_max docstring  [stated, trn3]
- **views-cannot-touch-partition-dim** — On on-chip tensors use view ops only on free dims: permute keeps dims[0]==0, reshape keeps shape[0], flatten_dims start_dim>0, broadcast/expand_dim/squeeze_dim/reshape_dim dim != 0.
  - why: Partitions are physically separate memory banks, so a view cannot reinterpret the partition axis.
  - when: t.permute((1,0)) on an SBUF tile to 'transpose'; t.reshape((256, 64)) from (128,128).
  - fix: Use nc_transpose/dma_transpose for real transposes; keep shape[0] in reshape.
  - check (static): view op on sbuf/psum tensor: partition dim unchanged (dims[0]==0, new_shape[0]==shape[0], dim>0)
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.permute/reshape/flatten_dims/broadcast/expand_dim/squeeze_dim docstrings  [stated, all]
- **view-dtype-reinterpret-rules** — Use t.view(dtype) for byte reinterpretation only when the last dim is contiguous and (for a larger dtype) divisible by the size ratio; not after dynamic/vector select.
  - why: view() rescales the last dim by the dtype size ratio without copying.
  - when: Viewing a strided slice as uint8; viewing (128, 3) uint8 as float32.
  - fix: Make the slice contiguous (tensor_copy) or pad the last dim.
  - check (static): view(): last dim stride==1 and (itemsize_new>itemsize_old -> shape[-1] % ratio == 0) and not is_indirect
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.view docstring  [stated, all]
- **reshape-element-count-validated** — Ensure reshape preserves total element count; since 0.5.0 mismatches raise at trace time.
  - why: Earlier releases silently allowed count-changing reshapes.
  - when: Legacy kernels reshaping (128,512) to (128,256) to 'crop'.
  - fix: Use slice() for cropping and reshape only for layout changes.
  - check (static): reshape: prod(new)==prod(old)
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.reshape docstring; migration/index.rst 0.4->0.5  [stated, all]
- **dynamic-select-rules** — Use at most one dynamic select/vector_select per tensor; vector_select only on HBM tensors with dim 0; dynamic select on on-chip tensors may not target dim 0; the indirect dim cannot be further sliced or selected.
  - why: Dynamic indexing becomes a single indirect DMA descriptor dimension.
  - when: sbuf_t.select(0, idx_tensor); hbm_t.vector_select(0, idx).select(0, 3).
  - fix: Check t.is_indirect() before chaining; restructure gathers as one indirect DMA.
  - check (static): chain of dynamic selects on one tensor > 1; vector_select on non-hbm or dim!=0
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.select and vector_select docstrings  [stated, all]
- **tensor-indirection-ti-rules** — Use .indirect(index) (Tensor Indirection) only on trn3, with index an SBUF (P,K) tensor where P == tensor.shape[0]; when manually allocated the index starts on a 32-partition quadrant boundary and operands start on the same partition as their index.
  - why: TI reads/writes a column at per-element free offsets stored in a snake across partition groups (16 for vector/scalar/gpsimd, 32 for tensor engine).
  - when: indirect views on trn2; index at partition 16 for a tensor engine op.
  - fix: Gate on nc_version>=4; allocate index/operands with address=(0 or 32 or 64 or 96, ...).
  - numbers: ti_group_vector_scalar_gpsimd = 16; ti_group_tensor = 32
  - check (static): indirect(): nc_version>=4 and index.shape[0]==self.shape[0] and buffer(index)==sbuf; manual address partition % 32 == 0
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.indirect docstring; nki.isa.* 'Tensor indirection' sections  [stated, trn3]
- **slice-semantics** — Slice with 0 <= start < end <= shape[dim], step >= 1, and never slice a dimension participating in an indirection.
  - why: slice() is a strided view; invalid ranges fail at trace time, and indirect dims are opaque.
  - when: Negative or reversed slices; slicing the vector_select dim.
  - fix: Compute explicit bounds with min(); use Python slice objects for bounds-safe tiling.
  - check (static): slice(): 0<=start<end<=shape[dim] and step>=1 and dim not indirect
  - source: nki.language.NkiTensor.slice docstring  [stated, all]
- **tile-size-deprecated-attributes** — Use nl.tile_size.psum_bank_fmax and sbuf_fmax_bytes/sbuf_size_bytes instead of the deprecated psum_fmax and total_available_sbuf_size.
  - why: psum_fmax is misnamed (it is per bank, not per partition) and total_available_sbuf_size returns per-partition bytes despite its name.
  - when: Kernels computing PSUM budgets from psum_fmax * psum_num_banks or total SBUF from total_available_sbuf_size.
  - fix: Replace attribute names; multiply psum_bank_fmax by psum_num_banks for the whole PSUM.
  - check (static): attribute access tile_size.psum_fmax or tile_size.total_available_sbuf_size
  - source: nki.language.tile_size rst and _tile_size.py deprecation notes  [stated, all]
- **tile-size-target-dependent-needs-kernel-context** — Read target-dependent constants (psum_num_banks, sbuf_fmax, sbuf_fmax_bytes, sbuf_size_bytes, get_nc_version) only inside a traced kernel or with a target set; at module import they raise 'No backend set'.
  - why: These are properties resolved from the compile target; the static ones (pmax, gemm_*_fmax, psum_bank_fmax, bn_stats_fmax) are plain ints.
  - when: Module-level constants like FMAX = nl.tile_size.sbuf_fmax crashing at import.
  - fix: Compute inside the @nki.jit function or hard-code per target with NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE.
  - check (static): module-level access of tile_size.{psum_num_banks,sbuf_fmax,sbuf_fmax_bytes,sbuf_size_bytes,total_available_sbuf_size} or nisa.get_nc_version()
  - source: introspection: nl.tile_size property access raised RuntimeError('No backend set'); _tile_size.py  [stated, all]
- **output-tensors-shared-hbm** — Allocate kernel output (returned) tensors with buffer=nl.shared_hbm; nl.hbm/nl.private_hbm outputs fail compilation.
  - why: Returned tensors must be visible to the host and to both cores under LNC2.
  - when: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.hbm); return out.
  - fix: buffer=nl.shared_hbm.
  - check (static): returned tensor buffer == shared_hbm
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Output tensors must use nl.shared_hbm'  [stated, all]
- **loops-dynamic-range-while-deprecated** — Replace 'for i in nl.dynamic_range(reg)' with nl.fori_loop(lo, hi, body) and bare 'while reg:' with nl.while_loop(reg, body).
  - why: Both old constructs are deprecated in 0.6.0 and unsupported by the tracer frontend (registers have no value at trace time).
  - when: TypeError from int()/range() on a VirtualRegister; deprecation warnings.
  - fix: def body(i): ...; nl.fori_loop(0, reg, body); def wbody(r): ...; return r; nl.while_loop(reg, wbody).
  - check (static): use of nl.dynamic_range or Python while on VirtualRegister
  - source: migration/index.rst 0.5->0.6; nki.isa.VirtualRegister docstring note  [stated, all]
- **loops-fori-rules** — In fori_loop/while_loop keep the step a positive compile-time int, treat the loop register as read-only (use it via .ap(scalar_offset=i)), carry state through SBUF/HBM, declare tensors used after the loop outside the body, and never nest these loops in nl.no_reorder().
  - why: The body is compiled once into a sequencer branch loop; Python arithmetic on the register and tensors allocated inside the body are not visible outside.
  - when: idx = i*128 in Python; accumulators created inside body and read after.
  - fix: Pre-scale by setting pattern stride; allocate accumulators before the loop and update in place.
  - check (static): fori_loop: step is int > 0; body_fun returns None; no Python arithmetic on VirtualRegister; not inside no_reorder
  - source: nki.language.fori_loop and while_loop docstrings; migration/index.rst 'Rules for migrated loops'  [stated, all]
- **register-budget-64-per-engine** — Budget at most 64 32-bit registers per engine sequencer for VirtualRegisters; register_load/register_store move single-element ([1] or [1,1]) tensors only.
  - why: Each of Tensor/Scalar/Vector/GpSimd/Sync sequencers has 64 scalar registers on NeuronCore v2-v4; the compiler allocates physical registers per engine.
  - when: Dozens of live loop registers; register_load from a (1,8) tile.
  - fix: Keep few live registers; materialize others to SBUF with register_store.
  - numbers: registers_per_engine = 64 x 32-bit
  - check (static): register_load/store: prod(src.shape)==1
  - source: nki.isa.register_alloc/register_load/register_store docstrings  [stated, all]
- **mig-neuronxcc-namespace-forbidden** — Import nki, nki.language as nl, nki.isa as nisa, nki.collectives; never import neuronxcc.nki.* inside kernels.
  - why: The legacy namespace raises a compilation error since NKI 0.4.0 (the package is still importable but is the old 0.1.0 API).
  - when: from neuronxcc import nki / import neuronxcc.nki.language as nl.
  - fix: Replace imports; follow the 0.1->0.2 migration (dst-first ISA calls, no mask/mgrid/arange).
  - check (static): import of neuronxcc.nki
  - source: migration/index.rst 'neuronxcc.nki.* inside kernels - now a compilation error'  [stated, all]
- **mig-isa-dst-first-no-return** — Call every nisa instruction with dst as the first (explicit) argument; instructions return an NkiInstruction handle, not the result tile.
  - why: Since 0.2.0 ISA APIs write into a pre-allocated destination to avoid hidden copies and to express accumulation.
  - when: out = nisa.tensor_tensor(a, b, nl.add) / result[...] = nisa.reciprocal(x).
  - fix: nisa.tensor_tensor(dst=out, data1=a, data2=b, op=nl.add).
  - check (static): nisa.* call result assigned to a tensor or used as operand
  - source: migration/index.rst 'All ISA functions require a destination parameter'  [stated, all]
- **mig-mask-mgrid-arange-removed** — Do not use nl.mgrid, nl.arange or the mask= parameter; use integer slices (with min()) and .ap() for strided/dynamic patterns.
  - why: These 0.1.0 indexing mechanisms were removed; slicing covers in-bounds tiling.
  - when: i_p, i_f = nl.mgrid[0:128, 0:512]; op(..., mask=(i_p < n)).
  - fix: p = slice(i*128, min(N, (i+1)*128)); nisa.tensor_copy(dst[p, f], src[p, f]).
  - check (static): use of nl.mgrid/nl.arange/mask kwarg
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Deprecation of masking', 'Update indexing syntax'  [stated, all]
- **mig-enums-and-buffer-objects** — Pass enum members (nisa.dge_mode.hwdge, nisa.engine.vector, nl.sbuf) rather than ints or strings for dge_mode/engine/oob_mode/reduce_cmd/buffer parameters.
  - why: Raw integer enum values and string buffer names are rejected since 0.3.0.
  - when: dge_mode=2, buffer='sbuf'.
  - fix: Use the named members; nl.ndarray buffer defaults to nl.sbuf.
  - check (static): enum kwarg is int or buffer kwarg is str
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Integer enum constants', 'String buffer names'  [stated, all]
- **mig-jit-kwargs-removed** — Do not pass platform_target= or mode= to @nki.jit; set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE (trn1|inf2|gen2, trn2|gen3, trn3|gen4) and let argument types select torch/jax/numpy execution.
  - why: platform_target raises since 0.3.0 and mode is ignored; framework is detected from args.
  - when: @nki.jit(platform_target='trn2', mode='baremetal').
  - fix: @nki.jit plus env var; nki.simulate for CPU runs.
  - check (static): nki.jit kwargs contain platform_target or mode
  - source: migration/index.rst 'nki.jit(platform_target=...)', 'nki.jit(mode=...)'; nki.jit docstring  [stated, all]
- **mig-no-benchmark-baremetal-profile** — Do not call nki.benchmark, nki.baremetal or nki.profile (absent in 0.6.0); run with @nki.jit on numpy inputs, nki.simulate for CPU, nki.compiler.parallel_compile for batch builds, and neuron-profile for timing.
  - why: The 0.1.0 decorators were dropped with the new compiler; nki exposes jit, simulate, debug, Kernel, compiler.
  - when: AttributeError: module 'nki' has no attribute 'benchmark'.
  - fix: Replace with nki.jit + external timing / neuron-profile.
  - check (static): attribute access nki.benchmark/baremetal/profile
  - source: introspection: dir(nki) == [Kernel, debug, jit, simulate, compiler, ...]  [stated, all]
- **mig-sub-kernel-no-decorator** — Decorate only the top-level kernel with @nki.jit; helper functions called from a kernel must be plain Python functions.
  - why: Nested decorated functions trigger 'classes need to inherit from nl.NKIObject' errors at the call site.
  - when: @nki.jit on tiled helper functions.
  - fix: Remove decorators; apply nki.jit(helper) at a standalone call site if needed.
  - check (static): nki.jit-decorated function called inside another nki.jit function
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Remove nki.jit decorator on sub-kernels'  [stated, all]
- **mig-python-subset-restrictions** — Avoid keyword-only '*' separators, 'is'/'is not' comparisons, list-typed kernel arguments, nested slicing, and non-string dict keys in kernels.
  - why: The NKI compiler parses a Python subset; these constructs fail at compile time.
  - when: def k(x, *, flag=True); if cfg is None; stride=[1,1].
  - fix: Use ==/!=, tuples, plain defaults, string dict keys.
  - check (static): AST of kernel contains kwonly separator, Is/IsNot, list args
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Language restrictions'; 0.1->0.2 feature list  [stated, all]
- **mig-renamed-parameters** — Use the 0.3.0+ signatures: affine_select(..., offset=) as keyword, register_move(dst, src) with src a VirtualRegister, sendrecv(dma_engine=nisa.dma_engine.*), dma_compute(dst, srcs, reduce_op, scales=None, unique_indices=True), and collective_permute_implicit(channel_ids=[...]) instead of num_channels.
  - why: Parameter positions/names changed in 0.3.0 and old call sites break silently or loudly.
  - when: affine_select(dst, pattern, offset, cm, ...) positional; register_move(dst, imm=42).
  - fix: Update call sites per the migration table.
  - check (static): register_move with imm kwarg; sendrecv with use_gpsimd_dma; *_rank_id with num_channels
  - source: migration/index.rst 0.2->0.3 API breaking changes  [stated, all]
- **mig-tensor-copy-dynamic-removed** — Replace nisa.tensor_copy_dynamic_src/_dst with nisa.tensor_copy on a .ap(..., scalar_offset=reg, indirect_dim=d) view.
  - why: The dynamic copy APIs were removed in 0.4.0.
  - when: AttributeError on tensor_copy_dynamic_src.
  - fix: nisa.tensor_copy(dst=out, src=src.ap(pattern, scalar_offset=idx, indirect_dim=1)).
  - check (static): call to nisa.tensor_copy_dynamic_src/_dst
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Removed APIs'  [stated, all]
- **mig-defaults-changed** — Rely on 0.3.0+ defaults: nl.ndarray/zeros buffer=nl.sbuf, program_id(axis=0), num_programs(axes=0), iota offset=0, core_barrier engine=gpsimd.
  - why: Several parameter defaults changed; code passing None for buffer now errors.
  - when: nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=None).
  - fix: Omit buffer or pass nl.sbuf.
  - check (static): buffer=None passed to creation ops
  - source: migration/index.rst 'Parameter default value updates'  [stated, all]
- **get-nc-version-inside-kernel** — Call nisa.get_nc_version()/get_nc_sub_version() inside the kernel to branch per generation (gen2=trn1/inf2, gen3=trn2, gen4=trn3; sub-version 0=trn3pre, 1=trn3).
  - why: The target context only exists during tracing/compilation.
  - when: Module-level version checks raising 'No backend set'.
  - fix: if nisa.get_nc_version() == nisa.nc_version.gen4: use exponential/activate2.
  - check (static): get_nc_version called outside @nki.jit body
  - source: nki.isa.get_nc_version/get_nc_sub_version docstrings; nki/compiler/target.py  [stated, all]
- **nl-wrappers-experimental** — Treat nl.* compute wrappers (softmax, rms_norm, matmul, transpose, load_transpose2d, gather_flattened, broadcast_to, where, dropout, ...) as experimental; for production kernels express the same work with nisa instructions and explicit tiles.
  - why: They are marked <<experimental>> and allocate intermediate tiles implicitly, hiding engine choice and PSUM/SBUF placement.
  - when: Performance or placement surprises from nl.softmax inside a tight loop.
  - fix: Build softmax from activation(exp, reduce)+reciprocal+tensor_scalar.
  - source: nki.language.* docstrings (<<experimental>> markers)  [stated, all]
- **dge-hwdge-transpose-constraints** — For dma_transpose with hwdge, make src.shape[0] == 16, src.shape[-1] % 128 == 0 and dtype 2 bytes.
  - why: Hardware DGE transpose descriptors are fixed to the 16-row cooperative tile and 128-wide output.
  - when: dma_transpose(..., dge_mode=hwdge) with other shapes.
  - fix: Tile the source into [16, 128k] bf16/fp16 pieces or let the compiler choose the mode.
  - numbers: src_shape0 = 16; src_last_dim = multiple of 128; dtype = 2 bytes
  - check (static): check src.shape[0]==16 and src.shape[-1]%128==0 and dtype_bytes==2.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: hwdge  [stated, trn2]
- **dge-swdge-indirect-transpose-constraints** — For indirect (gather) dma_transpose under swdge: src on HBM, src.shape[-1] <= 128, 2-byte dtype, src.shape[0] % 16 == 0, 2-D uint32 SBUF index tensor with shape[0] in [16,128] divisible by 16 (exactly 128 when indices.shape[1] > 1); NeuronCore-v3+ only.
  - why: Software DGE indirect-transpose descriptors are generated per 16-row group with a 128-wide limit.
  - when: Gather+transpose of K/V cache rows by a runtime index list.
  - fix: src_ap = hbm.ap(pattern=[[P,F],[1,P]], vector_offset=idx_u32, indirect_dim=0); nisa.dma_transpose(dst, src_ap, dge_mode=swdge)
  - numbers: src_last_dim = <= 128; src_shape0 = multiple of 16; index_rows = [16,128], multiple of 16
  - check (static): validate the listed shape/dtype constraints.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dge.rst :: swdge  [stated, trn2]
- **dge-vector-select-constraints** — Use vector_select/vector_offset only on HBM sources with indirect_dim=0; the output partition count equals the index vector length and only one dynamic select is allowed per view.
  - why: Hardware indirect DMA gathers whole rows: partition p reads row offsets[p]; the leading-dim stride is taken from the base tensor shape (pattern stride ignored) and the selected dim cannot be further sliced.
  - when: Gather implemented with indirect_dim != 0 or chained selects.
  - fix: src = A.vector_select(0, offsets[P,1]); nisa.dma_copy(dst=sbuf[P, cols], src=src)
  - check (static): validate indirect_dim==0, source buffer is HBM, no chained select.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Vector Dynamic Access  [stated, all]
- **sched-no-reorder-inside-dynamic-loop** — Place nl.no_reorder() blocks inside a dynamic_range body, never around the dynamic loop.
  - why: dynamic_range loops inside no_reorder are unsupported and error; the reverse nesting is allowed.
  - when: with nl.no_reorder(): for i in nl.dynamic_range(n): ...
  - fix: for i in nl.dynamic_range(n): with nl.no_reorder(): ...
  - check (static): AST check for dynamic_range nested in no_reorder.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-dynamic-loops.rst :: Interaction with no_reorder  [stated, all]
- **api-ap-not-composable** — Do not chain .ap() calls expecting composition: the outer .ap() addresses raw storage and fully overrides the inner one; use slice/reshape/permute/select views to compose.
  - why: ap() interprets pattern/offset against the underlying storage, ignoring the view it is called on.
  - when: inner = t.ap(...); outer = inner.ap(...)
  - fix: t.slice(...).slice(...) or compute one .ap() from the base tensor.
  - check (static): flag .ap() invoked on a tensor that is itself an .ap() result.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Composition and .ap on a view  [stated, all]
- **api-ap-pattern-order** — Write .ap() patterns as [[step, num], ...] from major to minor with the partition tuple first; the profiler displays them in reverse (hardware) order.
  - why: The NKI pattern order is opposite to what the hardware accepts, so profiler strings like [1,1,1][1,1,1] read minor-first.
  - when: Comparing profiler access patterns to source patterns.
  - fix: Reverse mentally when reading 'fp32@0x4000[strides][shape]' in Neuron Explorer.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: NKI API for the Access Pattern  [stated, all]
- **api-dynamic-select-rules** — Allow only one dynamic select per view, never on the partition dim of SBUF/PSUM tensors, and do not further slice the selected dimension.
  - why: Hardware indirect addressing applies one scalar or vector offset on a single indirect_dim.
  - when: A.select(0, idx).select(1, idx2) or sbuf_tile.select(0, idx).
  - fix: Resolve one index on device and the rest statically; use NkiTensor.is_indirect() to test.
  - check (static): count dynamic selects per view; check dim != 0 for SBUF/PSUM.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-aps.rst :: Scalar Dynamic Access  [stated, all]
- **api-register-alloc-immediate** — Initialize VirtualRegisters only with immediate ints (nisa.register_alloc(0)) and load runtime values with nisa.register_load(reg, tensor); uninitialized tensors used as loop conditions must be explicitly memset/dma'd.
  - why: Memory allocation does not initialize; register_alloc takes an optional immediate, not a tensor.
  - when: while reg: loops reading garbage conditions.
  - fix: zero = nl.zeros((1,1), nl.int32, nl.sbuf); nisa.dma_copy(dst=cond_hbm, src=zero); reg = nisa.register_alloc(1); ... nisa.register_load(reg, cond)
  - check (static): flag register_alloc(tensor) and reads of ndarray never written.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Direct Hardware Control; Control Flow Constructs  [stated, all]
- **api-kernel-io-hbm** — Pass kernel inputs/outputs as HBM tensors; load into SBUF before compute and allocate outputs with buffer=nl.shared_hbm (or nl.hbm).
  - why: NKI kernel parameters must be HBM references; host memory is not directly accessible.
  - when: Returning an SBUF tile from a kernel.
  - fix: out = nl.ndarray(shape, dtype, buffer=nl.shared_hbm); nisa.dma_copy(dst=out, src=sbuf_tile); return out

- **registers-only-for-loop-control** — Use register instructions (register_alloc(x=...), register_move(dst, src=...), register_load, register_store) only for dynamic loop bounds and while conditions, never for tensor arithmetic; imm= on register_move is removed.

- **output-proj-tkg-constraints** — For output_projection_tkg keep B*S <= 128, D <= 128, H divisible by LNC and by 512*LNC (or 128*LNC with TRANSPOSE_OUT), and N*H <= 81920 (fp32) / 163840 (16-bit) when TRANSPOSE_OUT.

- **output-proj-cte-constraints** — Use output_projection_cte with S >= 512 (smaller S degrades), attention [B,N,D,S], D <= 128, H <= 32768 (validated 20705), H divisible by LNC; fp32 may not fit SBUF.

- **attention-cte-scale-constraint** — Pre-scale Q by softmax_scale on the caller side and pass scale=1.0 when using sliding window, context parallel or prefix caching in attention_cte.
  - why: Those modes require scale == 1.0 inside the kernel.
  - when: Ring attention / SWA / prefix caching with attention_cte.

- **attention-cte-layouts** — Pass attention_cte q as (B, d, S_q) (tp_q=False, d on partitions) or (B, S_q, d) with tp_q=True for an internal DMA transpose; v is always (B_kv, S_kv, d); d <= 128.
  - why: QK^T contracts on d; PV contracts on S_kv so V keeps S on partitions.

- **attention-mxfp8-tkg-layout-differs** — Note that attention_mxfp8_tkg (trn3) puts q_heads H on the partition axis for packed-Q eviction, unlike attention_tkg which puts d on partitions; it requires q_head == 64, d_head == 128 and bucket >= 2048 tokens.

## Compiler flags and options (22)

- **simulator-precise-fp-default** — Expect nki.simulate to model bf16/fp8 precisely by default (NKI_PRECISE_FP=1) and to reproduce hardware sin extrapolation; set NKI_PRECISE_FP=0 only to restore fp32 approximation.
  - why: Since 0.4.0 the CPU simulator defaults to precise low-precision emulation.
  - when: Simulator/hardware mismatches attributed to the kernel when they come from precision mode.
  - fix: Run NKI_SIMULATOR=1 or nki.simulate(kernel)(...) with default precision; compare with rtol per dtype.
  - source: migration/index.rst 0.3->0.4 'CPU simulator precision default'; nki.api.shared.rst act note  [stated, all]
- **address-rotation-default-on** — Leave address rotation enabled (default) so multi-buffered tensors rotate addresses; disable with Kernel.disable_address_rotation() only when manual addresses must be stable.
  - why: Address rotation lets the compiler give loop-iteration copies of a tensor different physical addresses, enabling overlap.
  - when: Debugging with manual addresses while rotation moves buffers.
  - fix: kernel = nki.jit(fn).disable_address_rotation().
  - source: nki.Kernel docstring (address_rotation=True default)  [stated, all]
- **lnc-barrier-checker** — Compile LNC2 kernels with Kernel.enable_core_barrier_checker() during development to fail compilation on cross-PNC races.
  - why: The checker compares all memory accesses across the two PNCs and reports write/read overlaps lacking a barrier on a common engine.
  - when: Intermittent wrong results in LNC2 kernels.
  - fix: kernel = nki.jit(fn).enable_core_barrier_checker(); disable for production builds.
  - source: nki.Kernel.enable_core_barrier_checker docstring  [stated, trn2]
- **compiler-version-guard** — Guard version-specific code with nki.compiler.get_compiler_version() (0.6.0 -> major 0, minor 6).
  - why: Beta/0.x releases change APIs; the version call lets kernels branch.
  - when: Kernels that must run on 0.5 and 0.6.
  - fix: v = nki.compiler.get_compiler_version(); if v.minor >= 6: use fori_loop.
  - numbers: nki_0.6.0 = major 0 minor 6
  - source: nki.compiler.get_compiler_version docstring  [stated, all]
- **simulate-and-env-flags** — Run CPU simulation via nki.simulate(kernel)(numpy args) or NKI_SIMULATOR=1, select target with NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE, and use nl.device_print(prefix, tensor) with NEURON_RT_DEBUG_OUTPUT_DIR for on-device dumps.
  - why: These env vars drive frontend target resolution and runtime debug streams; device_print prefix must be a constant string.
  - when: Simulation on a laptop without target set defaulting to hardware detection.
  - fix: export NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE=trn2; nki.simulate(kernel[lnc])(...).
  - source: nki.simulate, nki.jit, nki.language.device_print docstrings; nki/compiler/target.py  [stated, all]
- **parallel-compile-api** — Use nki.compiler.parallel_compile(kernel_specs, compile_opts_dict={'target': ...}, artifacts_base_dir, max_workers) with unique config_ids for sweeping kernel hyperparameters.
  - why: It compiles variants in worker processes and returns CompilationResult entries with neff_path, times and estimated_utilization.
  - when: Sequential compile loops for autotuning.
  - fix: Build KernelSpec(kernel_module, kernel_func_name, inputs, outputs, hyperparams, config_id).
  - source: nki.compiler.parallel_compile/KernelSpec/CompilationResult docstrings  [stated, all]
- **lnc-flags-must-match** — Compile with --lnc (or --logical-nc-config) equal to the runtime NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG; only 1 or 2 are valid and 2 is the trn2 default.
  - why: The compiler shards the graph for the LNC degree; a mismatch with the runtime grouping is unsupported.
  - when: Kernel tested with NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=1 but compiled with -lnc 2.
  - fix: torch_neuronx.trace(..., compiler_args='--lnc=1') with os.environ['NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG']='1'.
  - numbers: valid_values = 1 or 2; trn2_default = 2; trn2_lnc2_cores_per_instance = 64; trn2_lnc1_cores_per_instance = 128
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/logical-neuroncore-config.rst :: Compiler and runtime settings  [stated, trn2]
- **cf-profiling-env-vars** — Set NEURON_FRAMEWORK_DEBUG=1 (save NEFF), XLA_IR_DEBUG=1 and XLA_HLO_DEBUG=1 before compiling to get profiler source mapping, then capture with neuron-explorer capture --profile-nth-exec=2.
  - why: The NEFF carries instructions and debug metadata; the second execution avoids one-time warmup effects.
  - when: Preparing a profile.
  - fix: neuron-explorer capture -n ./compiler_workdir/graph.neff -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2; neuron-explorer view --data-path ./ws (ports 3001/3002).
  - source: nki/guides/use-neuron-profile.rst :: Step 1-3  [stated, all]
- **cf-platform-target-override** — Set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE=trn2 (or trn3) when compiling kernels on a host without the target device so generation-specific features (hwdge, double FP8, transpose mode) are selected.
  - why: Tutorial kernels set this at import; the compiler chooses DGE modes and instruction variants by target.
  - when: Compiling on a CPU-only box.
  - fix: os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE'] = 'trn2'
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Starting simple; nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Example 2  [stated, all]
- **cf-auto-cast-and-int64** — Control graph-level precision with --auto-cast / --auto-cast-type (FP32 -> BF16 by default) and integer behavior with --native-int64 (trn2+) and --implicit-integer-downcast.
  - why: The Neuron compiler auto-converts FP32 models to BF16 and 64-bit ints to 32-bit unless told otherwise; accuracy should be benchmarked.
  - when: Unexpected bf16 inputs arriving at a kernel expecting fp32, or int64 indices truncated.
  - fix: Pass explicit compiler_args in torch_neuronx.trace.
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/data-types.rst :: Model Type Conversion; Integer Type Conversion  [stated, all]
- **cf-nki-compiler-preserves-choices** — Expect the NKI compiler to keep your instruction order, allocation and engine choices; it only does light middle/back-end passes and is inserted late into the graph compile.
  - why: NKI is compiled per kernel to NKI IR (MLIR) and spliced into the Neuron IR late so the Graph Compiler cannot undo kernel decisions.
  - when: Relying on the graph compiler to fix a poorly scheduled kernel.
  - fix: Optimize explicitly in the kernel (engine selection, tile sizes, buffering).
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki-compiler.rst :: Integration; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: NKI Compiler  [stated, all]
- **cf-persistent-cache** — Expect recompiles to hit the on-disk Neuron Persistent Cache at /var/tmp/neuron-compile-cache; clear it when changing kernels that produce identical graph hashes.
  - why: torch-neuronx caches compiled NEFFs by graph hash across runs.
  - when: Stale kernel behavior after edits.
  - fix: Remove the cache entry or change the graph.
  - numbers: cache_path = /var/tmp/neuron-compile-cache
  - source: about-neuron/arch/neuron-features/neuron-caching.rst  [stated, all]
- **psum-bank-7-reserved-when-dma-transpose-lowered** — If NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE=true, restrict manual PSUM allocation to banks 0-6: the compiler lowers dma_transpose to an identity matmul that uses bank 7 as scratch.
  - why: Otherwise the kernel's bank-7 accumulator is clobbered.
  - when: Manual PSUM addressing with that env var set.
  - fix: num_banks = 7 if os.environ.get('NKI_DMA_TRANSPOSE_AS_PE_TRANSPOSE','').lower()=='true' else 8
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/nkilib/core/utils/kernel_helpers.py _psum_num_banks  [stated, trn2/trn3]
- **skip-middle-end-and-manual-alloc-flags** — When hand-scheduling with manual SBUF/PSUM addresses (old API), decorate with @nki.compiler.skip_middle_end_transformations and pass --internal-skip-backend-allocation-opt-nki --disable-internal-io-dge; otherwise the compiler re-allocates and breaks the pipeline.
  - why: Middle-end transforms and backend allocation undo manual buffer placement; IO DGE adds descriptor overhead for static IO.
  - when: Fully manual kernels on internal builds.
  - fix: @nki.compiler.skip_middle_end_transformations
@nki.baremetal(artifacts_dir='debug', additional_compile_opt='--internal-skip-backend-allocation-opt-nki --disable-internal-io-dge')
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/pipelined_attention.py (old API, internal nightly only)  [stated, unknown]
- **lnc1-for-debugging-lnc2-default** — Debug and profile with --lnc 1 (single NeuronCore) and only switch to the default --lnc 2 (trn2/trn3) when explicitly targeting multi-core execution.
  - why: Single-core compilation gives simpler error messages, faster compiles, and bounds analysis currently assumes single-core kernels.
  - when: Developing or profiling a new kernel on trn2/trn3.
  - fix: os.environ['NEURON_CC_FLAGS'] = '--target trn2 --lnc 1'.
  - numbers: default_lnc_trn2_trn3 = 2
  - check (static): check NEURON_CC_FLAGS contains --lnc 1 in debug/profiling harnesses
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-debugging/references/compiler-flags.md :: --lnc (Logical NeuronCore); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profiling/SKILL.md :: Step 1  [stated, all]
- **target-flag-and-platform-override-must-match** — Set NEURON_CC_FLAGS --target and NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE to the same platform (trn1/trn1n/inf2/trn2/trn3) and do not pass platform_target= or mode= to @nki.jit.
  - why: @nki.jit(platform_target=...) and mode= were removed in NKI 0.3.0; the env var is the only override and the compiler auto-detects the framework from arguments.
  - when: @nki.jit(platform_target='trn2') or mismatched env vars.
  - fix: os.environ['NEURON_CC_FLAGS']='--target trn2 --lnc 1'; os.environ['NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE']='trn2'; plain @nki.jit.
  - numbers: generations = trn1/trn1n/inf2=gen2, trn2=gen3, trn3=gen4
