  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-debugging/SKILL.md :: Platform Target Mapping; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-writing/references/nki-language-constraint.md :: Hard Rules — Beta 2 → NKI 0.3.0  [stated, all]
- **pin-cores-and-isolate-outputs** — Pin each concurrent process to its own NeuronCore with NEURON_RT_VISIBLE_CORES and give it a unique NEURON_RT_INSPECT_OUTPUT_DIR.
  - why: Concurrent agents/processes on shared cores cause device contention, skewed latency and NEFF/NTFF collisions.
  - when: Multiple kernels being compiled/profiled on the same host.

  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-debugging/references/neuron-core-isolation.md  [stated, all]
- **verbose-only-when-investigating** — Add --verbose=info (or debug) only when inspecting compiler behaviour; read log-neuron-cc.txt in /tmp/$USER/neuroncc_compile_workdir/<uuid>/ for allocation and optimization decisions.
  - why: Verbose modes increase compile time; the workdir log is where memory-allocation and pass information appears.
  - when: Unexpected codegen, spills, or performance anomalies.

- **simulator-env-var-torch-only** — Run PyTorch scripts under NKI_SIMULATOR=1 to execute every @nki.jit kernel on the CPU simulator with no code changes; for JAX call nki.simulate(kernel)(...) explicitly.
  - why: NKI_SIMULATOR=1 does not currently support JAX.

- **platform-target-override-values** — Set NEURON_PLATFORM_TARGET_OVERRIDE to trn1/gen2, trn2/gen3 or trn3/gen4 explicitly; when unset the simulator auto-detects and otherwise defaults to trn3.
  - why: Instruction constraints and defaults differ per NeuronCore generation.

- **only-isa-and-dynamic-range-survive-specialization** — Write kernels knowing that every for/if/while and Python expression is evaluated at specialization time; only nki.isa.* calls and dynamic_range loops become device operations.
  - why: The compiler unrolls loops, inlines calls and resolves branches, producing a flat ISA sequence; print() runs at compile time.
  - when: Large trip counts or runtime-dependent bounds.

  - source: nki/get-started/nki-language-guide.rst :: Compilation Model; nki/get-started/about/index.rst :: Scheduling options for loops  [stated, all]
- **skip-middle-end-transformations** — Disable the compiler's heuristic middle-end loop reordering/fusion (skip_middle_end_transformations) for hand-tuned kernels whose loop structure is deliberate.
  - why: Those passes are unpredictable and can undo manual tiling decisions.

  - fix: Set the skip_middle_end_transformations directive on the kernel.
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Kernel Code Details  [stated, all]

## Reading a profile: diagnosis rules (49)

- **mm-profiler-two-instructions** — Expect each nc_matmul to appear as two ISA instructions in neuron-profile: a stationary load followed by a multiply.
  - why: The stationary operand is latched into the PE array by a separate load instruction; both show up for a single API call.
  - when: Instruction counts in the profile are ~2x the number of nc_matmul calls; stationary reloads dominate when the stationary tile changes every call.
  - fix: Keep the stationary operand fixed across consecutive matmuls (loop over moving tiles innermost) to amortize loads.
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul docstring, section Profiler view syntax  [stated, all]
- **nki-debug-lnc2-replay** — Debug device/simulator mismatches with nki.debug(kernel, dump_dir=NEURON_RT_DEBUG_OUTPUT_DIR)(args) and breakpoint() in the kernel; for LNC2 both cores run as threads and only core_id stops.
  - why: nki.debug replays the kernel in simulation while loading device dumps for tensor.sim_value vs device_value comparison.
  - when: Hardware NaNs not reproduced in nki.simulate.
  - fix: Set NEURON_RT_DEBUG_OUTPUT_DIR on the device run, then nki.debug(..., interactive=True).
  - numbers: rtol = 1e-2; atol = 1e-1
  - source: nki.debug docstring  [stated, all]
- **profiler-isa-syntax** — Read neuron-profile matmul rows as src=<dtype>@<addr>[strides][nums] dst=... M*K acc_flags=<f> psum_zero=<v>; acc_flags=2 means accumulator reset, and MX operands show as $MX[data,scale,start_scale_partition].
  - why: The profiler prints compact ISA operand syntax; acc_flags reveals whether accumulation groups were formed as intended.
  - when: Diagnosing unexpected PSUM resets or missing accumulation.
  - fix: Check acc_flags on consecutive matmuls of one K-loop: only the first should reset.
  - source: nki.isa.nc_matmul and nc_matmul_mx docstrings, Profiler view syntax  [stated, all]
- **dge-profile-queue-names** — Read the DMA queue name in the profiler to learn how a DMA was generated: qGpSimdDynamic means swdge (GpSimd-generated), qSyncIO* static/sync-triggered, qSyncSpillReload* compiler spills.
  - why: The queue ID is tied to the trigger engine and the descriptor-generation method; the trigger instruction can be found on the corresponding engine trace.
  - when: Diagnosing which engine is paying for descriptor generation.
  - fix: Click the DMA in Neuron Explorer, note the queue, then locate the trigger instruction on that engine's trace.
  - source: nki/get-started/about/nki-dma-overview.rst :: Example 2 Profile; nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #4  [stated, all]
- **dge-enable-dge-notifs** — Capture profiles with --enable-dge-notifs to see DGE DMA events, but expect notification-queue overflow and timeouts when the kernel issues very many DGE instructions.
  - why: DGE DMA events are not recorded by default; the notification queue has limited capacity.
  - when: Profiling hwdge-heavy kernels.
  - fix: neuron-explorer capture -n graph.neff -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2 --enable-dge-notifs; drop the flag if execution times out.
  - source: nki/guides/use-neuron-profile.rst :: Step 3: Profile the Generated NEFF  [stated, trn2]
- **mm-transpose-share-check** — When TensorE looks saturated, color the Device Timeline by tensor_instruction_type and measure how much is Transpose vs Regular before optimizing matmuls.
  - why: Transposes are 'not useful' TensorE work; a large red share means layout fixes (IO layout, operand swap, alternative engine) beat matmul tuning.
  - when: TensorE > 90% busy but MFU low.
  - fix: Reduce IO transposes by choosing kernel IO layout; reduce intermediate transposes by operand swap or engine choice.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #8  [stated, all]
- **mem-spill-metrics** — If Spill Save Bytes exceeds ~30% of Sbuf Read Bytes (or Spill Reload Bytes ~30% of Sbuf Write Bytes) in the Summary tab, fuse operators or shrink blocks.
  - why: The compiler spills intermediates to a TMPBUF in HBM and reloads them via qSyncSpillReload queues when SBUF overflows; this traffic competes with useful DMA.
  - when: Summary data_movement metrics; instructions waiting on qSyncSpillReload.
  - fix: Loop-fuse producer/consumer so each tile goes load -> op0 -> op1 -> store; reduce oversized blocks.
  - numbers: spill_fraction_threshold = ~30%
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #2  [stated, all]
- **prof-bound-targets** — Drive optimization until the Summary tab shows either a compute engine >= 90% active (compute-bound) or MBU >= 60% (memory-bound); matmul kernels should also approach 100% MFU.
  - why: These are the practical 'done' thresholds the performance guide uses; 100% is the ideal.
  - when: Summary tab engine/dma_active_time_percent, MBU, MFU.
  - fix: If neither threshold is met, follow Opt #1-#10 in order: arithmetic intensity, engine idle gaps, engine efficiency, DMA efficiency.
  - numbers: compute_bound_target = >= 90% engine active; memory_bound_target = >= 60% MBU
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Introduction  [stated, all]
- **prof-engine-semaphore-wait** — Diagnose each engine idle gap by the semaphore wait of the first instruction after it: a semaphore named after an engine (Vector/Scalar/GpSimd/Tensor) means a cross-engine dependency; a name starting with q means a DMA (qSyncIO* = loads, qSyncSpillReload* = spills).
  - why: Compiler-inserted semaphores encode data dependencies; the wait condition identifies the producer.
  - when: Visible idle gaps on the bottleneck engine.
  - fix: Engine wait -> tile the pipeline (Opt #3); DMA wait -> prefetch/overlap (Opt #4) or fix DMA efficiency (Opt #9); spill wait -> fuse (Opt #2).
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Reducing engine idle time / Opt #3 / Opt #4  [stated, all]
- **prof-tensor-info-repeat-factor** — Sort the Tensor Info widget by 'Load to SBUF Repeat Factor'; any input with factor well above 1 is being reloaded and should be cached in SBUF or its loops reordered.
  - why: Repeat factor = bytes loaded into SBUF / tensor size; e.g. a 32 KiB tensor loaded 512 KiB over 16 DMAs has factor 16.
  - when: Repeat factor >> 1 on large inputs.
  - fix: Hoist loads, reorder loops (Mamba tutorial), or block so the reused operand stays resident.
  - numbers: example = 32 KiB tensor, 512 KiB loaded, factor 16
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #1  [stated, all]
- **prof-small-instruction-signature** — Recognize overhead-bound engines by repeated instructions with one-element access patterns (e.g. fp32@0x4000[1,1,1][1,1,1]) and src==prior dst; measured II ~222 ns on NC-v3.
  - why: Each such instruction does ~1 cycle of work under ~100+ cycles of overhead plus RAW stalls.
  - when: ScalarE/VectorE busy with thousands of tiny TENSOR_SCALAR instructions.
  - fix: Increase free size per instruction or use a scan/fused instruction.
  - numbers: observed_II = 222 ns (266 ScalarE cycles)
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5a  [stated, trn2]
- **prof-channels-and-matmul-operands** — Check the channels= field on vector instructions and the '128*N' operand on MATMUL; values below 128 indicate idle lanes/PE columns to recover via partition vectorization.
  - why: Lane and column usage are directly encoded in instruction operands.
  - when: channels=64; MATMUL 128*96.
  - fix: Stack tiles across partitions; widen stationary free size to 128.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #5b  [stated, all]
- **prof-ldweights-vs-matmul-pattern** — If LDWEIGHTS (LoadStationary) shows 1 element/partition while MATMUL shows 128+ elements/partition back-to-back, swap stationary and moving operands.
  - why: This is the matrix-vector 'short stationary' pattern that loses Fast LoadStationary.
  - when: Decode GEMV kernels.
  - fix: nc_matmul(stationary=weights, moving=vector).
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #7  [stated, all]
- **prof-dma-per-engine-view** — Switch the DMA view to per-engine transfers; if gaps between bars exceed the bars or hover shows tiny sizes (32 B), transfers are too small.
  - why: Each transfer shows as a continuous bar; overhead appears as empty gaps. Good kernels show ~85% DMA utilization.
  - when: DMA engines 'busy' but MBU < 60%.
  - fix: Enlarge free/partition dims of nl.load/nl.store.
  - numbers: bad_example_transfer = 32 B; good_utilization = ~85%
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #9  [stated, all]
- **prof-search-dma-transposes** — Use the profiler search to highlight DMA activities performing transposes; if they take substantial time in a memory-bound kernel, move the transpose to TensorE.
  - why: load_transpose2d / dma_transpose run at reduced DMA bandwidth.
  - when: Transposing DMAs on the critical path.
  - fix: See dma-avoid-load-transpose2d-memory-bound.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #10  [stated, all]
- **prof-dma-vs-tensor-active** — Classify the kernel by comparing dma_active_time_percent with the busiest engine: DMA ~100% and TensorE < 90% (e.g. 99.93% vs 87.28%) means memory-bound; after blocking the tutorial reached DMA 21.5% / TensorE 99.5%.
  - why: Active-time percentages in the Summary tab summarize which resource is saturated.
  - when: Deciding between compute and data-movement optimizations.
  - fix: Memory-bound -> Opt #9/#10 and blocking; compute-bound -> Opt #5-#8.
  - numbers: naive = DMA 99.93% / TensorE 87.28%; hoisted = DMA 99.73% / TensorE 99.85%; blocked_mn = DMA 95.70% / TensorE 99.52%; blocked_k = DMA 21.54% / TensorE 99.50%
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Analyzing the kernel ... blocking  [stated, trn2]
- **prof-vector-scalar-bound-attention** — When TensorE shows clear idle gaps while VectorE or ScalarE is busy at every instant (typical self-attention inner loop), optimize by instruction combining and engine rebalancing, not matmul tuning.
  - why: Attention is vector/scalar heavy; the bottleneck engines are VectorE/ScalarE.
  - when: Profile fig19 pattern.
  - fix: activation with fused scale/bias, activation_reduce, DMA SBUF2SBUF transposes, trn3 VectorE exponential.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #6  [stated, all]
- **prof-spill-source-location** — Spill/reload DMAs have no nki_source_location; identify the spilled tensor by its name in the DMA details (e.g. inst__I-35-0:a_dst_L3_sg0000, Source [[TMPBUF]] -> Dest [SB]).
  - why: The compiler generates spill traffic from SBUF usage analysis, not from an explicit API call.
  - when: Instruction blocked on qSyncSpillReload0.
  - fix: Map the tensor name back to the kernel variable and reduce its live range or size.
  - source: nki/deep-dives/nki_perf_guide.rst :: Opt #4  [stated, all]
- **prof-source-linking** — Upload kernel source with the NEFF/NTFF (or rely on the filename:line in instruction details) and Cmd/Ctrl-click instructions to jump to the NKI line and highlight all related instructions.
  - why: Neuron Explorer links device instructions to NKI source locations when debug env vars are set.
  - when: Attributing hot instructions to code.
  - fix: Add Widget -> Code Editor; hover instruction -> Cmd+click.
  - source: nki/guides/use-neuron-profile.rst :: View NKI Source Code in Neuron Profile  [stated, all]
- **benchmark-save-neff-and-trace** — Benchmark with nki.benchmark(warmup, iters, save_neff_name, save_trace_name) and read nc_latency percentiles; validate numerics first with nki.simulate_kernel on CPU.
  - why: Traces (.ntff) expose per-engine timelines needed to apply engine-balancing heuristics; the simulator catches layout bugs before hardware.
  - when: Every new kernel.
  - fix: bk = nki.benchmark(warmup=10, iters=100, save_neff_name='file.neff', save_trace_name='profile.ntff')(kernel); bk(x); bk.benchmark_result.nc_latency.get_latency_percentile(50)
  - source: aws-neuron/nki-samples:contributed/interpolate_bilinear_fwd.py benchmark_kernel; decode_attention.py check_correct  [stated, all]
- **dma-engines-16-per-core-interval-merge** — Measure DMA time as the interval-merged wall-clock time across all 16 DMA engines (dma_active_time), never the sum of per-packet durations.
  - why: 16 DMA engines run in parallel per NeuronCore, so summed DmaPacket.duration_ns greatly exceeds wall clock; Summary.dma_active_time equals the interval merge (within 2 ns).
  - when: Any DMA-time computation from DmaPacket rows.
  - fix: Use interval_merge_ns(starts, ends, t0, t1) over DmaPacket rows filtered to queue_type != 'instruction' and transfer_bytes > 4.
  - numbers: dma_engines_per_core = 16; kernel_packet_filter = queue_type != 'instruction' and transfer_bytes > 4
  - check (profile): memory_bound = interval_merge(DmaPacket.start_ts, end_ts) / 1e9
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Input quantities / Interval merging; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/dma_efficiency.md :: Interval merge helper  [stated, all]
- **hardware-peaks-trn2** — Use the per-NeuronCore constants from Metadata (dma_ddr_bandwidth for DMA, tensor_engine rows*cols*2*clock for TE) when computing bounds; on trn2 these are 435 GB/s and 78.6 TFLOPS bf16.
  - why: Bounds assume a single core; dma_ddr_bandwidth is the max for one core's 16 DMA engines while hbm_ddr_bandwidth is per HBM stack shared across cores.
  - when: Computing memory_bound_ideal, compute_bound_ideal, or arithmetic-intensity break-even.
  - fix: te_peak = rows*cols*2*clock_GHz*1e9; dma_bw_peak = metadata['dma_ddr_bandwidth']; break-even intensity = te_peak / dma_bw_peak (~180 FLOP/byte on trn2).
  - numbers: trn2_dma_ddr_bandwidth = 435 GB/s per NeuronCore; trn2_te_peak_bf16 = 78.6 TFLOPS per NeuronCore; trn2_breakeven_intensity = ~181 FLOP/byte (inferred)
  - check (profile): read Metadata.parquet; derive peaks; compare kernel flops/bytes to te_peak/dma_bw
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/example-bounds-analysis.md :: Performance Bounds (Hardware); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Setup  [stated, trn2]
- **bottleneck-engine-is-argmax-active-time** — Identify the bottleneck as the engine with the largest interval-merged active time among Tensor, Vector, Scalar, GpSimd and DMA; perfect_pipeline equals that time.
  - why: With perfect overlap the kernel cannot be faster than its busiest engine; the gap total_time -> perfect_pipeline is cross-engine serialization.
  - when: Any profile analysis; Summary.*_engine_active_time and dma_active_time.
  - fix: engine_times = {Tensor, Vector, Scalar, GpSimd, DMA: memory_bound}; bottleneck = argmax; focus on that family's gaps.
  - check (profile): perfect_pipeline = max(engine_active_ns); serialization_gap = total_time - perfect_pipeline
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Pipeline family  [stated, all]
- **memory-family-gaps** — Decompose a DMA-bound kernel into three gaps: DMA idle (total_time - memory_bound), DMA inefficiency (memory_bound - dma_transfer_bytes/peak_bw), and excess traffic ((dma_transfer_bytes - necessary_bytes)/peak_bw).
  - why: memory_bound is actual DMA wall-clock; memory_bound_ideal is the same bytes at peak bandwidth; memory_bound_ideal_no_reloads moves each IN/OUT tensor exactly once.
  - when: bottleneck == DMA.
  - fix: Large excess gap -> run redundant-DMA investigation first; large inefficiency gap -> DMA efficiency (descriptor size); idle gap -> do not speculate on cause.
  - numbers: V0_example = DMA inefficiency 59.6% + excess traffic 29.6% of total
  - check (profile): memory_bound = merged DMA ns; ideal = bytes/peak; no_reloads = sum(TensorInfo.size for type in IN,OUT)/peak
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Memory family / Reading the gaps  [stated, all]
- **compute-family-gaps** — Decompose a TE-bound kernel into TE idle (total_time - te_active), TE underutilization (te_active - hw_flops/te_peak), and transpose overhead (transpose_flops/te_peak).
  - why: compute_bound is interval-merged TE active time; compute_bound_ideal assumes peak FLOP rate; useful_flops excludes TRANSPOSE matmuls.
  - when: bottleneck == Tensor.
  - fix: Underutilization -> check tile sizes (te_inefficiency); transpose gap -> pre-transpose operands; idle -> check what MATMULs wait on.
  - check (profile): compute_bound = merged TE ns; ideal = sum(adjusted_flops)/te_peak; useful = (hw - transpose)/te_peak
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Compute family  [stated, all]
- **bottleneck-aware-speedup-cap** — Bound the expected gain of any single-engine optimization by bn_speedup = total_time / max(bound_time, slowest non-improved engine time).
  - why: Removing overhead on one engine only helps until another engine becomes the limiter; e.g. eliminating all DMA overhead in V0 capped speedup at 1.79x because TE was at 4806 us.
  - when: Deciding whether to invest in a memory-side or compute-side fix.
  - fix: Compute bn_speedup for each candidate bound and pick the family with the largest achievable ratio.
  - numbers: V0_example_cap = 1.79x (TE at 4806 us)
  - check (profile): bn_speedup = total_time / max(bound, max_non_impacted_engine_time)
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Bottleneck-aware speedup  [stated, all]
- **gaps-are-not-deltas-reprofile** — Treat gaps as lower bounds on per-category overhead, not predicted savings; re-profile and recompute bounds after each change because the bottleneck engine and gap structure shift.
  - why: Gaps assume peak bandwidth/throughput, the engine may not be on the critical path, and engine times are coupled (data-starved TE active time shrinks when DMA improves).
  - when: After any optimization step.
  - fix: Profile again with the same methodology, present side-by-side bounds, and pick the next investigation from the new bottleneck.
  - check (profile): store bounds per iteration; diff them
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/performance-bounds.md :: Gaps are not improvement deltas  [stated, all]
- **excess-ratio-reloads-vs-spills** — Compute excess_ratio = dma_transfer_bytes / necessary_bytes and split the excess into input reloads (IN tensors with repeat > 1) versus spills ([VIRTUAL] transfers) before choosing a fix.
  - why: Reloads are fixed by blocking/reuse; spills by shrinking live SBUF; they need different code changes.
  - when: memory_bound_ideal -> memory_bound_ideal_no_reloads gap is large.
  - fix: Per-tensor repeat = transferred/size; flag IN tensors with repeat > 1.5; spill_bytes from [VIRTUAL] rows; localize via Instruction -> Flow -> DmaPacketAggregated filtered to source == '[[INPUT]]'.
  - numbers: reload_flag_threshold = repeat > 1.5x; V0_example = excess_ratio 12.0x, rhs repeat 32x, lhsT 3x
  - check (profile): excess_ratio > 1.0; reload_excess = sum(total - size for IN repeat > 1); spill = VIRTUAL bytes
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/redundant_dma_transfers.md :: Step 1 / Step 2a  [stated, all]
- **investigate-reloads-before-dma-efficiency** — When both the excess-traffic and DMA-inefficiency gaps are large, fix reloads first; the excess traffic is itself made of inefficient transfers.
  - why: Excess inefficient loads inflate both gaps; removing the reloads removes a proportional share of the inefficiency gap for free.
  - when: excess gap proportionally large alongside inefficiency gap.
  - fix: Block/reuse to cut reloads, re-profile, then widen transfers.
  - check (profile): if excess_gap/memory_bound > ~0.25 and inefficiency_gap large -> prioritize reloads
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/dma_efficiency.md :: Context (note); /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/example-bounds-analysis.md :: V0 Summary  [stated, all]
- **dma-efficiency-gap-threshold** — If the DMA efficiency gap (memory_bound - memory_bound_ideal) is under ~5% of memory_bound, stop optimizing transfer sizes and look at excess traffic or other engines.
  - why: Peak bandwidth is never fully achievable; a small residual gap is per-transfer overhead that cannot be removed.
  - when: Memory-bound kernel after transfer-widening.
  - fix: Switch to redundant-DMA or pipelining investigations.
  - numbers: threshold = < 5% of memory_bound
  - check (profile): efficiency_gap / memory_bound < 0.05 -> transfers efficient
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/dma_efficiency.md :: Compute the gap  [stated, all]
- **identify-hbm-transfers-and-descriptor-size** — Attribute DMA to source lines using Instruction rows with hbm_read_bytes > 0 (loads) or hbm_write_bytes > 0 (stores) joined via Flow to DmaPacketAggregated, and report shape = partitions x (transfer_bytes / partitions).
  - why: hbm_read/write_bytes are populated regardless of DGE mode/engine; descriptor size per partition is what governs DMA throughput.

- **te-utilization-and-tile-dims-from-operands** — Measure TE utilization as sum(adjusted_flops)/te_active_ns against te_peak, and extract K, M, N per MATMUL source line from Instruction.operands (trailing 'K*M', N from src stride) to find undersized tiles.

  - when: compute_bound -> compute_bound_ideal_flops gap is large.

- **matmul-last-finishing-dependency** — Classify each MATMUL's last-finishing dependency (previous MATMUL = normal pipeline, DPA = DMA-starved, Vector = PSUM evacuation) to decide between prefetching and compute fixes.
  - why: In a healthy pipeline ~95% of MATMULs wait only on the previous MATMUL; a high DPA share means the DMA schedule, not TE, limits throughput.
  - when: TE idle gap or TE underutilization gap present.

- **te-throttling-after-idle** — Expect TE active time to be inflated by throttling/warm-up after idle gaps and by late-arriving weights; fix the DMA side before concluding TE is inefficient.
  - why: Individual MATMUL durations lengthen when data is late, so compute-family bounds computed from current TE active time overstate remaining compute overhead.
  - when: TE underutilization gap with full-size tiles.

- **vector-scalar-gpsimd-bottleneck-window-analysis** — When perfect_pipeline exceeds both memory_bound and compute_bound (Vector/Scalar/GpSimd is the bottleneck), section the kernel logically and run windowed bounds per phase instead of whole-kernel analysis.

- **memory-vs-compute-bound-via-intensity** — Decide whether a kernel is memory- or compute-bound by comparing mm_arithmetic_intensity (FLOPs per DMA byte) with peak_flops_bandwidth_ratio, and by comparing necessary_bytes/peak_bw with hw_flops/te_peak before optimizing.
  - why: The larger of the two ideal bounds is the true floor; a batch=1 decode matmul has intensity ~2 FLOP/byte, far below trn2's ~180 FLOP/byte break-even, so it is DMA-bound regardless of TE tuning.
  - when: Planning an optimization for a new kernel.

- **profile-capture-flags** — Capture profiles on the 2nd execution with DGE notifications and debug info: NEURON_FRAMEWORK_DEBUG=1 (plus XLA_IR_DEBUG/XLA_HLO_DEBUG) at compile, NEURON_RT_ENABLE_DGE_NOTIFICATIONS=1 / --enable-dge-notifs and --profile-nth-exec=2 at capture.
  - why: Without DGE notifications DmaPacket tables are empty; without debug info bir_debug_info_source_location is NULL so nothing can be attributed to source lines; the first execution includes warm-up.
  - when: Empty DmaPacket table, NULL source locations, or noisy latency.
  - fix: neuron-explorer capture -n $NEFF -s profile.ntff --profile-nth-exec=2 --enable-dge-notifs; check DmaPacket COUNT(*) > 0 before analysis.
  - numbers: profile_nth_exec = 2 (skip warmup)
  - check (profile): assert DmaPacket count > 0 and Instruction.bir_debug_info_source_location not all NULL
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profiling/SKILL.md :: Step 4; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/SKILL.md :: Step 0: Check Profile Quality  [stated, all]
- **dpa-attribution-needs-hwdge-or-none** — When source-level DMA attribution matters, compile the profiled variant with dge_mode none or hwdge; DmaPacketAggregated and Instruction->DPA flow links may be missing for swdge (or compiler-chosen 'unknown').
  - why: Depending on NKI/neuronx-cc version the aggregated packet table is only produced for hwdge/none transfers, so reload/spill localization and descriptor-size analysis skip swdge lines.
  - when: DPA coverage < 95% of dma_transfer_bytes.
  - fix: Temporarily switch dge_mode=nisa.dge_mode.hwdge for the profiling run, or accept Step-1 totals only.
  - numbers: coverage_warning = < 95%
  - check (profile): coverage = sum(DPA.transfer_bytes)/dma_transfer_bytes; warn if < 0.95
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/dma_efficiency.md :: Check DPA coverage / Known issues  [stated, all]
- **transpose-flops-nan-when-zero** — Apply fillna(0) to Summary.transpose_flops before comparing; it is NaN for kernels with no transposes.
  - why: The summary field is undefined rather than zero when no TRANSPOSE matmuls exist.
  - when: Reading Summary.transpose_flops.
  - fix: summary['transpose_flops'] = summary['transpose_flops'].fillna(0).
  - check (profile): treat NaN transpose_flops as 0
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/references/investigations/redundant_te_transposes.md :: Known issues  [stated, all]
- **only-claim-what-profile-shows** — Report measured bounds, gaps and attributed source lines; do not diagnose causes from a single metric or from static code reading alone, and include investigations that found nothing.
  - why: Profile data is precise but narrow; low utilization or large byte counts need corroborating tables before they mean anything; static analysis of kernels is unreliable.
  - when: Writing a performance report or choosing the next optimization.
  - fix: Present bounds table, engine times, per-investigation findings ordered by relevance to the bottleneck.
  - source: /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/agents/neuron-nki-profile-analysis-agent.md :: Key Principles / After Optimization; /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/neuron_agentic_development/artifacts/skills/neuron-nki-profile-querying/SKILL.md :: Step 4: Interpret Results  [stated, all]
- **matmul-is-two-hw-instructions** — Read a matmul in the profiler as two TensorE instructions, load-weights (stationary) and matrix-multiply (moving), and treat gaps between them as data-wait, not compute.
  - why: nc_matmul lowers to a weight load followed by a multiply that streams the moving operand.
  - when: Inspecting TensorE / TensorMatrix rows in Neuron Explorer.
  - fix: Zoom into gaps; hover the first instruction after a gap to see the semaphore it waits on.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Writing the kernel  [stated, all]
- **choose-kernel-candidate-by-min-cut** — Pick kernel candidates where the profiler shows engines idle waiting on DMA in code that executes many times, and cut the graph where the region has few inputs and outputs.
  - why: A kernel replaces a subgraph; a minimum-cut boundary keeps the interface small while the hot region captures the idle time.
  - when: Model profile shows repeated regions with engine gaps.
  - fix: Use Neuron Profiler system view to find idle engines; wrap that region in a @nki.jit kernel with few tensors in/out.
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: When to write a kernel?  [stated, all]
- **profile-with-representative-sizes** — Profile the kernel with input sizes representative of the real workload, not the single-tile sizes used for correctness.
  - why: Memory-vs-compute balance and SBUF pressure only show up at realistic shapes, and the same driver doubles as a regression test.
  - when: Developing a kernel from a single-tile prototype.
  - fix: Grow the driver from 128x128 x 128x512 to e.g. 4096x8192 x 8192x8192 and wrap the call in profiler.profile(...) / jax.profiler.trace(...).
  - numbers: example_shape = 4096x8192 @ 8192x8192
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/kernel-optimization.rst :: Writing the kernel  [stated, all]
- **diagnose-idle-via-semaphore-wait** — Find why an engine is idle by hovering the first instruction after the gap and reading the semaphore condition; a wait on a qSyncIO queue means a blocking input load.
  - why: Semaphore waits name the DMA queue; hovering the queue activity shows the NKI tensor being loaded.
  - when: VectorE/TensorE active percentage drops below expectation.
  - fix: Hoist/prefetch the named tensor's load or reorder loops.
  - numbers: example = S[22] reaching 240 set by qSyncIO0
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Increasing input channels size  [stated, all]
- **reload-warnings-with-low-sbuf-mean-reorder** — Treat profiler reload warnings while SBUF usage is only ~50% as a loop-ordering bug, not a capacity limit.
  - why: Reloading the same input tensors multiple times is only justified when SBUF cannot hold them.
  - when: Orange performance-warning boxes on qSyncIO rows (tensor reloaded ~7x) with SBUF usage ~50%.
  - fix: Reorder loops so the larger reused tensors are loaded in the outer loop (see loop-order-prioritize-largest-reuse).
  - numbers: reload_count = ~7; sbuf_usage = ~50%
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: Increasing input channels size  [stated, all]
- **framework-op-with-tiny-dma-utilization-is-kernel-candidate** — When a framework-compiled op shows sparse engine activity and very low DMA throughput at the same time, rewrite it as a fused NKI kernel.
  - why: Neither compute nor memory is stressed, so the op is running at low efficiency due to many small spills/reloads.
  - when: Profile: compute engines sparse, qVectorSpillReload rows dominate, DMA ~0.33% utilization.
  - fix: Fuse the layer in NKI with explicit tiling.
  - numbers: torch_latency = 151.83 ms; nki_latency = 172.93 us; speedup = 878x; dma_util_before = 0.33%
  - source: nki/guides/tutorials/fused_mamba.rst :: PyTorch Reference Implementation  [stated, all]
- **simulator-not-for-performance** — Never benchmark with the simulator; it models no instruction latency, engine parallelism or scheduling.
  - why: Kernels are interpreted eagerly and sequentially on the CPU.
  - when: Any timing of simulated runs.
  - fix: Profile on hardware with Neuron Explorer or run NEFFs through nrtpy.
  - source: nki/guides/nki_simulator.rst :: Performance  [stated, all]
- **quantization-chain-is-serial** — Expect the abs-max -> scale -> clamp -> reciprocal -> multiply quantization chain to run serially on VectorE; overlap it with another tile's work rather than trying to parallelize within one tile.
  - why: Each step depends on the previous result.
  - when: FP8 row quantization.
  - fix: Process tiles in batches of 8 so independent chains interleave.
  - numbers: batch = 8 tiles
  - source: nki/library/specs/design-rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Phase 3: Quantization; nki/library/api/rmsnorm-quant.rst :: Optimized Batch Processing  [stated, all]
